docs.title: Instalação
docs.text: Use Python >=3.12,<4.0. A CI verifica Python 3.12, 3.13 e 3.14. O espaço em disco e a memória necessários dependem dos arquivos e anos processados.

docs.title: Instalar com pip
docs.text:
Crie um ambiente virtual:

python -m venv .venv

Ative-o com o comando do seu terminal:

Terminal Comando Linux/macOS source .venv/bin/activate Windows PowerShell .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 Windows cmd .venv\Scripts\activate.bat

Instale a biblioteca no ambiente ativo:

python -m pip install globaldatafinance

docs.title: Instalar em um projeto com uv
docs.text:
uv add globaldatafinance

Para alterar o código da biblioteca, siga o ambiente com lockfile do guia de contribuição.

docs.title: Conferir a instalação
docs.text:
No mesmo ambiente em que instalou a biblioteca:

from importlib.metadata import version
from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM, HistoricalQuotesB3

print(version("globaldatafinance"))
print(FundamentalStocksDataCVM().get_available_docs())
print(HistoricalQuotesB3().get_available_assets())

Essas consultas não baixam dados. PyArrow já é instalado pela biblioteca. Pandas e Polars são leitores opcionais para análise dos Parquets e devem ser instalados separadamente quando necessários.

docs.title: Resolver problemas comuns
docs.text:
Sintoma O que verificar No module named globaldatafinance Use o mesmo Python na instalação e na execução; confira python -m pip show globaldatafinance. Python incompatível Crie o ambiente virtual com uma versão no intervalo suportado. Conflito de dependências Instale em um ambiente virtual novo; as versões do projeto ficam em pyproject.toml. Falha de permissão ao instalar Use um ambiente virtual em uma pasta onde você tenha permissão de escrita.

Continue pelo início rápido.

docs.title: Migração CVM para preservação textual exata
docs.text:
O contrato exact-text-v1 grava todas as colunas CVM como Arrow string. Isso altera os schemas persistidos: consumidores que dependiam de int64, uint64, float64, booleanos ou nulos inferidos devem migrar explicitamente. O ZIP original permanece disponível mesmo após extração bem-sucedida.

Entrada CSV Parquet anterior Parquet exact-text-v1 000012345 Inteiro sem os zeros iniciais "000012345" 1.234567890123456789 Decimal arredondado em float64 "1.234567890123456789" 1e-400 0.0 "1e-400" N/A, NULL, None Nulo inferido Texto original Campo vazio Nulo inferido "" TrUe Booleano "TrUe" CSV apenas com cabeçalho Colunas Arrow null Colunas Arrow string, zero linhas

docs.title: Regeneração e troca do consumidor
docs.text:
1. Guarde os ZIPs originais e a saída antiga durante a migração.
  2. Regenere os Parquet em um diretório novo com automatic_extractor=True. O padrão sem extração, automatic_extractor=False, continua disponível.
  3. Confira has_errors() e os identificadores {DOC}_{YEAR} concluídos.
  4. Confira o metadata cvm.contract=exact-text-v1 nos arquivos regenerados.
  5. Converta somente as colunas necessárias conforme seu dicionário de dados e teste esses consumidores antes de trocar o diretório lido pela aplicação.

Um Parquet antigo que já arredondou números ou removeu zeros não permite recuperar o texto original. Regenerar exige o ZIP correspondente ou um novo download oficial. Misturar schemas antigos e novos em um dataset pode causar incompatibilidade ou coerções; mantenha a migração em um destino novo.

from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

import pyarrow.parquet as pq

path = Path("cvm-exact/DFP/2024/dfp_cia_aberta_DRE_con_2024.parquet")
table = pq.read_table(path)
assert table.schema.metadata[b"cvm.contract"] == b"exact-text-v1"

raw_value = table.column("VL_CONTA")[0].as_py()
amount = Decimal(raw_value) if raw_value else None

A conversão de valores financeiros exige também interpretar moeda, escala, exercício, versão e tipo de demonstração conforme o conjunto CVM. O pipeline preserva os campos fornecidos; a consistência contábil do documento declarado permanece uma validação de negócio do consumidor.

docs.title: Integridade e operação
docs.text:
Antes da publicação, o pipeline compara o SHA-256 de todos os registros decodificados com o conteúdo reaberto do Parquet. Os metadados incluem cvm.contract, cvm.content-sha256, cvm.source-archive, cvm.source-archive-sha256, cvm.source-member e cvm.source-encoding. A confirmação de extração exige todos os Parquet esperados e sua associação ao ZIP consumido. Checksums de página, leitura completa e fsync protegem a publicação persistida.

Todas as passagens leem o mesmo ZIP aberto; alterações na origem interrompem a extração antes da publicação.

docs.title: Inventário das saídas
docs.text:
Os Parquets esperados pelo ZIP são publicados nos nomes correspondentes, substituindo na transação o arquivo comum que ocupar um desses nomes. Um link simbólico em um nome esperado é rejeitado como ExtractionError: a extração desse ZIP falha, a facade registra a falha em failed_downloads e nem o link nem o alvo são alterados. Arquivos comuns fora desse inventário bloqueiam o reprocessamento quando cvm.source-archive os associa a um ZIP de mesmo nome. Sem essa identidade, são preservados como dados do chamador, sem reconhecimento pelo nome, e podem coexistir com as saídas novas mesmo após sucesso. Links simbólicos fora do inventário não são inspecionados e também são preservados.

O resultado confirma as saídas esperadas, sem certificar todos os Parquets do diretório. Para substituir um dataset, preserve os arquivos anteriores, regenere em um destino novo e confira os dados antes de trocar o consumidor.

docs.title: Limites do contrato textual
docs.text:
Aspas continuam literais no dialeto QUOTE_NONE. Linhas curtas recebem campos vazios ao final; o ZIP retido preserva a diferença entre campos ausentes e campos vazios. Linhas com campos excedentes, cabeçalhos vazios ou duplicados, mais de 4.096 colunas ou registros físicos acima de 8 MiB em UTF-8 falham explicitamente. Row groups usam até 50.000 linhas, reduzidas para respeitar um orçamento estimado de 16 MiB de dados e offsets; esse orçamento não é um limite absoluto de RSS do processo.

UTF-8 e BOM UTF-8 são validados integralmente. Fora de UTF-8, a política documentada distingue CP1252 de Latin-1 pelos bytes observados. Uma fonte sem declaração de encoding pode ser ambígua; os bytes originais ficam no ZIP para conferência independente.

Chamadas concorrentes para o mesmo destino são rejeitadas antes de substituir o ZIP. .cvm-write-lock/owner.json identifica o processo responsável. Após terminação abrupta, a biblioteca conserva esse lock e exige inspeção explícita antes da recuperação: confirme que não existe escritor ativo, preserve a evidência e recupere o estado derivado da transação. A biblioteca nunca toma automaticamente um lock sem verificar sua autoridade. Falhas permanecem no resultado; não interprete apenas a existência de um Parquet como sucesso.

IPE inclui 2003 em diante. get_available_years().ipe_min_year informa esse limite como propriedade; os quatro campos da tupla continuam representando documentos gerais, ITR, CGVN/VLMO e ano corrente.

Consulte a referência CVM e o guia de testes para a campanha oficial com comparação independente de todos os arquivos e registros.

docs.title: Migração: corte limpo de infraestrutura
docs.text: Esta quebra de compatibilidade pertence à linha 0.x e deve ser publicada como v0.2.0, não como uma versão patch v0.1.5. APIs genéricas obsoletas e a dependência automática de Pandas foram removidas. As fachadas raiz, as assinaturas públicas de CVM/B3, os nomes de saída, os schemas Parquet e a publicação transacional continuam iguais. A mudança é intencionalmente incompatível: não há alias, warning, shim ou fallback para os nomes removidos.

docs.title: Versão removida da raiz
docs.text:
globaldatafinance.__version__ não é mais exportado. Consulte os metadados da distribuição no runtime:

from importlib.metadata import version

package_version = version('globaldatafinance')

docs.title: Timeout de download
docs.text:
Antes:

from globaldatafinance.macro_exceptions import TimeoutError

Depois:

from globaldatafinance.macro_exceptions import DownloadTimeoutError

try:
    download()
except DownloadTimeoutError:
    recover_or_report()

DownloadTimeoutError mantém o construtor (doc_name, timeout=None) e o formato da mensagem anterior. O nome antigo não pode mais ser importado. O TimeoutError nativo do Python continua sendo um erro de transporte interno reconhecido pelo adapter CVM; não o confunda com a classe de domínio.

docs.title: Adapters genéricos removidos
docs.text:
ExtractorAdapter e ReadFilesAdapter não fazem mais parte de globaldatafinance.macro_infra, e os módulos globaldatafinance.macro_infra.extractor_file e globaldatafinance.macro_infra.read_files foram removidos.

Antes:

from globaldatafinance.macro_infra import ExtractorAdapter, ReadFilesAdapter

Depois, use a fronteira da fonte que conhece o contrato do dado:

from globaldatafinance.brazil.cvm.ingestion.extract import (
    CvmParquetExtractor,
)

cvm_extractor = CvmParquetExtractor()
convert_zip = cvm_extractor.extract
convert_zip('download.zip', 'cvm-output')

Para leitura ou inspeção de arquivos B3, use a fachada HistoricalQuotesB3 e os componentes source-owned documentados em Cotações Históricas B3. Não recrie um adapter genérico para reproduzir os módulos removidos: CVM e B3 têm regras de formato, anos mínimos e diagnósticos diferentes.

docs.title: Pandas deixou de ser dependência automática
docs.text:
O runtime da biblioteca usa PyArrow para CSV e Parquet. Um consumidor que ainda precisar de DataFrames deve declarar a dependência por conta própria:

python -m pip install pandas

Para o caminho recomendado e limitado por memória, nenhuma instalação adicional é necessária além das dependências da biblioteca:

import pyarrow.parquet as pq

for batch in pq.ParquetFile('cotahist.parquet').iter_batches(
    batch_size=200_000
):
    consume(batch)

Pandas e Polars podem continuar sendo usados como leitores downstream opcionais, mas não são instalados nem importados pelo pacote.

docs.title: Fronteira de captura B3
docs.text:
As exceções de validação de entrada B3 preservam seus tipos e herdam de B3Error. A captura abaixo usa funções de execução e tratamento definidas pelo consumidor:

from globaldatafinance.brazil.b3_data.historical_quotes.errors import B3Error

try:
    result = run_b3_operation()
except B3Error as error:
    handle_b3_input_error(error)
else:
    if not result["success"]:
        raise RuntimeError(result["errors"] or result["message"])

B3Error é source-local e não é exportado por globaldatafinance nem usado como base global. As regras de ano continuam separadas das regras CVM: o limite mínimo B3 continua sendo 1986, e InvalidFirstYear/InvalidLastYear de cada fonte continuam sendo classes distintas.

CotahistCatalogError herda de ValueError e CotahistPreflightError de ExtractionError; são tipos internos fora dessa hierarquia. A fachada retorna as falhas de fonte em errors, com success=False. O catálogo de exceções distingue esses caminhos.

docs.title: Falhas de escrita Parquet CVM
docs.text:
Falhas de filesystem durante criação, escrita, fechamento ou reabertura do Parquet staged agora são ParquetWriteError, com a causa original preservada. ENOSPC continua produzindo DiskFullError; erros de CSV, Arrow, schema, contagem de linhas, ZIP corrompido e falha combinada de rollback continuam sendo ExtractionError quando esse é o contrato apropriado.

Na agregação de downloads, uma falha conhecida aparece como:

ParquetWrite: Failed to write Parquet file '...'

O ZIP de origem é mantido para diagnóstico. Consumidores que tratavam qualquer ExtractionError podem adicionar uma captura explícita para ParquetWriteError quando precisarem distinguir falha de infraestrutura de falha de conteúdo.

docs.title: Destinos e temporários internos
docs.text: Os owners CVM e B3 compartilham apenas a normalização e a preparação de destinos invariantes. A criação de diretórios continua sendo responsabilidade do owner da fonte, e o publicador transacional não cria o destino. Downloads e writers Parquet reservam arquivos temporários ocultos no mesmo diretório do destino para preservar a elegibilidade de publicação no mesmo filesystem.

docs.title: Migração 0.2.0: PyArrow e integridade de ingestão
docs.text:
A versão 0.2.0 substitui os caminhos produtivos de ingestão por PyArrow, remove Polars das dependências da biblioteca e fortalece as garantias de integridade de CVM e B3. As três fachadas públicas raiz e suas assinaturas permanecem estáveis:

from globaldatafinance import (
    ExtractionResultB3,
    FundamentalStocksDataCVM,
    HistoricalQuotesB3,
)

docs.title: Mudanças para consumidores
docs.text: Mudança Ação necessária Parser B3 estrito Corrija o arquivo-fonte ou trate ExtractionError; valores inválidos não recebem fallback para zero, string vazia ou nulo. Polars removido Instale Polars explicitamente caso sua aplicação queira usá-lo para ler Parquet. ExtractorAdapter.extract_csv_from_zip_to_parquet removido Migre código interno para a fachada CVM ou para uma interface pública apropriada. Metadata pandas removida Não dependa de metadata física b'pandas'; use schema e valores lógicos. B3 totalmente filtrado Trate Parquet vazio como resultado válido quando o filtro TPMERC não encontra ativos. Namespace de arquivo canônico Use Settings.archive; Settings.archive_safety não existe mais e não há alias de compatibilidade. Configuração de logging estrita Use apenas os campos e variáveis documentados de LoggingSettings; LoggingSettings(structured=True) e variáveis DATAFIN_LOG_* desconhecidas agora falham com ValidationError. Destino e contexto de logging Use um log_file em diretório aprovado pela aplicação; raízes/diretórios protegidos são rejeitados, e campos comuns de segredo recebem redação de melhor esforço. Não envie segredos ao logging. Preservação CVM exata Regenere os Parquets como exact-text-v1; todas as colunas são string e conversões numéricas são explícitas. Corte interno B3 Remova data_writer de integrações que constroem ExtractionServiceB3 e não passe resource_monitor para ParquetWriterB3; use as fachadas e as assinaturas atuais. Sentinela B3 reservada O texto literal __GLOBALDATAFINANCE_NULL__ não é um valor aceito; use None para nulos.

docs.title: CVM
docs.text:
O contrato CVM atual é exact-text-v1: colunas string, campos vazios como "", valores originais preservados e ZIP retido após extração. QUOTE_NONE mantém aspas literais e linhas curtas recebem somente campos vazios finais. A publicação de vários Parquets permanece recuperável por lote, com confirmação de todos os registros antes da promoção. Consulte a migração CVM exata para regeneração dos arquivos, conversões explícitas e inspeção de locks após interrupção.

O logging da biblioteca não altera o root logger da aplicação. Antes de uma chamada explícita a setup_logging(), o namespace globaldatafinance usa NullHandler e permanece silencioso; uma falha ao reconfigurar handlers preserva a configuração anterior.

docs.title: Notas para a release 0.2.0
docs.text:
O texto abaixo é o corpo preparado para a release 0.2.0 no GitHub. O workflow existente .github/workflows/publish.yml executa os gates e a publicação a partir do evento de release publicada. A versão, tag e publicação devem aguardar a aprovação das evidências de aceitação; este texto não afirma que a release já foi publicada.

Requisitos de dependências da próxima release:

  • PyArrow: >=26.0.0,<27.0.0.
  • psutil: >=7.2.2,<8.0.0.
  • pydantic-settings: >=2.16.2,<3.0.0.

O lock de desenvolvimento também atualiza virtualenv para 21.14.13, corrigindo o GHSA-cx6f-vjhg-g3cc na ativação de ambientes Bash. Essa dependência é usada pelo pre-commit.

Mudanças incompatíveis do contrato COTAHIST:

  • A seleção padrão agora preserva todas as cotações 01, incluindo TPMERC 021 e mercados numéricos desconhecidos. Omita assets_list ou use todos; use classes explícitas quando o consumidor precisar de um filtro.
  • O Parquet passa para o schema versionado 2, com 32 colunas. Os 20 campos anteriores mantêm sua ordem e valores; as 12 adições incluem os campos oficiais antes ausentes, proveniência e os 245 bytes originais.
  • Regenere Parquets v1 a partir dos ZIP/TXT originais. Append e merge entre schemas incompatíveis falham; uma conversão dos arquivos v1 não recupera os dados ausentes. Siga os procedimentos de corte e rollback desta página.
  • Informe um intervalo anual disponível: qualquer ano solicitado ausente ou registro inválido, inclusive em mercado excluído pelo filtro, falha a extração.
  • A publicação exige leitura integral da saída staged e verificação exata dos dados e do manifesto. Falhas preservam a saída anterior; consumidores devem verificar success, schema_version e integrity antes de mudar de arquivo.

O corpus local de aceitação cobre 2000–2026 e seu snapshot termina em 2026-09-02. A release deve anexar as evidências finais do corpus congelado e os manifestos de checksums; esses limites não são uma confirmação externa de completude da bolsa ou de disponibilidade de todos os anos históricos.

Todas as linhas 01 são validadas e convertidas antes da seleção de mercados. Linhas vazias e controles 00/99 são contados, e qualquer outro identificador não vazio falha. Ambos os modos usam a conversão canônica e lotes limitados de linhas CSV pelo Arrow. fast usa lotes de até 25.000 registros e pode processar fontes em paralelo; slow usa lotes de até 10.000 registros e um worker. Os modos preservam o mesmo schema, ordem e valores lógicos.

docs.title: B3 schema v2 e regeneração
docs.text:
O contrato persistido COTAHIST mudou de forma incompatível para o schema versionado 2. O padrão agora é assets_list=None, equivalente a assets_list=["todos"]: todas as cotações 01 com TPMERC numérico são preservadas, incluindo 021 e códigos ainda desconhecidos. A saída tem 32 colunas, incluindo os cinco campos oficiais antes ausentes, coordenadas da fonte e os 245 bytes originais de cada cotação. Valores financeiros são decimais exatos; preco_exercicio_pontos usa escala 6.

Parquets v1 não contêm linhas TPMERC 021, todos os campos oficiais nem bytes originais. Não converta nem acrescente esses arquivos para v2: regenere a partir dos ZIP/TXT brutos e valide o resultado antes de trocar o consumidor.

Procedimento de corte:

  1. Preserve as fontes COTAHIST e registre seus hashes.
  2. Escolha o intervalo anual realmente disponível. Informe initial_year e last_year; os padrões continuam cobrindo 1986 até o ano atual e uma lacuna no intervalo solicitado falha a extração.
  3. Gere a saída em outro diretório, usando assets_list=["todos"] (ou omita assets_list).
  4. Exija result["success"] is True e result["schema_version"] == 2. Confirme result["integrity"]["selection_complete"], source_complete, contagens, anos selecionados e output_sha256 conforme a necessidade do consumidor.
  5. Leia o schema Arrow e adapte os consumidores às 12 colunas adicionais e aos tipos exatos listados na referência do schema B3 v2.
  6. Troque os consumidores para a saída verificada e retenha os arquivos v1 até aceitar o corte.

Procedimento de rollback:

  1. Preserve juntos a versão anterior do pacote, a configuração dos consumidores e os caminhos dos Parquets v1 até aceitar a migração. Registre o SHA-256 de cada saída anterior e gere v2 em um diretório separado.
  2. Se a aceitação falhar, restaure a versão anterior do pacote e a configuração dos consumidores para ler os caminhos v1 preservados. Mantenha os COTAHIST originais e os artefatos v2 separados disponíveis para diagnóstico.
  3. Confira os hashes v1 preservados e reabra esses arquivos com o consumidor anterior. Não sobrescreva v2 com v1 nem acrescente linhas entre versões.

A biblioteca publica uma saída escolhida pelo chamador; mudar o caminho lido pelo consumidor pertence à aplicação. Uma extração malsucedida preserva o arquivo anterior nesse caminho e retorna output_file="". Essas garantias são exercitadas por tests/application/b3_docs/test_publication_integrity.py e tests/application/b3_docs/test_schema_migration.py.

Um Parquet v2 filtrado pode ter zero linhas e ainda ser completo para a seleção solicitada; consulte selection_complete, source_complete e as contagens de exclusões no relatório. source_complete=True exige nenhuma exclusão. Os relatórios incluem hashes externos e descompactados, controles codificados, convenção do trailer, datas observadas, digest das linhas e hash do Parquet. Esse hash atesta os arquivos fornecidos; não confirma calendário de negociação ou instrumentos fora do corpus. A faixa anterior a 2000 exige suas próprias fontes, que não fazem parte do corpus local auditado.

Integrações que dependiam de objetos internos removidos devem migrar para o fluxo da fachada. A session B3 agora tem ciclo de vida explícito (NEW → OPEN → CLOSED) e não pode ser reaberta depois do fechamento, inclusive quando a validação final falha.

Os workers internos usam apenas a conversão canônica de CotahistParserB3, incluindo as verificações de releitura e digest para subclasses. Fábricas customizadas que ofereciam somente parse_line() devem implementar o contrato completo do parser; o caminho alternativo de dicionários foi removido. O helper interno normalize_decimal_v99 e os tipos sem consumidores ZipProcessingResult/ProcessSingleFileResult foram removidos. Use normalize_decimal com escala explícita em extensões internas.

As interfaces de leitura textual e ParquetWriterB3 com consumidores existentes continuam disponíveis sobre a implementação atual. A documentação do módulo fica em README.md e README.en.md; a cópia antiga README.pt.md foi removida.

Nesta migração para 0.2.0, os cinco nomes históricos abaixo são mantidos para preservar integrações existentes em seus namespaces internos atuais:

Nome Status nesta migração CotahistParserB3.EXPECTED_LINE_LENGTH Atributo histórico de largura do registro, derivado do layout canônico de 245 bytes. extraction_service.types.ParsedRecord Alias de tipagem preservado para imports existentes. extraction_service.types.ExtractionSummary Tipo histórico preservado para imports existentes; não define o resultado público completo. ExtractHistoricalQuotesUseCaseB3.execute_sync Entrada síncrona preservada sobre a implementação assíncrona atual. CreateSetToDownloadUseCaseB3 Descoberta de arquivos preservada sobre a validação atual de caminhos e fontes.

Novas integrações devem usar HistoricalQuotesB3 e o contrato público ExtractionResultB3. A preservação desses nomes nesta migração não amplia os exports da raiz.

docs.title: Dependências e medição
docs.text: O ReadFilesAdapter foi removido junto com a dependência automática de Pandas; consumidores que ainda quiserem DataFrames devem instalar Pandas por conta própria. PyArrow é o único engine produtivo de CSV/Parquet. A migração completa de timeout, adapters genéricos, fronteira de captura B3 e falhas de escrita está em Corte limpo de infraestrutura. Use scripts/benchmark_ingestion.py para medições locais em processo novo; seus números dependem de hardware, ambiente e corpus, portanto não são uma garantia universal de tempo ou RSS.

docs.title: Início rápido
docs.text: Após instalar a biblioteca, escolha uma fonte. CVM requer internet; B3 usa arquivos locais. Os exemplos abaixo processam somente 2023.

docs.title: Baixar documentos CVM
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM

result = FundamentalStocksDataCVM().download(
    destination_path="./data_cvm",
    list_docs=["DFP"],
    initial_year=2023,
    last_year=2023,
    automatic_extractor=True,
)
if result.error_count_downloads > 0 or result.success_count_downloads == 0:
    raise RuntimeError(result.failed_downloads)
print(result.successful_downloads)

O download salva o ZIP original e converte seus CSVs em Parquet na pasta indicada. As colunas CVM são texto; datas e números são convertidos na análise, quando necessário. Para baixar somente ZIPs, use automatic_extractor=False.

Confira o guia CVM para escolher documentos e tratar falhas parciais.

docs.title: Extrair cotações B3
docs.text:
Obtenha os arquivos na página oficial da B3 e coloque o ano desejado na pasta de entrada. O extrator aceita ZIP ou TXT locais, com nomes COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP ou COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT. A biblioteca não baixa esses arquivos. Para este exemplo, forneça 2023:

cotahist/
└── COTAHIST_A2023.ZIP

from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3

b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
result = b3.extract(
    path_of_docs="./cotahist",
    destination_path="./data_b3",
    assets_list=["ações"],
    initial_year=2023,
    last_year=2023,
)
if not result["success"]:
    raise RuntimeError(result["errors"])
print(result["output_file"], result["total_records"])

ações seleciona os mercados à vista e fracionário. O resultado é um dicionário com status e metadados; os dados ficam no Parquet informado em output_file. Veja o guia B3 para outros mercados, anos e modos de processamento.

docs.title: Ler o Parquet
docs.text:
Use o caminho retornado pela extração B3 anterior. Para inspecionar uma pequena amostra sem carregar o arquivo inteiro:

import pyarrow.parquet as pq

parquet = pq.ParquetFile(result["output_file"])
print(parquet.schema_arrow)
for batch in parquet.iter_batches(batch_size=5):
    print(batch.to_pydict())
    break

Para executar os exemplos do repositório com amostras B3 sintéticas já incluídas, consulte exemplos práticos.

docs.title: Global-Data-Finance
docs.text:
Python library for obtaining CVM regulatory filings and converting B3 historical quotes to Parquet. Requires Python >=3.12,<4.0.

Source Input Result CVM Download of selected filings Original ZIP and optional Parquet conversion B3 Annual files supplied by the user Consolidated Parquet and integrity report

The B3 extractor accepts local ZIP or TXT files: COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP and COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT. The files must exist before extraction.

docs.title: Use the library
docs.text:
python -m pip install globaldatafinance

Start with the quickstart: one CVM download and one B3 extraction, including result checks.

I need to… Page Set up an environment Installation Choose documents and years CVM guide Prepare COTAHIST and filter markets B3 guide Run examples or resolve a question Examples · FAQ

docs.title: Develop the project
docs.text: Follow contributing to set up the environment and validate a change. The architecture shows where responsibilities belong; the testing guide explains commands and test classification.

docs.title: Look up details
docs.text: Use the API reference for signatures, results, schemas, and exceptions. Configuration, operation, and migrations are grouped under the reference; benchmarks, external campaigns, and decisions are in the maintenance section of the developer guide.

docs.title: ZIP limits and allowlisted UNC destinations
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-08-31 Scope: shared archive security and caller-provided destinations

docs.title: Context
docs.text: CVM and B3 consume ZIP archives obtained from external sources. Streaming avoids extractall(), but does not itself bound the CPU, disk, or memory cost of an archive with many members, deceptive metadata, or excessive expansion. Both sources also receive caller-provided destinations. Blocking only selected POSIX directories does not protect Windows drive roots or UNC paths.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
core/archive_safety.py owns the reusable ZIP policy. Before CRC, parsing, or writes, CVM and B3 validate compressed size, member count, individual and total uncompressed sizes, compression ratio, encryption, absolute or .. names, links/special types, output-name duplicates after case-insensitive normalization, and collisions where a file is an ancestor of another member. Each component is also checked against Win32 semantics: ambiguous separators, ADS, invalid characters, trailing dot/space, and reserved DOS device names are rejected. Each decompressed stream is also counted while reading, so false metadata cannot authorize more bytes than the policy permits.

The limits are typed global configuration:

Variable Default DATAFINANCE_ARCHIVE_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES 2 GiB DATAFINANCE_ARCHIVE_MAX_MEMBERS 10,000 DATAFINANCE_ARCHIVE_MAX_MEMBER_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES 2 GiB DATAFINANCE_ARCHIVE_MAX_TOTAL_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES 8 GiB DATAFINANCE_ARCHIVE_MAX_COMPRESSION_RATIO 200.0

Values are positive, have defensive upper bounds, and are validated while creating Settings; the allowed total cannot be lower than the per-member limit.

assert_path_not_sensitive() remains the single shared destination policy. It blocks /, roots of every Windows drive, Windows, Program Files, and Program Files (x86) on every drive, as well as sensitive POSIX directories. UNC is denied by default. The only exception is a path equal to or below a root in the JSON list DATAFINANCE_PATH_SAFETY_ALLOWED_UNC_ROOTS; administrative shares ending in $ remain forbidden even in that list.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Sources retain source-owned naming rules: CSV belongs to CVM and COTAHIST belongs to B3; only generic limits and security are shared.
  • Rejected input fails before material decompression or any write.
  • Limits reduce denial-of-service exposure, but an archive within a permitted ceiling may still consume resources up to that ceiling.
  • This is a defense for caller-provided destinations. It does not claim to constrain a caller that already has the process’s privileges.
  • The library never loads .env implicitly. The caller must export variables or explicitly use uv run --env-file ... when running a local process.

docs.title: CVM failure-atomic batch commit
docs.text:
Status: Accepted Date: 2026-08-31 Scope: automatic CVM ZIP CSV-to-Parquet extraction

Partially superseded (2026-09-10): the PyArrow ingestion and transactional-integrity cutover retains the failure-atomic commitment, but replaces this CVM-local mechanism with shared publication backed by a durable manifest, lock, and recovery.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: One CVM ZIP can generate multiple Parquet files in a caller-owned directory. Writing directly to the destination lets a failure on the second CSV alter or delete a Parquet that existed before the call. A temporary file for each output prevents individual corruption, but still exposes a partially updated batch.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
CvmFailureAtomicBatchCommit is the internal module executing extraction. It:

  1. validates the ZIP and lists every CSV before writing;
  2. rejects ZIPs with no CSV and basename collisions before creating outputs;
  3. creates a hidden staging area inside the destination directory so it stays on the same filesystem;
  4. converts every CSV only in that area and validates staged Parquet size, footer, and rows;
  5. backs up every pre-existing target before changing any target, preferring a hard link and falling back to metadata-preserving copy;
  6. applies os.replace() in deterministic order;
  7. on failure, removes new outputs and restores backups in reverse order;
  8. removes staging and backups only after a complete commit or normal rollback.

If restoration itself fails, the recovery area is preserved and the ExtractionError includes its path, the original failure, and the restore failure. This avoids deleting the only recoverable copy and retains the diagnostic cause.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The contract is a failure-atomic, recoverable batch commit, not a multi-file transaction with instant atomic visibility.
  • Concurrent readers and simultaneous writes to the same destination remain unsupported; the directory is caller-owned and may contain unrelated files, so it is never swapped as a whole.
  • The public CvmParquetExtractor.extract(...)->None signature, output names, and persisted schemas remain unchanged.
  • CSV, disk, staged-validation, replace, and corrupted-ZIP failures preserve pre-existing Parquets whenever normal rollback completes.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Other CVM families need download, conversion, and publication without depending on the company catalog. These mechanics know CVM CSV, ZIP, Parquet, and metadata contracts; global foundations serve multiple sources.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• brazil/cvm/ingestion/ owns reusable mechanics. An import contract prevents dependencies on fundamental_stocks_data/.
  • fundamental_stocks_data/ owns company catalogs, URLs, years, and destinations. The facade composes ingestion.http.CvmDownloadAdapter; extraction uses ingestion.extract.CvmParquetExtractor, and results belong to ingestion.models.DownloadResultCVM.
  • Configuration, safety, and transactional publication use their existing owners in core/ and macro_infra/.
  • Inventory associates outputs with their source through cvm.source-archive, without inferring ownership from Parquet filenames. The inventory guide defines replacement, preservation, and rejection of existing files.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Promoting the entire pipeline globally would spread CVM-specific contracts across other sources.
  • Keeping mechanics under companies or copying them into each family would preserve coupling or duplication.
  • Sharing within CVM separates these responsibilities and retains canonical owners without imposing common parsing or schemas on B3.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Compatible new families use the mechanics without consulting the company catalog. The exact-text-v1 contract, output names, and public signatures remain. Integrating another family’s official archives requires validating its format and rules. This change does not add public support for FIIs.

Automatic extraction checks inventory before and after the collaborator; the transaction checks direct extraction before publication. The default path scans three times, with cost proportional to destination files. A supplied extractor owns its writes and transaction; the later check does not undo arbitrary effects.

The .cvm-write-lock and publisher lock retain their lifecycles and concurrency limits. Relocation does not expand those guarantees.

docs.title: Migration and rollback
docs.text:
Internal consumers use canonical ingestion/ modules without aliases or forwarding modules. Filename inference present in develop was removed before reaching releases. Destinations with unidentified data require explicit preparation as described in the inventory guide.

A rollback restores implementation, imports, and checkers together, retaining one owner of writer state.

docs.title: Revisit triggers
docs.text: Revisit when another source needs the same operations and guarantees, or a CVM family requires a different dialect, schema, or publication lifecycle.

docs.title: PyArrow ingestion and transactional-integrity cutover
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-09-10 Scope: CVM and B3 extraction, Parquet publication, and runtime imports Decisions: Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The package loaded ingestion engines during import globaldatafinance, including for consumers that only queried the API. The CVM path inferred types per chunk and could encounter a decimal after fixing a column as an integer. The B3 path retained large dictionary buffers, rewrote Parquet during append, and accepted some invalid financial fields with silent defaults.

The existing CVM commit reduces the chance of a partially published batch but does not preserve a durable manifest or automatically recover an interruption between backups and replacements. That compromises financial-artifact integrity and recovery.

docs.title: Q1 — Source-owned PyArrow pipelines
docs.text:
Productive CVM and B3 pipelines remain independent and use PyArrow for Parquet reading, conversion, and writing. CVM preserves its QUOTE_NONE CSV dialect; B3 uses a strict fixed-width parser. The sources do not share inference, parsing, financial schemas, or filter rules.

Keeping only lazy imports around the existing pipelines was rejected because it does not correct local CVM inference, B3 buffering, or permissive parsing. A single generic framework was also rejected because the sources own different formats, lifecycles, and diagnostics.

docs.title: Q2 — Runtime imports and dependencies
docs.text:
Polars will be removed from runtime, the lockfile, tests, and scripts. PyArrow is the sole productive engine and loads only in the first operational path that needs it. The former ReadFilesAdapter was also removed by the infrastructure clean cut; Pandas is only an optional downstream dependency installed by the consumer.

Public facades and init.py files remain lightweight. Constructing a facade, querying B3 assets/years, or downloading CVM without extraction must not load pandas, NumPy, PyArrow, or Polars. The three root exports and public signatures remain unchanged.

docs.title: Q3 — Recoverable, failure-atomic publication
docs.text:
The internal macro_infra/transactional_publication/ facility provides same-filesystem staging, durable JSON manifests, directory locks, hard-link-or-copy backups, rollback, and recovery on the next call. It knows artifacts and paths only; it does not know source fields, schemas, filters, or formats.

The manifest records OPEN, VALIDATED, BACKUPS_READY, PUBLISHING, COMMITTED, CLEANUP_PENDING, ROLLING_BACK, and ROLLED_BACK. Every manifest path remains below the destination or staging area. A concurrent write to the same destination is rejected; a lock from another host or a live process is never removed merely because it is old.

The resulting contract is recoverable, failure-atomic batch commit. It does not offer instantly atomic visibility to concurrent readers of multiple CVM Parquets because multiple names cannot be replaced by one operation.

docs.title: Q4 — Per-source integrity rules
docs.text:
The CVM inference and types in this historical decision were superseded by the CVM exact text preservation contract, authorized on 2026-10-12. The other decisions remain applicable.

CVM performs a global text validation/inference pass followed by a second pass with an explicit schema. Short rows are padded at the end only; extra rows, missing headers, and ambiguous structures fail without publishing. A header-only CSV produces an empty Parquet with null fields, header order, and no pandas metadata.

B3 accepts only blank lines, 00/99 controls, and type-01 records that are exactly 245 bytes. Every quotation field is validated before TPMERC filtering; invalid values never become zero, an empty string, or null. Complete selection preserves every numeric code and reports unknown TPMERC values. The current persistence and verification contract is documented in the COTAHIST complete preservation and verified publication decision.

docs.title: Review-remediation decisions
docs.text:
The following decisions close the contracts found during the implementation review:

  • Settings.archive is the only canonical namespace for ZIP limits; Settings.archive_safety is not a compatibility alias. infos=None means that central-directory validation must run; a supplied list, including [], is an already validated selection and must be honored literally.
  • The globaldatafinance logger is isolated from the application hierarchy at import time with a NullHandler and propagate=False. setup_logging() only installs managed handlers after all candidates are prepared; a preparation or swap failure restores the previous level, propagation, and handlers without touching external handlers. LoggingSettings is strict and rejects the removed structured field and unknown DATAFIN_LOG_* variables. File destinations pass through the path-safety policy before any creation, and the formatter redacts known sensitive parameters and context fields; consumers still must not send secrets to logging.
  • CVM inference keeps nullable signed integers as int64; a null does not by itself promote the column to float64. The QUOTE_NONE dialect also keeps a physical blank one-column CSV record as a logical null.
  • The B3 clean cut removes the writer from service state and leaves closing to the concrete session. The session has explicit NEW, OPEN, and CLOSED states; a close failure is terminal, and the internal null marker is never accepted as literal input data.
  • ResourceMonitor remains a deliberate singleton, while the Arrow import cache remains lazy and private to the operational path that needs it. These are not compatibility shortcuts or parallel ingestion paths.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• This is release 0.2.0: strict B3 parsing, Polars removal, and removal of the internal legacy CSV path can require consumer migration.
  • CVM can reopen a source for multiple passes and create a transactional UTF-8 spool for CP1252 or Latin-1.
  • Publication now needs staging, manifests, backups, locks, and fsync where the platform supports it.
  • Fast and slow B3 retain logical equivalence but can use different memory and concurrency limits.
  • Input ZIPs and TXTs are never removed on failure; only transaction-derived artifacts can be cleaned up.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Do not change root exports, signatures, defaults, output names, logical schemas, or the Parquet format.
  • Do not add a service, queue, external process, web framework, or feature flag.
  • Do not support RFC quoted/multiline CSV alongside QUOTE_NONE in this cutover.
  • Do not retain a productive pandas/Polars fallback pipeline. This historical decision is superseded by the infrastructure clean cut for the removal of ReadFilesAdapter and the automatic Pandas dependency.
  • Do not make the annual COTAHIST corpus mandatory in CI before a licensed fixture exists.
  • Do not promise serializable isolation to concurrent CVM batch readers.

docs.title: Auditable real-data validation campaign
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-09-01 Scope: opt-in validation of external data and library artifacts

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Complete COTAHIST and CVM validation is executed by scripts/real_validation.py, an opt-in development command outside the library API. The executor is split into case-matrix construction, isolated workers, source validators, and evidence persistence.

The command requires explicit paths. COTAHIST is always caller-owned and is never downloaded; CVM contacts only the official endpoints in the matrix. Reports, work artifacts, and CVM output must be outside the repository. The campaign does not implicitly read .env and does not add financial data to Git.

Each case uses the corresponding public facade (HistoricalQuotesB3 or FundamentalStocksDataCVM) as its only processing path. The worker validates the input, executes the case, reads produced Parquet files with the real engines, and checks schema, counts, minimum content, and cleanup. One process per case limits leaked state and enables timeout with explicit classification.

The external report contains manifest.json, one current result per case in results.jsonl, individual logs, artifact evidence, and summary.json. Statuses are passed, failed, skipped, external_failure, and not_published. Exit code zero is reserved for a fully classified campaign with no failures, no pending external dependency, and no orphan-process finding. --resume uses the existing manifest and reruns only external failures or cases not yet executed.

Every --report, --cvm-output, and persisted campaign.cvmOutput from the manifest passes through the shared sensitive-destination policy. The original path text is retained so drive-relative, root-relative, and UNC semantics are validated even on a POSIX host. Validation occurs before mkdir, mkdtemp, a manifest, or an artifact. When resuming COTAHIST, the executor revalidates the catalog, compares each input’s size and SHA-256 with the manifest, and hashes each shared path only once. Drift raises ReportFormatError with the caseId, requires a new campaign, and leaves existing results neither rerun nor overwritten.

Persisted results are caller-owned evidence, not a signed attestation. When a pass/fail conclusion must serve as evidence, resume requires a trusted report directory.

When resuming CVM, the executor first reads, normalizes, and validates campaign.cvmOutput with the same policy. It then rebuilds every case from the official document/year matrix and requires caseId, source, document, year, mode, inputPath, url, and outputRoot to match the campaign destination before a worker is created. A tampered outputRoot is rejected before mkdir, mkdtemp, a worker, or an HTTP client. The publication probe uses only the canonical HTTPS URL, does not follow redirects, and never writes the response body. The compressed-ZIP limit is applied before a write from Content-Length, when present, and by the facade stream counter. The recorded size and SHA-256 are observed on the ZIP that the public facade passes to extraction, rather than on a separately downloaded copy.

The executor scripts have deterministic coverage separate from src, with an independent 85% floor in pre-push and in the quality pipeline.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
This boundary keeps network access, large datasets, execution time, and reports outside the library runtime. The matrix can prove real availability without treating CVM or DNS unavailability as approval. The campaign is slower than the deterministic suite and requires the caller to provide the COTAHIST dataset and an external CVM output directory.

Detailed source rules remain owned by their source areas: COTAHIST cataloging and member resolution belong to brazil/b3_data/historical_quotes/; CVM download, extraction, and commit behavior belong to brazil/cvm/fundamental_stocks_data/.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• The repository retained generic ZIP/CSV adapters with no active owning contract, duplicated destination preparation in CVM and B3, and duplicated temporary-file reservation.
  • Pandas remained a runtime dependency only for the legacy CSV reader, although the productive CVM/B3 pipelines already use PyArrow.
  • CVM and B3 have different formats, year floors, diagnostics, and ownership.
  • This is a deliberate breaking release. Root facades, Parquet schemas, output names, and transactional publication must remain stable.
  • Dominant attributes: data correctness, path safety, changeability, failure traceability, and low operational cost.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Extract only true invariants: destination normalization/preparation in core.utils.destination_paths and same-directory temporary reservation in macro_infra.temporary_files. CVM and B3 retain ownership of orchestration, year validation, formats, and source-specific messages.

ExtractorAdapter, ReadFilesAdapter, their modules, and the direct Pandas dependency are removed without an alias, warning, shim, or fallback. DownloadTimeoutError replaces the old custom timeout class. B3Error is a B3-only domain base; no GlobalDataFinanceError or other global catch-all base will be introduced. CVM staged filesystem write failures become ParquetWriteError, except ENOSPC, which remains DiskFullError.

There is no OpenSpec change: this is a release and accepted-contract cleanup, not a new shared specification lifecycle.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Keep local helpers and legacy adapters: rejected because it preserves divergence, an unnecessary runtime dependency, and an unowned surface.
  • Force CVM and B3 into one extractor/year validator: rejected because it mixes source rules, year floors, diagnostics, and responsibilities.
  • Extract only invariant primitives and hard-cut obsolete adapters: chosen because it removes duplication without inventing a domain abstraction while preserving same-filesystem publication.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• One internal contract normalizes and prepares destinations, checks safety before mkdir, and revalidates after creation.
  • One temporary reservation mechanism keeps .part and .parquet.tmp suffixes and cleans only the file created by the current call.
  • Fewer dependencies and no automatic Pandas installation.
  • Explicit B3 catch boundary without polluting the global hierarchy; CVM write failures distinguish infrastructure from source-content failures.

docs.title: Negative and mitigation
docs.text:
• Consumers of the old adapters or timeout class break immediately; the migration guide provides before/after imports and source-owned alternatives.
  • Consumers who need DataFrames must install Pandas; PyArrow is the documented default, and real artifact tests cover schemas and values.
  • The shared helpers become internal cross-owner contracts; direct unit tests cover races, chained causes, temporary files, and permissions.

docs.title: Migration/rollback note
docs.text: Migration is a single v0.2.0 cut: replace the timeout import, remove generic adapter imports, and declare Pandas in the consumer project when needed. Incremental compatibility is intentionally absent. Reverting requires restoring the modules, tests, dependency, and lockfile together; restoring only an alias would recreate a partial and ambiguous contract.

docs.title: Revisit trigger
docs.text: Revisit when a third source needs source-independent destination preparation or sibling temporary files with different semantics. Evaluate a new source-owned boundary then; do not extend these helpers with CVM- or B3-specific rules.

docs.title: Test execution tiers and local COTAHIST validation
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-08-30 Scope: repository tests and quality gates

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The test suite assigns exactly one primary tier to every test:

  • unit: isolated behavior using pure functions, fakes, stubs, or controlled local collaborators;
  • integration: a flow crossing two or more real production components, including deterministic local filesystem, ZIP, CSV, Parquet, and tmp_path behavior;
  • perf: a benchmark or a time, memory, or resource measurement, always opt-in.

unit and integration are mutually exclusive. The structural checker scripts/check_test_quality.py rejects tests with no tier or with more than one tier. It is a structural heuristic: it checks classification and an accepted observation in the test’s direct executable body without descending into nested helpers, lambdas, or classes. It does not replace review that an assertion protects a regression or prove the absence of every semantic tautology.

The slow, asyncio, and real_data markers are orthogonal qualifiers:

  • slow identifies heavy or time-sensitive work;
  • asyncio identifies a test that needs the async plugin;
  • real_data identifies caller-owned COTAHIST input and may only accompany the integration tier.

The deterministic default gate is:

uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m "not slow and not real_data and not perf" \
  --cov --cov-report=xml --cov-report=term-missing

Repository-created integrations stay in this gate when they are neither slow nor real_data. Performance and real-data suites are outside the default gate:

uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m unit
uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m "integration and not slow and not real_data and not perf"
uv run --locked --no-sync pytest tests/perf -m perf -o addopts=''

docs.title: Local COTAHIST
docs.text:
The directory configured in COTAHIST_PATH is always caller-owned. cotahist_b3_local/ is ignored by Git and is never downloaded by the suite. The two versioned synthetic samples in cotahist_b3/ belong to the examples and deterministic validation under tests/examples, without real_data. The fixture in tests/brazil/b3_data/historical_quotes/conftest.py, consumed by integration/test_real_cotahist.py, enforces these rules:

  1. Without COTAHIST_PATH, only the suite explicitly selected with -m real_data is skipped, with an actionable instruction. The default gate does not select it.
  2. With COTAHIST_PATH, a missing, unreadable, empty path, a path without a valid COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP or COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT, or a missing selected year fails; it does not skip.
  3. When present, COTAHIST_TEST_YEAR must contain exactly four digits. When absent, the fixture infers a year only when the catalog contains one year; with multiple years it fails with an actionable instruction and never picks the largest year.
  4. Extraction receives the resolved year explicitly. It never uses the system’s current year and never downloads data during the test.
  5. In the current implementation, the catalog fully preflights every available file: years, ZIP limits, members, hashes, and every record. This setup also runs with real_data and not slow; that selection avoids Parquet extraction but does not guarantee a short source read.
  6. Limited parity derives a non-empty sample of up to 20,000 real 01 records in tmp_path and compares fast and slow across all 32 Arrow fields with exact types and values. Because it runs both modes, it is marked slow.
  7. An annual fast proof validates the Arrow schema, record count, and date bounds. Another annual slow proof compares counts, schema, and table equality or a logical digest between fast and slow.

Run the catalog check and processing proofs with:

COTAHIST_PATH=./cotahist_b3_local COTAHIST_TEST_YEAR=2000 \
  uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m "real_data and not slow"
COTAHIST_PATH=./cotahist_b3_local COTAHIST_TEST_YEAR=2000 \
  uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m "real_data and slow"
COTAHIST_PATH=./cotahist_b3_local COTAHIST_TEST_YEAR=2024 \
  uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m "real_data and not slow"
COTAHIST_PATH=./cotahist_b3_local COTAHIST_TEST_YEAR=2024 \
  uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m "real_data and slow"

docs.title: Official-data trigger
docs.text: A future official annual sample becomes mandatory in CI only after an explicit release decision provides a repository-versioned fixture or a published CI artifact under a compatible license. Until that trigger exists, official data remain opt-in and caller-owned. Mandatory adoption must update provenance and licensing, the expected schema, the CI fixture, the corresponding job, and this decision together.

docs.title: Consequences and non-goals
docs.text: This decision makes test selection predictable, keeps CI deterministic, and allows parity validation without placing external financial data in Git. The persisted COTAHIST v2 contract with 32 fields is defined by the PyArrow integrity cutover decision; this decision keeps official data opt-in and caller-owned.

docs.title: Advanced Usage
docs.text: Advanced computational techniques, customization strategies, and optimization patterns for Global-Data-Finance.

docs.title: Logging System
docs.text:
Enable professional centralized logging for pipeline tracing and diagnostics:

from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM
from globaldatafinance.core.logging_config import (
    LoggingSettings,
    get_logger,
    log_execution_time,
    setup_logging,
)

# Configure system-wide logging
setup_logging(LoggingSettings(level="INFO", log_file="app.log"))

# Retrieve module-specific logger instance
logger = get_logger("globaldatafinance.example")
cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM()

# Emit structured contextual logging events
logger.info(
    "Download workflow initiated",
    extra={"doc_type": "DFP", "year": 2023}
)

# Measure execution performance via timing context manager
with log_execution_time(logger, "CVM Filing Ingestion", total=5):
    result = cvm.download(
        destination_path="/data/cvm",
        list_docs=["DFP"],
        initial_year=2023,
        last_year=2023,
    )

See logging configuration

The globaldatafinance logger starts quiet with a NullHandler and propagate=False; setup_logging() does not alter the application root logger. Reconfiguration replaces only library-managed handlers. If preparation or the swap fails, the previous configuration is restored. LoggingSettings rejects extra fields and unknown DATAFIN_LOG_* variables, including the removed structured field.

docs.title: Global Configuration Tuning
docs.text:
Customize underlying network timeout and retry behavior via environment variables:

The library reads defaults and DATAFINANCE_* variables from the process environment. It does not search for or load a .env file automatically from the current working directory. Advanced callers may pass _env_file=... directly to Settings when they explicitly want pydantic-settings to load a file; this does not add a dotenv option to the public facades.

When passing _env_file to the root Settings, configure networking through a nested JSON object, such as DATAFINANCE_NETWORK={"timeout": 240} in the file. The flat DATAFINANCE_NETWORK_TIMEOUT key works in the process environment; do not assume the root model’s file propagates to NetworkSettings. Inject the explicit snapshot with FundamentalStocksDataCVM(settings=...) or HistoricalQuotesB3(settings=...).

# Expand socket timeout threshold for high-latency connections
export DATAFINANCE_NETWORK_TIMEOUT=900

# Increase maximum connection retry attempts
export DATAFINANCE_NETWORK_MAX_RETRIES=10

# Configure an aggressive exponential retry back-off factor
export DATAFINANCE_NETWORK_RETRY_BACKOFF=3.0

from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM, HistoricalQuotesB3
from globaldatafinance.core.config import NetworkSettings, Settings

# Immutable snapshot from current environment
settings = Settings()
print(f"Active network timeout: {settings.network.timeout}s")
print(f"Max configured retries: {settings.network.max_retries}")

# Explicit configuration injected into public facades
custom_settings = Settings(network=NetworkSettings(timeout=300))
cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM(settings=custom_settings)
b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3(settings=custom_settings)

docs.title: ZIP limits and UNC destinations
docs.text:
Archive limits also belong to Settings, apply to both CVM and B3, and are validated before extraction begins. Defaults are 2 GiB for the compressed ZIP and each member, 8 GiB total uncompressed data, 10,000 members, and a maximum compression ratio of 200. Invalid values fail during configuration startup, not during a partial write.

export DATAFINANCE_ARCHIVE_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES=2147483648
export DATAFINANCE_ARCHIVE_MAX_MEMBERS=10000
export DATAFINANCE_ARCHIVE_MAX_MEMBER_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES=2147483648
export DATAFINANCE_ARCHIVE_MAX_TOTAL_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES=8589934592
export DATAFINANCE_ARCHIVE_MAX_COMPRESSION_RATIO=200

# UNC is denied by default. The JSON list may contain only trusted roots.
export DATAFINANCE_PATH_SAFETY_ALLOWED_UNC_ROOTS='["\\\\fileserver\\finance\\exports"]'

POSIX roots, Windows drive roots, Windows system directories, and unauthorized UNC shares are rejected before a directory is created. Even with an allowlist, administrative shares ending in $ remain forbidden. This policy reduces accidental writing to sensitive destinations; it does not constrain a caller that already has the process’s privileges.

ZIP limits live in the canonical Settings.archive namespace; do not use the removed Settings.archive_safety name. The CRC helper distinguishes infos=None (validate the central directory) from infos=[] (an already validated empty selection).

docs.title: Resource Monitoring Engine
docs.text:
Use the monitor to inspect resources and choose how many workers to start:

from globaldatafinance.core import ResourceMonitor, ResourceState

# Initialize monitor telemetry instance
monitor = ResourceMonitor()

# Evaluate immediate system capacity state
state = monitor.check_resources()
if state == ResourceState.CRITICAL:
    print("Warning: System resources entering critical saturation!")

# Calculate a safe worker count for the current resources
safe_workers = monitor.get_safe_worker_count(max_workers=16)
print(f"Allocated {safe_workers} safe concurrent worker threads")

# Pause execution until system resources return below saturation thresholds
if not monitor.wait_for_resources(timeout_seconds=120):
    raise TimeoutError("Resources unavailable after 120 seconds")

View resource monitoring documentation →

ResourceMonitor retains its singleton contract; the B3 path uses an isolated instance when it needs source-specific limits, without replacing the global singleton. The private cache for PyArrow modules is also lazy and is populated only when the Parquet operation is actually used.

docs.title: Custom Retry Strategies
docs.text:
Implement tailored retry loop policies when constructing defensive pipeline wrappers:

from globaldatafinance.core.utils.retry_strategy import RetryStrategy
import time

strategy = RetryStrategy(
    initial_backoff=1.0,
    max_backoff=30.0,
    multiplier=2.0
)

max_retries = 5  # Additional attempts after the first execution.
for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
    try:
        result = risky_operation()
        break
    except Exception as exc:
        if not strategy.is_retryable(exc):
            raise

        if attempt < max_retries:
            backoff = strategy.calculate_backoff(attempt)
            print(f"Retry attempt {attempt + 1} scheduled in {backoff}s...")
            time.sleep(backoff)
        else:
            raise

View retry strategy documentation →

docs.title: Custom Adapter Substitution & Duck Typing
docs.text: The CVM download and extraction adapters are concrete classes. DownloadDocumentsUseCaseCVM accepts a collaborator with the expected download_docs(tasks, *, automatic_extractor=False) method. This is an internal extension example: its result is illustrative. Implement the transport and record actual outcomes before using a custom adapter.

docs.title: Replacing the HTTP Download Adapter
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.brazil.cvm.fundamental_stocks_data.client import (
    DownloadDocumentsUseCaseCVM,
)
from globaldatafinance.brazil.cvm.ingestion.models import (
    DownloadResultCVM,
)
from globaldatafinance.brazil.cvm.ingestion.http import (
    DownloadTaskCVM,
)


class MyCustomAdapter:
    """Alternative download adapter utilizing duck-typed interface matching."""

    def download_docs(
        self,
        tasks: list[DownloadTaskCVM],
        *,
        automatic_extractor: bool | None = None,
    ) -> DownloadResultCVM:
        # tasks represents a list of DownloadTaskCVM: (url, doc_name, year, destination_path).
        # Implement your customized transport infrastructure (wget, aiohttp, gsutil, etc.)
        # and return the expected result tracking object.
        return DownloadResultCVM(
            successful_downloads=["DFP_2023"],
            failed_downloads={},
            elapsed_time=0.0,
        )


adapter = MyCustomAdapter()
use_case = DownloadDocumentsUseCaseCVM(repository=adapter)
result = use_case.execute(
    destination_path="./cvm_custom_data",
    list_docs=["DFP"],
    initial_year=2023,
    last_year=2023,
)

The orchestrator uses the collaborator’s method contract without requiring a shared base class. See architecture for ownership and boundaries.

docs.title: Configuring Dedicated Logging Handlers
docs.text:
import logging
from globaldatafinance.core import get_logger

# Register custom module logger
logger = get_logger("my_custom_pipeline")
logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

# Attach file output handler with explicit debugging threshold
file_handler = logging.FileHandler("globaldatafinance_debug.log")
file_handler.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
formatter = logging.Formatter(
    '%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s'
)
file_handler.setFormatter(formatter)
logger.addHandler(file_handler)

# Emit diagnostic record
logger.info("Custom pipeline execution starting...")

docs.title: Spawning Concurrent Multi-Year Extractions
docs.text:
The B3 extractor accepts COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP or .TXT. When both exist for one year, both are validated; ZIP is selected only when their decompressed contents are identical. Different contents cause failure.

For one consolidated output, prefer a single call covering the full range: the extractor coordinates its sources. The example below produces one file per year. Its outer pool is caller-managed: GDF_B3_WORKER_LIMIT applies to each extraction, not the total number of external processes. Set the outer limit from the total CPU and RAM budget; each call uses slow to keep one source worker.

Each parallel call uses its own destination directory: the publication lock is directory-scoped, even when output filenames differ.

from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
from globaldatafinance import ExtractionResultB3, HistoricalQuotesB3

def extract_year(year: int) -> ExtractionResultB3:
    b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
    return b3.extract(
        path_of_docs="/data/cotahist",
        assets_list=["ações"],
        initial_year=year,
        last_year=year,
        destination_path=f"./data_b3/{year}",
        output_filename=f"stocks_{year}",
        processing_mode="slow",
    )

def main() -> None:
    years = range(2020, 2024)
    caller_worker_limit = 2
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=caller_worker_limit) as executor:
        results = list(executor.map(extract_year, years))

    for year, result in zip(years, results):
        if not result["success"]:
            raise RuntimeError(result["errors"] or result["message"])
        print(f"{year}: {result['total_records']:,} records")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Column projection and batch filtering
docs.text:
import pyarrow.compute as pc
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

# Read only required columns in bounded batches
parquet = pq.ParquetFile("cotahist.parquet")
for batch in parquet.iter_batches(
    batch_size=100_000,
    columns=["data_pregao", "ticker", "preco_fechamento"],
):
    petr4 = batch.filter(pc.equal(batch.column("ticker"), "PETR4"))
    process_chunk(petr4)

Polars is not a runtime dependency. Applications that use it as a downstream reader must declare it in their own environment.

docs.title: Batch Processing via Streaming (PyArrow)
docs.text:
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

# Stream large Parquet dataset in memory-efficient batches
parquet_file = pq.ParquetFile("cotahist.parquet")
for batch in parquet_file.iter_batches(batch_size=100000):
    process_chunk(batch)

The PyArrow modules used for writing remain lazily imported and privately cached; the dependency is loaded only when the Parquet path runs.

Import the main clients and the B3 result type from the package root:

from globaldatafinance import (
    FundamentalStocksDataCVM,

docs.title: FundamentalStocksDataCVM
docs.text: Downloads CVM regulatory filings and optionally extracts them to Parquet.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
__init__()

def __init__(self, *, settings: Settings | None = None) -> None:
    ...

Creates a CVM client with the standard download and validation components.

settings accepts an immutable Settings snapshot imported from globaldatafinance.core.config. With None, each client reads a fresh snapshot of the current environment; the settings property exposes the snapshot used.

download()

def download(
    self,
    destination_path: str,
    list_docs: list[str] | None = None,
    initial_year: int | None = None,
    last_year: int | None = None,
    automatic_extractor: bool = False,
) -> DownloadResultCVM:
    ...

Downloads regulatory CVM archives directly into a local filesystem directory.

Parameters:

  • destination_path (str): Target destination storage directory.
  • list_docs (list[str], optional): Selected document type codes (e.g., ["DFP", "ITR"]). Defaults to all supported document categories when omitted.
  • initial_year (int, optional): First year, inclusive. None uses the first supported year for each document type.
  • last_year (int, optional): Last year, inclusive. None uses the current system year.
  • automatic_extractor (bool): Extract downloaded ZIP archives to Apache Parquet. Default: False.

When enabled, the CVM extractor uses PyArrow and QUOTE_NONE, with Arrow string columns and exact text preservation, including empty fields as "". The original ZIP is retained and every record is checked before publication. Header-only CSVs keep string columns and zero rows. See the CVM exact text migration for the persisted contract and consumer changes.

Returns:

  • DownloadResultCVM: Structured result object containing:
  • success_count_downloads (int): Count of successfully downloaded archives.
  • error_count_downloads (int): Count of failed downloads.
  • successful_downloads (list[str]): List of completed document identifiers in {DOC}_{YEAR} format (e.g., DFP_2023). These values are logical identifiers, not full filesystem paths or filenames.
  • failed_downloads (dict[str, str]): Mapping of failed document identifiers to failure messages.
  • elapsed_time (float): Total wall-clock execution time in seconds.
  • has_errors() (bool): Helper method returning True if any download failed.

async_download()

async def async_download(
    self,
    destination_path: str,
    list_docs: list[str] | None = None,
    initial_year: int | None = None,
    last_year: int | None = None,
    automatic_extractor: bool = False,
) -> DownloadResultCVM:
    ...

Asynchronous counterpart to download(). Use when calling from inside an existing asyncio event loop to avoid nested loop runtime errors.

get_available_docs()

def get_available_docs(self) -> dict[str, str]:
    ...

Returns document codes ("DFP", "ITR", "FCA", "FRE", "CGVN", "VLMO", "IPE") and their descriptions.

get_available_years()

def get_available_years(self) -> AvailableYearsInfoCVM:
    ...

Returns an AvailableYearsInfoCVM named tuple with the first supported years and the current system year:

  • general_min_year (int): Minimum available year for standard documents (e.g. 2010).
  • itr_min_year (int): Minimum available year for quarterly ITR filings (e.g. 2011).
  • cgvn_vlmo_min_year (int): Minimum available year for CGVN / VLMO filings (e.g. 2018).
  • current_year (int): Current system year.
  • ipe_min_year (int, property): First IPE year, 2003.

years._asdict() contains the four tuple fields; ipe_min_year is an additional property accessed through its attribute.

docs.title: HistoricalQuotesB3
docs.text: Extracts and consolidates historical B3 quotations from local COTAHIST files.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
__init__()

def __init__(self, *, settings: Settings | None = None) -> None:
    ...

Creates a B3 client with the standard parser and extraction components.

settings accepts an immutable Settings snapshot imported from globaldatafinance.core.config. With None, each client reads a fresh snapshot of the current environment; the settings property exposes the snapshot used.

extract()

def extract(
    self,
    path_of_docs: str,
    assets_list: list[str] | None = None,
    initial_year: int | None = None,
    last_year: int | None = None,
    destination_path: str | None = None,
    output_filename: str = "cotahist_extracted",
    processing_mode: str = "fast",
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> ExtractionResultB3:
    ...

Parses COTAHIST ZIP or TXT files (COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP or .TXT), filters quotations by market type, and writes one consolidated Parquet file. It returns an ExtractionResultB3 mapping containing status, counts, errors, and the output path.

Parameters:

  • path_of_docs (str): Directory containing local COTAHIST ZIP or TXT files.
  • assets_list (list[str] | None): Asset categories; None selects todos, every valid numeric TPMERC.
  • initial_year (int, optional): First year, inclusive. None uses 1986.
  • last_year (int, optional): Last year, inclusive. None uses the current system year.
  • destination_path (str, optional): Custom directory destination for the generated Parquet artifact (defaults to path_of_docs when omitted).
  • output_filename (str): Base output filename for the created Parquet file (must be a basename without path separators; a .parquet suffix is optional and is appended when omitted). Default: "cotahist_extracted".
  • processing_mode (str): Both modes use bounded batches and the same Parquet schema. "fast" allows concurrent sources within resource limits; "slow" uses one source worker and smaller batches. Default: "fast".
  • verbose (bool): When True (default), prints a formatted summary to stdout.

Returns:

  • ExtractionResultB3 (TypedDict): A result mapping with these keys:
  • success (bool): True if extraction completed without errors.
  • message (str): Human-readable execution outcome summary.
  • total_files (int): Number of annual inputs resolved for the request.
  • success_count (int): Number of sources included in committed output.
  • error_count (int): Number of entries in errors.
  • total_records (int): Committed output row count.
  • output_file (str): Newly committed output path; empty on failure.
  • assets (list[str]): Asset categories filtered during run.
  • processing_mode (str): Execution mode selected ("fast" or "slow").
  • elapsed_time (float): Elapsed execution time in seconds.
  • schema_version (int): Parquet schema version (2).
  • integrity (B3IntegrityReport): Requested coverage, sources, counts, verification, warnings, and published-artifact hash. See the complete key contract.
  • errors (dict[str, str]): Dictionary mapping failed files to failure error messages. The key is always present and may be empty.

Official B3 downloads use ZIP archives, but the API accepts both COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP and the uncompressed COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT. When both formats exist for the same year, both are fully validated. ZIP is selected only when their uncompressed contents are identical; different contents cause failure. output_filename must be a basename without path separators; the .parquet suffix is optional and is appended only when omitted.

A missing requested year returns success=False, lists missing years in integrity.missing_years, and does not publish a new output. An empty directory reports zero resolved files and every requested year as missing.

If every requested source is valid and the filter excludes all quotations, extraction publishes an empty result (success=True). On preflight failure, integrity retains previously validated sources and missing years; success_count and total_records remain zero.

All 01 records are validated before filtering. TPMERC 021 is selected with lote_bloco; todos also includes unknown numeric codes. Every requested year must be present, and the complete output is read back before publication. See the B3 v2 schema reference and migration guide.

  • 'etf': Exchange Traded Funds

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Global-Data-Finance is a Python library consumed by applications. It receives caller selections, files, and paths; it returns structured results and Parquet artifacts. Current sources are CVM and B3.

flowchart TD
    Caller[Python application] --> API[Public facades]
    API --> CVM[CVM download and extraction]
    API --> B3[B3 COTAHIST extraction]
    CVM --> Shared[Shared configuration, safety, and I/O]
    B3 --> Shared

docs.title: Where to start in the code
docs.text:
Paths below are relative to src/globaldatafinance/.

Responsibility Location Public exports __init__.py: FundamentalStocksDataCVM, HistoricalQuotesB3, ExtractionResultB3 Facade validation and orchestration application/cvm_docs/ and application/b3_docs/ CVM company selection and policies brazil/cvm/fundamental_stocks_data/ CVM archive downloads and preservation brazil/cvm/ingestion/ B3 behavior brazil/b3_data/historical_quotes/ Configuration, logging, retry, and safety core/ Generic I/O and recoverable publication macro_infra/ Shared base exceptions macro_exceptions/

For CVM, fundamental_stocks_data/client.py plans company documents and years. The facade directly composes ingestion/http.py for downloads; ingestion/csv_pipeline/ preserves CSV content and ingestion/transaction.py coordinates publication. Shared CVM infrastructure does not depend on the company catalog. For B3, catalog.py resolves inputs, source_validation/ and cotahist_parser/ validate and interpret records, and extraction_service/ and parquet_writer/ coordinate output.

docs.title: Data flows
docs.text:
CVM: the facade validates the request, resolves document/year selections, and calls the HTTP adapter. The ZIP is validated and retained. When requested, extraction converts CSVs in staging, checks content, and publishes the Parquet batch.

B3: the facade resolves local COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP or COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT files. The extractor accepts ZIP and TXT; it validates each source and every record before filtering, processes batches, merges the Parquet, and verifies output before publication.

Presentation belongs to *_formatter.py modules in application/. Orchestrators coordinate collaborators; validation and transformation should not incorporate I/O that belongs to adapters.

Additional CVM families can consume ingestion/ when they share the exact-text-v1 contract. They retain document and period selection in their own modules and use canonical ingestion types. Source-identity metadata determines inventory in direct and automatic extraction, including supplied extractors. There are no compatibility adapters or ownership inference from old filenames. Another CSV dialect requires its own decision.

docs.title: Contracts a change must preserve
docs.text:
• API: public imports, signatures, defaults, results, and exceptions. CVM uses DownloadResultCVM; B3 uses ExtractionResultB3. Check partial failure diagnostics rather than relying only on the absence of exceptions.
  • CVM: retained ZIPs and Parquet string columns under exact-text-v1.
  • B3: annual COTAHIST names, every requested year, complete default selection, and Parquet schema v2. Coexisting ZIP/TXT inputs require equivalent content. fast uses bounded concurrency; slow uses one worker.
  • Safety: validate inputs, ZIPs, names, and destinations before creating directories or writing. Source-specific rules stay within their source.
  • Publication: macro_infra/transactional_publication/ provides staging, a journal, lock, backups, and recovery; sources retain parsing, schemas, and validation. Recovery does not authorize removing caller files or guarantee simultaneous batch visibility for concurrent readers.

Persistence and recovery details belong to the technical reference and publication protocol.

docs.title: Organize a change
docs.text:
CVM and B3 have different needs and may use different internal organizations. Move a responsibility to core/, macro_infra/, or macro_exceptions/ when it is actually shared. Avoid creating interfaces, layers, or re-exports merely to make sources uniform.

A new source needs a complete delivery: source implementation, a facade in application/, a public export, behavior tests, and documentation in Portuguese and English. Keep dependencies acyclic and restrict __init__.py to explicit exports.

Tests mirror public, source, and shared boundaries. Their subdirectories organize topics; they do not create runtime layers. See testing and contributing to validate a change.
