docs.title: Performance Benchmarks
docs.text:
This document records reproducible baselines for extraction and processing across the B3 and CVM modules. The numbers are evidence from a reference scenario and serve as a regression metric, not a fixed-time promise for every machine or dataset.

The 2026-10-06 COTAHIST optimizations, comparisons, and operating conditions are documented in the performance and integrity guide.

docs.title: 1.1. Historical Measurement of Implementation v3 — 27 Years (2026-09-16, Revision f1a2f47)
docs.text:
Environment: Python 3.13.7 · Linux x86_64 (kernel 6.8) · 8 CPUs · 7.55 GB total memory. No network calls; local extraction of official ZIPs only.

  • Dataset: 27 official ZIP files (2000–2026), 666.00 MB compressed.
  • Asset scope: public categories supported in revision v3; the selection did not include TPMERC 021.
  • Errors: 0 (all 27 files processed successfully).
  • Consolidated Parquet output: 481.86 MB per mode (505,265,249 bytes).
Mode Written rows Elapsed time (API) Elapsed time (end-to-end) Peak RSS Throughput fast 22,303,577 649.99 s 650.50 s 429.88 MiB 34,313.8 rows/s slow 22,303,577 749.45 s 750.10 s 331.11 MiB 29,759.9 rows/s

Note: The slow mode peaked at only 331.11 MiB (~0.32 GiB) RSS (a ~23% memory reduction compared to fast mode), preserving 100% schema and data parity across all 22,303,577 records of the 27-year series. The modest ~98 MiB memory difference between fast and slow stems from bounded per-worker limits (python_record_limit of 25,000 vs 10,000 rows) and chunked flushes (ROW_GROUP_LIMIT = 200,000), keeping memory complexity $O(1)$ relative to the time span. The moderate ~15% speed advantage of fast mode reflects the plausible hypothesis of CPython GIL contention in ThreadPoolExecutor during the CPU-intensive positional string parsing loop and batch building in Python, alongside the sequential disk merge stage (while zlib decompression and C++ PyArrow writes release the GIL, Python positional slicing and row validation retain the lock). Compared to historical baseline v2 (~4.4 GB), the columnar streaming architecture reduced peak memory by over 90%.

Measurement scope: these are historical figures from before the COTAHIST schema v2 contract. The corpus contained 22,305,860 quotations, and the measurement excluded 2,283 TPMERC 021 rows. It therefore does not measure the current contract’s volume, schema, or processing cost and is not directly comparable.

This measurement uses the Arrow ingestion runner introduced by this cutover. It does not replace the historical v1 baseline: the corpus generator, explicit schema, and separation between operation and validation time are part of a stricter protocol. It is reproducible candidate evidence and a starting point for future comparisons made under the same protocol.

Scenario Repeats Rows Operation time (median) Peak RSS (median) Parquet output Logical equivalence B3 250k 3 250,000 5.832 s 215.898 MiB 5,822,005 B 3/3

docs.title: 4. Limitations and Contracts
docs.text:
• The synthetic B3 fixture validates the complete parsing, filtering, and Parquet-writing path, but does not represent the cardinality, compression, or asset mix of a real B3 year.
  • When updating reproducible numbers, preserve: dataset, checksum, hardware, Python version, code revision, repetition count, and metric definitions.
  • To attribute an improvement to refactoring, freeze two distinct versions and record product and validation module hashes. Runs with identical modules measure host variability. Compare versions with the same data, dependencies, markets, backend, and effective resource limits, alternating fresh-process order and retaining every sample.
  • Operation time includes preflight, workers, merge, and complete final readback; the subsequent independent audit has its own timer. Record host load and swap activity as well as aggregate RSS. When measuring CPU, add parent and completed worker CPU and report it separately from wall time.
  • Profiler timings locate bottlenecks but do not establish throughput gains. A microbenchmark improvement requires confirmation in the complete operation; synthetic workload results cannot be extrapolated to all official years.

docs.title: 5. Fresh-process ingestion runner
docs.text:
scripts/benchmark_ingestion.py measures root import, CVM, CVM text, B3 at 100k and 250k records, the multi-file scenario b3_multi_4x25k (four 25k-row files by default), runtime footprint, and, when available, the annual B3 corpus. It generates deterministic corpus data in a temporary directory, repeats each scenario three times by default, runs the operation in a fresh Python process, and samples child RSS every 10 ms. It supports comparative evaluation via --backend thread|process and --processing-mode fast|slow. Before recording a result it validates row count, order, schema, boundary values, and the logical Parquet artifact. For the annual corpus, both the reference digest and extraction cover every asset class supported by the API across the 27 official ZIPs; each repeat is compared with that typed digest. --processing-mode runs only the selected mode and does not start the other mode automatically. --source-count is exclusive to the synthetic b3_multi_4x25k corpus and partitions requested rows across the exact number of sources; the annual corpus always uses its 27 sources. --worker-limit applies a cap in the fresh measurement process through GDF_B3_WORKER_LIMIT; JSON records both requested and effective values after resource policy and backend fallback.

The annual reference uses the independent COTAHIST decoder and includes all 32 fields, with the textual uncompressed-content hash, source year, physical line, and original bytes. The todos marker also preserves quotations from markets without a mapped asset class. Preparing this digest is outside extraction timing.

# Small measurement to verify the JSON protocol
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/benchmark_ingestion.py \
  --scenario import_root --scenario cvm --rows 10 --repeats 1

# Full synthetic corpora, three repetitions, and a persisted report
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/benchmark_ingestion.py \
  --scenario cvm --scenario cvm_text --scenario b3_100k \
  --scenario b3_250k --scenario b3_multi_4x25k --repeats 3 --output benchmark.json

# Explicit comparison of execution backend and processing mode
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/benchmark_ingestion.py \
  --scenario b3_multi_4x25k --backend process --processing-mode fast --repeats 3

# Fallback proof: two sources, but only one effective worker
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/benchmark_ingestion.py \
  --scenario b3_multi_4x25k --rows 100 --source-count 2 --worker-limit 1 \
  --backend process --processing-mode fast

# Run only slow across all markets; all 27 ZIPs are required
mkdir -p .benchmarks
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/benchmark_ingestion.py \
  --scenario b3_annual --cotahist-path /path/to/COTAHIST \
  --processing-mode slow --repeats 1 \
  --output .benchmarks/b3-annual-slow.json

Each JSON result contains schema version, revision, environment, input checksum, row count, schema fingerprint, logical equivalence, a typed logical digest, physical artifact SHA-256 (artifact_sha256), operation time, operation/validation phases, processing mode, execution backend, requested and effective source/worker counts, initial/peak/final parent RSS (rss_peak_mib, preserving comparison with historical baseline v1), aggregate tree peak RSS (aggregate_rss_peak_mib), observed child process count, output bytes, status, and worktree_sha256. RSS is resident memory per process, not heap. aggregate_rss_peak_mib is the sum of parent and descendant RSS in the same sample; shared pages can be counted more than once, so it is not unique physical memory, host-wide memory, or cgroup memory use. Equivalence compares every typed row (including nulls, ordering, and decimal tuples), not only boundary values. The child verifies the checksum before measuring, so a changed source fails instead of producing an invalid comparison. An annual run without all 27 required ZIPs reports skipped with external corpus unavailable; release reports must not turn that into success.

When git_sha ends in -dirty, worktree_sha256 identifies the tracked diff and the contents of non-ignored untracked files present when measurement began. Results under .benchmarks/ are deliberately local and ignored; for a reviewable claim, preserve the emitted JSON in a tracked review artifact and cite both provenance fields.

Reference gates for this change are compared only on the same baseline/candidate machine: root import ≤50 MiB and ≤0.50 s; CVM 269,181 rows ≤60% of baseline time and ≤70% of baseline RSS; B3 250k ≤50% of baseline time and ≤25% of baseline RSS; and a closed runtime footprint without Polars ≤260 MiB. These are release objectives, not universal CI limits.

docs.title: 6. CVM Optimizations — Encoding, Inference, and HTTP
6.1. Historical Encoding Scan and Terminal Inference
docs.text:
The CVM measurements from 2026-09-23 predate the exact-text-v1 contract and its complete content validation. They are not a baseline for the current implementation. The current runner verifies digests with every CVM field preserved as text; the numeric and long-text scenarios share the same input preparation in integration tests and the CLI.

On 2026-09-23, the cvm and cvm_text scenarios ran in three fresh processes per stage against the same deterministic corpora. Environment: Python 3.13.9, Linux x86_64, kernel 6.8, 8 CPUs. The scan stage replaces per-byte classification with a C-level block translation; scan + inference also stops observing columns once they have been promoted permanently to strings.

Scenario Stage Repeats Median time Median peak RSS cvm baseline 3 4.092 s 166.30 MiB cvm scan 3 1.798 s 165.99 MiB cvm scan + inference 3 1.593 s 162.10 MiB cvm_text baseline 3 2.705 s 227.28 MiB cvm_text scan 3 0.822 s 227.13 MiB cvm_text scan + inference 3 0.762 s 227.33 MiB

The scan reduced median time by 56.1% for cvm and 69.6% for cvm_text. Terminal inference reduced it by a further 11.4% and 7.3%, respectively, compared with the scan stage. Final peak RSS was 2.5% below baseline for cvm and 0.02% above baseline for cvm_text.

All three stages produced identical row counts, schema fingerprints, logical digests, and physical Parquet SHA-256 values across all nine repeats per scenario. The logical digests were 1ef1f6d9cd9ade4fba4551796916241ff0966620846a219b1f87be78f0e186c9 for cvm (269,181 rows) and 2f3649d866f98263ce2156bdb688733da3ae31b0fbc7c963c720675c6ae49d0b for cvm_text (8,000 rows).

Full reports with input checksums, each repeat, and git_sha / worktree_sha256 provenance are available as baseline, scan, and scan + inference reports. Measure the same scenarios on the current version with the command below. Reproducing the historical stages requires their implementations and contracts.

mkdir -p .benchmarks
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/benchmark_ingestion.py \
  --scenario cvm --scenario cvm_text --repeats 3 \
  --output .benchmarks/cvm-optimizations.json

docs.title: 6.2. CVM Download Phase Measurements
docs.text:
scripts/benchmark_cvm_http.py separately measures time and bytes for GET, ZIP validation, and Parquet extraction. Local mode serves the same deterministic ZIP over HTTP/1.1, runs batches of three downloads by default, and compares 8, 64, and 256 KiB chunks. GET bytes are transferred bytes; validation records the ZIP size read; extraction records the uncompressed CSV bytes. The report also counts httpx.AsyncClient constructions and measures their synchronous constructor cost.

The current download validates its size against the GET response’s own Content-Length, when available and valid, and makes no HEAD request. To preserve JSON schema 1, the head phase fields and announced_bytes counters remain in the report with zero values. The client-initialization fraction uses only cumulative GET time as HTTP time.

mkdir -p .benchmarks
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/benchmark_cvm_http.py \
  --source local --repeats 3 --batch-size 3 --payload-mib 4 \
  --output .benchmarks/cvm-http-local.json

For a few equivalent official sources, provide explicit URLs:

mkdir -p .benchmarks
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/benchmark_cvm_http.py \
  --source official \
  --official-url https://dados.cvm.gov.br/dados/CIA_ABERTA/DOC/DFP/DADOS/dfp_cia_aberta_2022.zip \
  --official-url https://dados.cvm.gov.br/dados/CIA_ABERTA/DOC/DFP/DADOS/dfp_cia_aberta_2023.zip \
  --official-url https://dados.cvm.gov.br/dados/CIA_ABERTA/DOC/DFP/DADOS/dfp_cia_aberta_2024.zip \
  --repeats 3 --output .benchmarks/cvm-http-official.json

On 2026-09-23, the local run completed with passed: nine batches, three repeats per chunk size, and three downloads per batch. The medians below show total batch time; phase times sum the concurrent operations in each batch. This historical measurement used a HEAD request after each GET; the HEAD column and client counts below describe that implementation.

Chunk Total batch HEAD GET Validation Extraction HTTPX client initialization 8 KiB 0.246 s 0.049 s 0.201 s 0.013 s 0.136 s 6 clients; 0.0369 s 64 KiB 0.241 s 0.046 s 0.151 s 0.014 s 0.133 s 6 clients; 0.0371 s 256 KiB 0.236 s 0.047 s 0.157 s 0.013 s 0.128 s 6 clients; 0.0371 s

Each batch transferred 12,590,178 bytes across three GETs. HEAD announced the same size; validation read the same number of bytes; extraction processed 6,612 CSV bytes. All nine runs produced three Parquet files and 768 rows, with identical schema fingerprints and artifact SHA-256 values. The best median total time was 4.2% below the 8 KiB chunk, with variation between repeats and a small difference between 64 and 256 KiB. The six httpx.AsyncClient constructors totaled about 37 ms per batch, 18% of cumulative GET and HEAD time. The synthetic local benchmark did not compare shared clients and found a small total-time difference between chunks. At the time, these results supported keeping the 8 KiB chunk and HTTPX client-construction lifecycle.

The full report, including each repeat, fixture checksum, and git_sha / worktree_sha256 provenance, is available as cvm-http-local-20260923.json. The first local attempt inside the sandbox failed to bind the fixture server to 127.0.0.1 (PermissionError: Operation not permitted); the later local run passed. The official measurement was skipped: DNS lookup for dados.cvm.gov.br still fails in this environment.

docs.title: 6.3. Full benchmark against live CVM data
docs.text:
scripts/benchmark_cvm_full.py manually downloads and extracts CVM filings from 2010 through 2026, measures elapsed time and parent-process peak RSS, and summarizes the generated Parquet files. It accesses CVM and writes large artifacts, so it is outside deterministic tests and CI. Provide an existing, empty directory:

mkdir -p .benchmarks/cvm-full
uv run --locked --no-sync python -m scripts.benchmark_cvm_full \
  --output-dir .benchmarks/cvm-full

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Use Python >=3.12,<4.0, Git, and uv. Create your branch from develop and open the pull request against that same branch.

docs.title: Set up the environment
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/jordanestralioto/Global-Data-Finance.git
cd Global-Data-Finance
uv sync --locked --all-extras --dev
uv run --locked --no-sync pre-commit install --install-hooks
git switch -c fix/cotahist-validation develop

uv sync prepares the environment once. Afterwards, run tools with uv run --locked --no-sync to use the already resolved dependencies.

docs.title: Make the change
docs.text:
• Follow the architecture: CVM and B3 behavior belongs to its source; share only what is reusable.
  • Preserve public signatures, results, exceptions, and schemas. Breaking changes require an explicit decision and documented migration.
  • Use English names, code, comments, and commits. Add type annotations, use Google docstrings, and keep Ruff’s 79-character formatting.
  • Use _ for helpers confined to their module. A name shared between modules does not thereby become part of the public API. Keep mutable state private and expose operations when another module needs access.
  • Validate inputs and paths before writing. Preserve failure causes.
  • Update tests that prove the behavior and regression, and maintain product documentation in Portuguese and English.

Keep local drafts and working notes in docs/internal/. Git ignores this directory, and check-docs-contracts excludes it, including the English translation requirement. The MkDocs build also excludes it.

docs.title: Validate before the PR
docs.text:
uv run --locked --no-sync pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
uv run --locked --no-sync pytest

Default pytest selects deterministic tests. For coverage, markers, integrations, and local data, use the testing guide.

Change Additional validation Python code uv run --locked --no-sync mypy src --pretty Documentation uv run --locked --no-sync mkdocs build --strict Packaging uv build and release acceptance

Installed hooks distribute checks by cost:

Stage What it checks pre-commit Diff integrity, lockfile, syntax, formatting, lint, and contracts. commit-msg Conventional Commits format. pre-push Types, tests with coverage, and dependency auditing.

Canonical entries are in .pre-commit-config.yaml and pyproject.toml. To reproduce the complete push stage, run uv run --locked --no-sync pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --all-files. Diff gates inspect the index during commits; in CI, they inspect the cumulative range since the previous release. With no staged changes, diff-based gates can return SKIP even with --all-files; that is not approval of those gates. Local Gitleaks scans the index; CI also scans the complete checkout.

docs.title: Submit the PR
docs.text:
Review the diff and stage only the paths belonging to the change. Review automatic formatting before staging it.

git commit -m "fix: validate COTAHIST inputs before writing"

Describe the problem, final behavior, validation commands, and checks skipped or dependent on an external environment. For test deletions or consolidations, record the reason in .test-integrity-policy.json.

docs.title: Dependencies and internal tooling
docs.text:
Change dependencies deliberately with uv and review pyproject.toml and uv.lock. Do not edit the lockfile by hand. Hooks validate the resolution; updates and environment synchronization stay outside the commit path.

Agent projections in .agents/, .claude/, .codex/, and .opencode/ are maintained by the central-skills repository. Change the source and regenerate rather than editing generated files. harness-sync --check is a manual maintainer check; ordinary contributors do not need to install that tool.

To report vulnerabilities, follow the security policy.

docs.title: Optimization contract
docs.text:
The 2026-10-06 optimizations preserve public signatures, schema v2, output names, and market selection. All 32 fields, exact decimals, original bytes, provenance, order, and repeated occurrences remain verified before publication. CRC, source identity, replay, and complete final readback remain mandatory.

The current implementation validates readback coordinates with Arrow reductions within contiguous source segments. Required nulls are rejected first; a failing segment uses scalar diagnostics to preserve the first invalid row. Preflight keeps a validated container open through the 64 KiB content hash and strict scan. The worker validates a fresh container and hashes actual converted Arrow batches against the independent canonical preflight digest. Fixed binary framing reads Arrow buffers with their slice offsets; schema v2 and digest framing are unchanged.

docs.title: Refactor closure: 2026-10-20
docs.text:
The project owner accepted and closed the refactor on 2026-10-20. By explicit decision, the minimum 20% improvement target was removed from the acceptance requirements. The real gains demonstrated in the controlled 2026-10-19 comparison were accepted as sufficient for closure, together with the reviewed corrections and data-integrity and contract checks. No minimum performance percentage remains pending for this delivery.

Measured percentages remain bound to the 2026-10-19 snapshot. The supplemental final-version campaign confirmed data integrity, but its timing result remains inconclusive and establishes no new reliable percentage. Increased CPU and RSS remain documented as costs of the observed gains.

Original reports and samples remain preserved, including records of the unmet target while it was still required. This decision supersedes that requirement for closing the refactor.

docs.title: Current executor policy
docs.text:
HistoricalQuotesB3() defaults to process. Eligible fast extraction uses spawned workers with at least two resolved sources and two workers allowed by resource policy. slow, one source, or a one-worker limit use one thread worker. Daemons and callers without an importable main module or readable script fall back before submission; the logger records the reason and execution telemetry reports the actual backend. Pool and worker failures retain normal diagnostics and cleanup. Scripts must guard extraction with if __name__ == '__main__':. Explicit GDF_B3_EXECUTOR_BACKEND=thread and process remain supported.

The parser produces a canonical tuple directly and applies a layout-derived plan that reuses existing scalar validators. The digest uses constant tag and length tables. Final readback builds the same v2 framing with Arrow in bounded source segments. These tables do not store financial values. See the digest contract.

docs.title: Review follow-up: 2026-10-20
docs.text:
Preflight validates the path and captures the outer hash before opening the handle used for the content hash and scan. The final pathname check remains. A rename replacement in this window is therefore rejected during preflight, without producing a descriptor that mixes two files. Regressions cover TXT and ZIP, before and after opening, through the validator and facade, including handle cleanup and absence of publication.

The old _ProcessingModeConfig, the four resource properties on ProcessingModeEnumB3 without production consumers, and the uncalled validate_one_temp_file() helper were also removed. ResourcePolicyB3 continues to own the effective policy; removal of the exported properties was authorized.

The complete 72-observation comparison below belongs to the 2026-10-19 snapshot before this correction and was not repeated. Its historical gains and increased RSS and CPU remain bound to that version. The closure decision above accepts this evidence without requiring a minimum improvement percentage.

A supplemental final-version campaign on 2026-10-20 ran 18 complete extractions for one ZIP with 100,000 quotations: three alternating pairs for each of slow/thread, fast/thread and fast/process. Product snapshots, dependencies and input bytes were checked; all 32 fields and schema metadata matched, and two independent reconciliations checked 100,000 rows each. Timing was inconclusive: identical-version fast/process runs ranged from 12.44 to 18.77 s for the baseline and from 10.35 to 15.13 s for the candidate. The three paired reductions were 16.75%, 44.66% and 17.14%. Host variation prevents treating the nominal medians as new acceptance evidence. The supplemental report retains every sample, CPU/RSS measurements, provenance, independent audits and limitations. The last accepted controlled default comparison remains 15.41%.

Separate profiling located the largest preflight costs in canonical scalar field conversion and the independent scalar digest. A small framing experiment showed no measurable benefit and was discarded; product code is unchanged by this supplemental campaign.

docs.title: Complete API comparison: 2026-10-19
docs.text:
Three pairs per configuration ran sequentially in fresh Python processes, in alternating order, for 72 accepted observations. Environment: Python 3.13.9, PyArrow 23.0.1, Linux x86_64, eight logical CPUs and 7.55 GiB RAM. Both versions used the same locked dependencies, input bytes, all-market selection and four requested workers. One source and slow used one thread worker. Stored TXT inputs for four sources exceed the 64 MiB preflight threshold; ZIP inputs do not.

The timer includes construction, preflight, worker replay, full Parquet readback and transactional publication. Independent reconciliation has its own timer. All 32 fields, occurrences, order and complete schema metadata matched across versions and modes. Eight independent raw audits verified 2,400,000 rows in total.

Sources / quotations Input Mode / requested backend Baseline API (s) Candidate API (s) Reduction 1 / 100,000 TXT slow/thread 9.019 7.812 13.39% 1 / 100,000 TXT fast/thread 9.435 7.981 15.41% 1 / 100,000 TXT fast/process 9.496 8.057 15.15% 1 / 100,000 ZIP slow/thread 9.733 8.099 16.79% 1 / 100,000 ZIP fast/thread 9.604 8.133 15.32% 1 / 100,000 ZIP fast/process 9.563 8.124 15.04% 4 / 500,000 TXT slow/thread 46.889 39.480 15.80% 4 / 500,000 TXT fast/thread 46.113 37.736 18.17% 4 / 500,000 TXT fast/process 25.171 20.518 18.49% 4 / 500,000 ZIP slow/thread 48.029 40.048 16.62% 4 / 500,000 ZIP fast/thread 51.285 42.172 17.77% 4 / 500,000 ZIP fast/process 35.419 29.426 16.92%

Changing from the previous default (fast/thread) to the new eligible default (fast/process) reduced the median by 55.51% for TXT (46.113 to 20.518 s) and 42.62% for ZIP (51.285 to 29.426 s) with four sources. The one-source ZIP default comparison improved 15.41%. No matched mode/backend showed a time regression in that campaign.

Memory increased in the multi-source fast profiles: 24.31% for threads/TXT, 37.29% for threads/ZIP, and 24.16% for processes in both formats. Separate instrumentation observed up to four concurrent digest updates, batches bounded to 25,000 rows, and worker Arrow high-water allocation rising from 64.0 to 106.5 MiB. After each source, only 17,536 Arrow bytes remained for constant prefix tables; RSS also includes allocator reservations. These observations locate the additional framing buffers and preserve the existing buffering limits.

The backend switch itself adds 46.78% aggregate RSS for TXT and 47.16% for ZIP, comparing candidate threads with candidate processes. Including both code and backend changes, median RSS moves from 676.12 to 1,233.73 MiB for TXT and 613.48 to 1,239.46 MiB for ZIP. Total API CPU moves from 50.06 to 72.18 s and 53.71 to 60.09 s, respectively. Lower elapsed time therefore has a CPU and memory cost. Aggregate RSS can count shared pages more than once. RSS sampling covers the native runner’s API and bounded post-API comparison; raw audits are separate.

The caller-provided 2023 ZIP separately passed both modes: 2,257,424 quotations per mode, all 32 fields independently reconciled, exact ordered parity and no remaining workers. Its SHA-256 is ad1603788d78aaa1de806498572277f1d9443f88ae116452751b5800cb23523e. This campaign overlapped quality gates and provides integrity evidence.

Synthetic workload Combined input SHA-256 1-100000-txt 253a8e7e8448b25b8293cef8d130a3821a161682ca15dc17ffe1e9e6ab0c0646 1-100000-zip 410e7200bbb04bb7b4af8a75164d34dd8153ed7203ccf3247f46dea37697d9e0 4-500000-txt 3847bb6d8f4bac24449f623c1255acbd80625b4f8b98f0a3dcd111639321ab1d 4-500000-zip b618ff2947498c82d022c7fb2ffe0c0d9016f60bbaafef885f36cd80f4ddd366

The comparison and phase metrics link every raw sample. Provenance binds product/support hashes, dependencies and individual inputs. Memory investigation, independent audits, annual reconciliation and the env-unset default smoke are retained separately. The validation report records gate results and the criteria in force at the time of the campaign; the closure above removes the percentage requirement. Instrumented single-ZIP counts changed from 4 to 2 complete CRC scans and 7 to 5 decompressions; hash-pass record contexts changed from 4 to 0 on a two-quotation fixture, with every archive closed.

The synthetic corpus has one trading day per year, market 010 and balanced sources. Three observations per version/configuration and warm OS file caches limit precision and extrapolation. These are measured workloads, not a throughput guarantee for another machine or the complete annual corpus.

uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/benchmark_ingestion.py \
  --scenario b3_multi_4x25k --rows 500000 --source-count 4 --worker-limit 4 \
  --b3-input-format zip --backend process --processing-mode fast --repeats 3 \
  --output .benchmarks/b3-processing-zip.json

The native CLI defaults to TXT and selects stocks; the controlled comparison used todos through its operation seam. The archived coordinator preserves that selection and alternates distinct snapshots. The 2026-10-06 sections below are historical measurements of earlier versions and campaigns.

docs.title: Parser and final readback: distinct-version comparison
docs.text:
Three pairs per mode processed the same 500,000 records across four sources, in alternating fresh Python processes. Environment: Python 3.13.9, PyArrow 23.0.1, Linux x86_64, eight CPUs, with other host processes running. The requested backend was thread; slow retained one worker.

Mode Starting median Optimized median Time reduction CPU reduction fast 84.148 s 57.901 s 31.19% 29.57% slow 66.477 s 47.089 s 29.16% 28.63%

Time includes preflight, workers, merge, and complete final readback. The subsequent independent audit is outside this timer. Every pair produced byte-identical Parquets. The synthetic expectation covers business fields; internal 32-field readback and physical equality also cover provenance. Official reconciliation is a separate additional proof.

Median aggregate RSS for fast remained approximately stable: 640.86 to 642.42 MiB. For slow, it decreased from 492.79 to 407.54 MiB. Final readback times went from 21.576 to 6.819 s for fast and from 16.486 to 5.260 s for slow.

The raw report retains every sample, load, swap, input checksum, and module hash. These numbers describe this workload and host; they are neither guaranteed throughput nor a projection for the 27 official years.

docs.title: Final integrated version: repeated comparison
docs.text:
The final integration repeated three pairs per mode using the same thread configuration, four sources, and 500,000 records. Other applications and the real-data opt-in suite were active. Both versions had the same effective source and worker counts within every pair.

Mode Starting median Integrated median Time reduction CPU reduction fast 96.363 s 63.489 s 34.11% 29.34% slow 76.374 s 50.380 s 34.04% 33.85%

All six pairs improved wall time and CPU, and all 12 processes produced identical Parquets within their pairs. Median aggregate RSS went from 679.44 to 665.44 MiB in fast and from 453.68 to 405.96 MiB in slow.

The integrated version report preserves every sample and the compared source hashes. Host variation limits the precision of the observed improvement; this measurement does not establish a throughput guarantee for the complete annual corpus.

docs.title: Complete 2000–2026 acceptance
docs.text:
The final acceptance processed all 27 supplied annual sources, spanning 2000-01-03 through 2026-09-02, with the default thread backend and four requested workers. Each mode read, selected, wrote, and verified 22,305,860 quotations, without exclusions or missing years. Independent reconciliation checked all 32 fields and every row’s order. Physical Parquets matched between modes and the historical acceptance.

The 27 frozen-manifest checksums also passed, as did preservation of the previous 20 fields in 22,303,577 quotations and all 2,283 block-lot trades, covering 345 distinct codes and an exact decimal volume total of 57,359,085,637.97. Cleanup left no active processes or temporary artifacts.

Mode API in earlier campaign API in current campaign Observed reduction fast 3,895.088 s (64m55s) 2,989.776 s (49m50s) 23.24% slow 3,350.505 s (55m51s) 2,297.342 s (38m17s) 31.43%

Each campaign ran one complete extraction per mode. Other machine processes remained active, but the campaigns ran on different days and machine loads. These percentages are historical observations, not a controlled causal estimate or full-corpus median. The repeated 500,000-row comparison has its own methodology and results, described above.

API times include preparation, extraction, merge, and full readback before publication. The entire current campaign took 12,861.443 s, approximately 3h34m, including external audits, parity, and cleanup. This total measures complete acceptance and does not replace the API processing timer.

The report states its code binding: the full campaign retained a 323-file snapshot; a later correction affects only the process-preflight waiter, and another change synchronizes a cancellation test. The other 321 files and the rest of that module’s AST remained identical. thread and slow do not call the corrected waiter. The process correction passed official 2002–2003 acceptance again on a snapshot matching all 112 current product modules. Local gates covered the current code and tests on all three supported Python versions.

docs.title: Concurrent preflight
docs.text:
The 2026-10-06 campaign used the then-default thread backend. Under the current process default or explicit process selection, fast admits concurrent preflight only in a compatible spawn context with at least two workers allowed by resource policy and at least 64 MiB of total stored annual candidate sizes. This includes coexisting ZIP and TXT inputs, because both require validation. slow, one source, one worker, or a smaller workload retain serial preflight.

The threshold is conservative and measures stored bytes, not quotation count or uncompressed size. Compression, source balance, CPUs, and memory affect results. Size-read failures are deferred to canonical serial validation, which preserves diagnostic order.

In three additional pairs, both sides used process extraction with 500,000 records across four sources. Concurrent preflight reduced the median from 34.294 to 25.514 s: 25.60% less time. Median total CPU increased from 67.295 to 81.940 s. This trades additional CPU for lower wall time; it does not represent less computational work.

The preflight report records every sample, aggregate RSS, CPU, and compared version. All three pairs produced the same Parquet. The implementation preserves source and first-error order, typed causes, and worker shutdown before completing cancellation or failure. Polling retrieves results completed at the wait boundary and preserves a TimeoutError produced by the worker itself.

An additional official acceptance used 2002-2003 ZIPs identical to the originals and coexisting equivalent TXT files, totaling 77.69 MiB of candidates above the threshold. With process requested, both modes independently reconciled all 32 fields of 278,085 quotations each, without exclusions or duplication from equivalent representations. Ordered rows and physical Parquets matched between modes; no workers or temporary artifacts remained after cleanup. This case proves integrity, not a performance improvement.

mkdir -p .benchmarks
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/benchmark_ingestion.py \
  --scenario b3_multi_4x25k --rows 500000 --source-count 4 --worker-limit 4 \
  --backend process --processing-mode fast --repeats 3 \
  --output .benchmarks/b3-process-500k.json

docs.title: Accepting another change
docs.text:
The implementation passed local pre-push on Python 3.12.3, 3.13.9, and 3.14.0. Each environment ran 2,330 deterministic tests and 200 validation-executor tests. Product coverage, including branches, was 91.22%, 91.22%, and 91.12%, respectively; executor coverage was 91.12% on all three. The audit of 116 locked dependencies also passed. These are local results; remote CI execution and publication are separate steps.

  1. Freeze distinct baseline and candidate versions with product, support, and input hashes. Keep dependencies, selection, and resources identical within pairs.
  2. Alternate fresh-process order, retain every sample, and measure the complete operation. CPU, aggregate RSS, and external audits have separate metrics.
  3. Require equality of every value and occurrence, plus corruption, exclusion, zero-selected-source, and cancellation tests.
  4. Reconcile the supplied official corpus in both modes on the final version; pass tests, hooks, and documentation checks before accepting the change.

Rust can be evaluated as a batch kernel if a material bottleneck remains after these changes. That decision requires additional complete-operation benefit, exact equivalence, and distribution compatible with supported Python versions. An isolated microbenchmark does not justify changing the library’s language.

docs.title: Logging System
docs.text: Complete technical reference covering the advanced centralized logging infrastructure implemented across Global-Data-Finance.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Global-Data-Finance incorporates a professional centralized logging subsystem designed specifically for high-throughput library distribution:

  • ✅ Lazy Initialization: Logging remains silently disabled by default (respecting standard Python library citizenship practices)
  • ✅ Multi-Target Handlers: Configurable simultaneous routing to console outputs and filesystem files
  • ✅ Granular Level Filtering: Full support for standard severity thresholds (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL)
  • ✅ Performance Benchmarking: Integrated timing context managers designed to capture operation latencies automatically
  • ✅ Structured Metadata Binding: Context-aware log emission supporting structured parameter propagation
  • ✅ Environment Override Compatibility: Runtime configuration via confirmed OS environment variables

docs.title: Initial State and Isolation
docs.text:
Importing the library does not configure the application root logger or attach visible output handlers. The globaldatafinance logger starts with a NullHandler and propagate=False, so events remain quiet until the consumer explicitly calls setup_logging(). Configuration affects only this logger hierarchy.

LoggingSettings accepts only its documented fields: level, format, log_file, and detailed_format. Extra fields, including the removed structured field, raise ValidationError.

Supported environment variables are DATAFIN_LOG_LEVEL, DATAFIN_LOG_FORMAT, DATAFIN_LOG_FILE, and DATAFIN_LOG_DETAILED_FORMAT. DATAFIN_LOG_LOG_FILE is also accepted for compatibility with the field-derived name. Any other DATAFIN_LOG_* variable, including DATAFIN_LOG_STRUCTURED, raises ValidationError when LoggingSettings() is created.

The formatter performs best-effort redaction for common URL parameters and sensitive context fields such as token, password, authorization, and cookie. It also covers URL parameters key, code, and state, and quoted sensitive fields in JSON text, including formatted exceptions. URL authority credentials (https://<userinfo>@host/) become [REDACTED]@, preserving the host, path, and public parameters. The same protection covers protocol-relative authorities (//user:password@host/). This does not replace the consumer’s responsibility: secrets must not be passed in messages, exceptions, or logging context.

Compound names with _ or -, such as id_token and auth_token, receive the same protection in URLs, serialized messages, and context fields. URL parameter names are decoded before identifying sensitive fields; the original parameter spelling and public values are preserved.

log_file must point to a consumer-approved application path. Before creating directories or the file, setup_logging() rejects system roots, protected directories, and untrusted UNC destinations using the same path-safety policy as the data facades. Use an application-owned directory or /tmp for local diagnostics.

docs.title: Reconfiguration and Rollback
docs.text:
setup_logging() builds and configures every candidate handler before touching the package logger. On success, only library-managed handlers are replaced; external handlers are preserved. If file creation or the handler swap fails, the candidates are closed and the previous level, propagation setting, and handlers are restored.

This lets applications reconfigure library logging without losing the active configuration:

from globaldatafinance.core.logging_config import LoggingSettings, setup_logging

setup_logging(LoggingSettings(level="INFO"))
setup_logging(LoggingSettings(level="DEBUG", log_file="app-debug.log"))

docs.title: Primary Subsystem Components
docs.text:
src/core/logging_config.py
├── setup_logging()           # Subsystem configuration entrypoint
├── get_logger()              # Module logger registry retrieval
├── log_execution_time()      # Latency tracking performance context manager
├── log_with_context()        # Structured key-value event logger
├── LoggingSettings           # Pydantic configuration container
├── StructuredFormatter       # Custom formatting layout engine
└── ContextFilter             # Metadata enrichment logging filter

docs.title: 1. Enable Library Logging
docs.text:
In accordance with Python best practices for dependency distributions, logging is disabled by default. To activate event reporting:

from globaldatafinance.core.logging_config import LoggingSettings, setup_logging

# Activate logging across the library hierarchy at severity INFO
setup_logging(LoggingSettings(level="INFO"))

docs.title: 2. Retrieve a Module Logger Instance
docs.text:
The examples use a child of globaldatafinance to receive the handlers configured above. Configure application loggers with application-owned handlers separately.

from globaldatafinance.core.logging_config import get_logger

logger = get_logger("globaldatafinance.example")
logger.info("Processing job started")
logger.debug("Detailed debug tracing")
logger.warning("Potential configuration warning")
logger.error("Exception encountered during operational step")

docs.title: 3. Structured Context Logging
docs.text:
logger.info(
    "Dataset normalization completed",
    extra={
        "file_target": "dfp_cia_aberta_2023.csv",
        "records": 1000,
        "elapsed_ms": 250
    }
)

Console Output:

2025-11-25 17:30:00 | INFO     | my_pipeline_module | Dataset normalization completed | file_target=dfp_cia_aberta_2023.csv | records=1000 | elapsed_ms=250

docs.title: Severity Level Thresholds
docs.text: Severity Level Operational Scope Typical Example Event DEBUG Deep diagnostic execution traces Variable parameter inspections, worker loop steps INFO Standard operational lifecycle metrics “Download initiated”, “Parquet file persisted” WARNING Recoverable anomalies or degradations “Target archive exists, skipping”, “Timeout retry” ERROR Non-fatal operation exceptions “Failed downloading individual DFP table slice” CRITICAL Severe failures impacting overall runtime “Storage exhaustion detected”, “Out of memory”

docs.title: Programmatic Configuration
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.core.logging_config import LoggingSettings, setup_logging

# Standard activation
setup_logging(LoggingSettings(level="INFO"))

# Route logging outputs directly to a filesystem log destination
setup_logging(
    LoggingSettings(
        level="DEBUG",
        log_file="/tmp/datafinance/execution.log",
    )
)

# Enable detailed formatting (includes precise line numbers and symbol signatures)
setup_logging(
    LoggingSettings(
        level="DEBUG",
        detailed_format=True,
    )
)

docs.title: Environment Variable Configuration
docs.text:
Confirmed environment configuration parameter names:

# Define threshold level
export DATAFIN_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG

# Direct logging output to file destination
export DATAFIN_LOG_FILE=/tmp/datafin.log

# Enable detailed structural reporting
export DATAFIN_LOG_DETAILED_FORMAT=true

Unknown DATAFIN_LOG_* variables are rejected so removed or misspelled options cannot appear to have been applied.

from globaldatafinance.core.logging_config import setup_logging

# Ingest settings directly from environment declarations (default LoggingSettings snapshot)
setup_logging()

docs.title: Performance Timing & Latency Profiling
docs.text:
Leverage the automated log_execution_time() context manager to track operational durations:

from globaldatafinance.core.logging_config import log_execution_time, get_logger

logger = get_logger("globaldatafinance.example")

with log_execution_time(logger, "Parse COTAHIST ZIP archive", file_target="COTAHIST_A2023.ZIP"):
    parse_file("COTAHIST_A2023.ZIP")

Console Output:

Starting: Parse COTAHIST ZIP archive | operation=Parse COTAHIST ZIP archive | file_target=COTAHIST_A2023.ZIP
Completed: Parse COTAHIST ZIP archive | operation=Parse COTAHIST ZIP archive | elapsed_seconds=2.45 | file_target=COTAHIST_A2023.ZIP

Upon encountering runtime failures:

Failed: Parse COTAHIST ZIP archive | operation=Parse COTAHIST ZIP archive | elapsed_seconds=1.23 | error=File not found | file_target=COTAHIST_A2023.ZIP

docs.title: Contextual Event Reporting
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.core.logging_config import log_with_context, get_logger

# my_processing_pipeline.py
from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM

    LoggingSettings,
    get_logger,
    log_execution_time,
    setup_logging,
)

setup_logging(LoggingSettings(level="INFO"))

def process_financial_filings():
    logger.info("Starting filing processing workflow")

        cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM()
        cvm.download(
            destination_path="/data/cvm",

            initial_year=2023

Appends exact module line numbering and caller function terminology:

docs.title: 1. Choose a name within the configured logger hierarchy
docs.text:
Inside library modules, use get_logger(__name__): those names already start with globaldatafinance. In applications, a name such as the example below inherits the library handlers; names outside that hierarchy need their own configuration.

logger = get_logger("globaldatafinance.example")

docs.title: 2. Match Severity Levels Accurately to Impact
docs.text:
# ✅ Correct usage
logger.debug("Inspected iteration state variable: %s", value)
logger.info("Extraction loop commenced")
logger.warning("Archive verification checksum bypassed")
logger.error("Failed decompressing archive file", exc_info=True)

# ❌ Discouraged usage
logger.info("Loop index variable: %s", value)  # Should utilize DEBUG
logger.error("Completed extraction step")      # Should utilize INFO

docs.title: 3. Rely on Structured Metadata Dictionaries
docs.text:
# ✅ Correct - explicit structured field assignment
logger.info(
    "Dataframe normalized",
    extra={"file_target": "cotahist.parquet", "size_mb": 10.5}
)

# ❌ Discouraged - mixing unparseable values within string interpolation
logger.info(f"File cotahist.parquet processed with size: 10.5 MB")

docs.title: 4. Harness Context Managers for Latency Profiling
docs.text:
# ✅ Correct - automated exception tracking and duration timing
with log_execution_time(logger, "Download Workflow"):
    time.sleep(1)

# ❌ Discouraged - manual timer bookkeeping
start = time.time()
time.sleep(1)
logger.info(f"Execution took {time.time() - start} seconds")

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
To audit the complete matrix without relying on implicit environment configuration, run the opt-in executor with every path supplied explicitly. Keep the report and temporary artifacts outside the repository:

uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/real_validation.py \
  --source all \
  --cotahist-path /external/path/COTAHIST \
  --cvm-output /tmp/globaldatafinance-cvm-output \
  --report /tmp/globaldatafinance-real-validation/first-run \
  --timeout 3600

--timeout limits each case, including extraction and independent reconciliation. The default is 60 seconds, which can be insufficient even for a single year’s fast/slow parity checks. For annual validation, use an explicit limit such as --timeout 1200 and adjust it to the corpus and environment; that value does not guarantee a completion time. The executor classifies an exceeded limit as external_failure and terminates the case process. The manifest records the limit in campaign.timeoutSeconds.

docs.title: Scope and validation
docs.text:
all creates COTAHIST cases for every local catalog year in the requested range (or every available year when the range is omitted) and valid combinations in the seven CVM document windows, including IPE since 2003. A missing year in the requested range fails the campaign before processing. With --cotahist-mode all, every year gets a fast proof and a complete fast/slow parity; the campaign also includes complete multi-year parity over the full range. Preparation checks names, containers, years, and hashes and applies ZIP precedence. Coexisting ZIP/TXT representations of one year still require identical complete contents. Every quotation is validated by the API before publication and by independent reconciliation; preparing the manifest does not repeat that complete parsing pass. Invalid containers prevent campaign creation; invalid quotation fields produce a failed case without API publication. COTAHIST is never downloaded by the executor. The CVM matrix contacts only the official URLs defined explicitly in code and classifies HTTP 404/410 as not_published, network unavailability as external_failure, and invalid content or processing failures as failed.

For CVM, --verify-cvm-catalog writes cvm-catalog.json with all published years and selection omissions. If a published year of the selected documents is outside the matrix, the campaign stops with exit code 1; omit this option for intentionally partial campaigns. Every CSV is reconciled field by field by an independent parser, including headers, ordering, empty fields, and counts. Results record hashes for every ZIP member, attachments, and compared fields. For complete CVM history, use --initial-year 2003 --document all; ZIPs the facade retains in the isolated workspace are removed by the executor only after evidence is persisted, along with other campaign artifacts.

docs.title: Historical baseline and monitoring
docs.text:
By default, COTAHIST campaigns reconcile caller-provided inputs against the checksums frozen in that run’s own manifest. Selecting 2000–2026 does not implicitly require the historical corpus used in the initial audit. To require that specific corpus, its 27 checksums, and historical metrics, explicitly select multi-year parity with --cotahist-frozen-baseline:

uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/real_validation.py \
  --source cotahist --cotahist-path /external/path/COTAHIST \
  --initial-year 2000 --last-year 2026 --cotahist-mode all \
  --cotahist-frozen-baseline --case cotahist-multi-parity-2000-2026 \
  --report /external/path/cotahist-historical-acceptance --timeout 43200 --progress

--progress writes preparation, case start/results, and updates every 30 seconds while the worker is active to stderr. Stdout retains the final JSON summary. Extraction, Parquet validation, and reconciliation stages appear in the individual case log. Activity updates are not row progress and do not prove the current stage is free of blocking. Full campaigns read every quotation in both modes and can take hours; do not launch a second campaign to replace one that is still active.

--cotahist-frozen-baseline requires the complete range and selection of the multi-year case. The case persists this intent as frozenBaseline, preserved by --resume; resume cannot switch a generic campaign to historical acceptance. Use a new report directory to change this selection. Without --resume, the CLI rejects directories with previous campaign evidence and preserves their files. Output paths are resolved consistently, including a symlink in directory ancestry; destination containment and the exactly-one-Parquet requirement remain mandatory.

In the COTAHIST campaign, extraction-reported DiskFullError and PathPermissionError are external_failure; original diagnostics remain in the report. Invalid content and integrity mismatches remain failed.

docs.title: Reports and resuming
docs.text: Each case runs in an isolated process. The directory supplied to --report contains manifest.json, one current result per case in results.jsonl, summary.json, individual logs, and artifact evidence. Use --resume --report <same-directory> to rerun only external_failure cases or cases that have not been classified; functional results and not_published cases are preserved. Persisted results are caller-owned evidence, not a signed attestation: use --resume only with a trusted report directory when a pass/fail conclusion must serve as evidence. Before resuming, every COTAHIST input is compared with the manifest inputSizeBytes and inputSha256. A shared path is hashed once; any drift raises ReportFormatError, does not rerun or overwrite old results, and requires a new campaign. The COTAHIST caseId, year, mode, and input must also agree with the current catalog. CVM resume first validates the persisted campaign.cvmOutput with the external-destination policy, then rebuilds cases from the official document/year matrix: persisted fields, including inputPath, url, and outputRoot, must match both the rebuilt case and the campaign destination before a worker starts. A tampered outputRoot fails before mkdir, mkdtemp, a worker, or an HTTP client. The CVM probe uses only the canonical HTTPS endpoint, does not follow redirects, and never persists a preflight body. The compressed-archive byte limit is enforced from both Content-Length and the public-facade stream; the recorded hash is taken from the ZIP immediately before that facade extracts it. --report and --cvm-output pass through the sensitive-destination policy before any directory is created; system roots, protected directories, relative Windows drives, and untrusted UNC paths are rejected, while /tmp and an explicitly allowed UNC root can be used under the shared policy. Exit code 0 is reserved for a fully executed matrix with no functional failures, external failures, unexecuted combinations, or orphan processes; 1 indicates a functional failure, and 2 indicates an external dependency, timeout, incomplete execution, or orphan process. I/O, report-format, security, or campaign configuration failures handled as invalid_campaign return 3. Argument syntax errors return 2 through argparse.

docs.title: Release Acceptance
docs.text: Acceptance gathers evidence for the same candidate commit before publication. The canonical testing, transactional publication, HTTP and retry, and logging contracts remain in their owner documents.

docs.title: Required validation
docs.text:
Environment Execution Linux, Python 3.12/3.13/3.14 Complete deterministic suite, gates, product coverage, and real-validation executor coverage. Windows/macOS, Python 3.12/3.13/3.14 Native lock, recovery, ZIP, HTTP, retry, logging, CVM, and B3 regressions. Linux, Python 3.13 Complete process-crash and storage-failure campaign across eight shards. Distributions Wheel/sdist inspection and local CVM/B3 flows from independent installations.

Both aggregate coverage floors remain 85%, including branches. The native suite is focused; required cases must execute and pass. Windows error 1314 when creating symlinks may skip only that alias case. It cannot waive publication or recovery executions.

The tests.support.release_evidence plugin records actual pytest outcomes and rejects empty, entirely skipped, unfinished, or missing critical behavior. Artifacts include JUnit, environment versions, and the candidate commit.

docs.title: Fault campaign
docs.text:
The campaign uses temporary directories, caller files, and small valid Parquet payloads. It covers fresh/existing destinations and hard-link/copy backups. Every operation is interrupted before and after execution; resulting states receive further crashes during recovery. Three recovery attempts must retain one complete old or new batch, according to the journal, without changing caller files or leaving residues with established ownership.

It also injects ENOSPC/EIO, partial writes, persistent rollback failures, and interrupted child cleanup. Each recovery phase receives storage failures. The empty Windows guard file is persistent by contract and is not residue.

Run the complete local campaign:

GDF_PUBLICATION_REPORT_DIR=.cache/publication-campaign/reports \
uv run --locked --no-sync pytest \
  tests/macro_infra/test_publication_fault_campaign.py \
  -m "integration and slow" --no-cov

To partition it, set GDF_PUBLICATION_SHARDS=8 and execute each GDF_PUBLICATION_SHARD index from 0 through 7, retaining reports together. These variables configure test tooling rather than library runtime settings. The complete campaign uses Linux processes; native suites use portable checkpoints. Normal pytest collection does not start the slow campaign.

The verifier requires all four scenarios and every shard, derives expected cases from operation traces, and rejects missing executions:

uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/check_release_evidence.py \
  .cache/publication-campaign/reports --shards 8

Use --shards 1 when verifying an unpartitioned campaign. Processes execute real operations and terminate through os._exit; storage faults are injected at the I/O boundary without filling the host disk.

docs.title: Packages and publication
docs.text:
After uv build, inspect metadata, safety modules, and both distribution digests:

uv run --locked --no-sync python -m scripts.check_distributions dist

The release workflow requires the stable tag version through --expected-version. Untagged local builds may have development versions. Each distribution receives its own installation, and smoke checks run with Python -I outside the checkout. They verify the loaded installation, public exports, local CVM extraction, and ZIP/TXT B3 extraction in fast/slow modes.

The release-acceptance job requires quality, security, package checks, every native environment, the complete campaign, coverage, and matching downloaded artifact digests. A failed prerequisite produces a pending report and blocks publication. Dry-run performs these checks without uploading to PyPI.

docs.title: Evidence and limitations
docs.text:
Acceptance and test artifacts remain available in the CI run for at least 30 days. Reports identify SHA, version, hashes, and execution URL, separating passed, failed, skipped, and external_failure. Acceptance uses evidence produced by CI, without depending on versioned planning documents or review records in the repository. Unavailable native environments or required executions keep acceptance pending.

Process-crash recovery does not establish universal power-loss durability or simultaneous batch visibility during commit. The HTTP budget does not measure total process memory. Ownership and the outer CVM lock contracts remain active.

docs.title: Resource Monitoring
docs.text: Resource measurements, limits, and admission helpers used by Global-Data-Finance.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
ResourceMonitor measures CPU and memory and offers operations to its caller:

  • A singleton constructor for shared use, or create_isolated() for isolation.
  • Manual helpers to size workers and batches and wait for resources.
  • States and a circuit breaker consulted by the flow using the monitor.
  • Garbage collection on warning when enabled in the limits.

A reported state does not automatically resize an operation already running.

docs.title: Resource Saturation States
docs.text:
State Description Action HEALTHY Memory and CPU below warning thresholds No action required WARNING Memory or CPU warning threshold reached Considers GC when enabled CRITICAL Critical threshold reached or resource telemetry failed Caller decides how to reduce work EXHAUSTED Memory exhaustion threshold reached, insufficient free memory, or circuit breaker still active Activates the circuit breaker when enabled

Thresholds are configurable through ResourceLimits; the example below shows the defaults. High CPU alone reaches CRITICAL.

docs.title: Configuring ResourceLimits
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.core import ResourceLimits

limits = ResourceLimits(
    memory_warning_threshold=70.0,      # RAM % threshold triggering WARNING state
    memory_critical_threshold=85.0,     # RAM % threshold triggering CRITICAL state
    memory_exhausted_threshold=95.0,    # RAM % threshold triggering EXHAUSTED state
    cpu_warning_threshold=80.0,         # CPU % threshold triggering WARNING state
    cpu_critical_threshold=90.0,        # CPU % threshold triggering CRITICAL state
    min_free_memory_mb=100,             # Absolute minimum available RAM allowance (MB)
    auto_gc_on_warning=True,            # Automatically fire garbage collector on WARNING
    circuit_breaker_cooldown_seconds=10,# Mandatory rest timeout during breaker trips
    circuit_breaker_enabled=True        # Enable hardware circuit breaker protection
)

docs.title: Instantiate Singleton Monitor
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.core import ResourceLimits, ResourceMonitor

# The first initialization defines the active limits.
limits = ResourceLimits(memory_warning_threshold=60.0)
monitor = ResourceMonitor(limits)
# Later calls return the same object and do not replace its limits.
same_monitor = ResourceMonitor(ResourceLimits(memory_warning_threshold=50.0))
assert same_monitor is monitor
assert monitor.limits.memory_warning_threshold == 60.0

docs.title: Inspect Current Resource State
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.core import ResourceMonitor

monitor = ResourceMonitor()
state = monitor.check_resources()
print(f"Current telemetry assessment: {state}")  # Returns HEALTHY, WARNING, CRITICAL, or EXHAUSTED

docs.title: Calculate Safe Worker Concurrency
docs.text:
# Derive permissible concurrent worker allocation matching available memory and cpu room
safe_workers = monitor.get_safe_worker_count(max_workers=16)
print(f"Allocating {safe_workers} worker threads")

docs.title: Calculate Safe Batch Size
docs.text:
# Dynamically scale data ingestion batch chunking limits
safe_batch = monitor.get_safe_batch_size(desired_batch_size=10000)
print(f"Optimal adjusted batch size: {safe_batch}")

docs.title: Pause Until Resources Free Up
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.core import ResourceMonitor, ResourceState

monitor = ResourceMonitor()
success = monitor.wait_for_resources(
    required_state=ResourceState.WARNING,
    timeout_seconds=60
)

if success:
    print("✓ Resource availability restored within operating boundaries")
else:
    print("⚠️ Timeout exceeded awaiting resource release")

docs.title: Query Current Process RAM Footprint
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.core import ResourceMonitor

monitor = ResourceMonitor()
memory_mb = monitor.get_process_memory_mb()
print(f"Active process consuming: {memory_mb:.2f} MB")

get_process_memory_mb() uses 0.0 as a sentinel when psutil cannot read telemetry; it is not a real zero-usage measurement. A known telemetry failure in check_resources() produces ResourceState.CRITICAL.

docs.title: Source-Specific Policy
docs.text:
The CVM flow uses a static concurrency semaphore in CvmDownloadAdapter; it does not query ResourceMonitor to resize workers during downloads. The limit is set by max_concurrent when the adapter is constructed.

ResourcePolicyB3 creates an isolated monitor, without warning GC or CPU utilization as a trigger. fast bounds workers by source count, CPU count, available RAM, and GDF_B3_WORKER_LIMIT (default 4); slow uses one worker. Admission waits under critical memory and fails on exhaustion or timeout. The singleton’s manual helpers do not resize B3 batches.

docs.title: Practical Standalone Scripting
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.core import ResourceMonitor, ResourceState

monitor = ResourceMonitor()

# Verify operational headroom prior to running intensive data operations
state = monitor.check_resources()

if state == ResourceState.EXHAUSTED:
    print("System entering EXHAUSTED capacity state! Awaiting cooldown...")
    if not monitor.wait_for_resources(timeout_seconds=120):
        raise TimeoutError("Resources remain unavailable")

# Retrieve safe concurrent worker threshold
workers = monitor.get_safe_worker_count(max_workers=16)
process_data(workers=workers)

# Track memory footprint
memory = monitor.get_process_memory_mb()
print(f"Final runtime consumption: {memory:.2f} MB")

docs.title: External Dependencies
docs.text:
The monitoring module utilizes psutil to query OS-level process and system metrics. The psutil package is a mandatory core dependency of globaldatafinance and is installed automatically.

If the installation is incomplete or the module cannot be loaded, importing the package fails explicitly. There is no degraded mode that reports ResourceState.HEALTHY without telemetry, because that result could admit work without the memory and CPU safety limits.

docs.title: Retry Strategy
docs.text: Retry classification and exponential backoff used by Global-Data-Finance.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: RetryStrategy classifies exceptions by type and message and calculates exponential backoff with jitter. The caller decides when to repeat an operation.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Exception classification with a message-keyword fallback.
  • Exponential backoff with multiplicative jitter and a configurable cap.
  • Explicit exclusions for PathPermissionError, DiskFullError, and ValueError.

docs.title: Always Retryable Exceptions
docs.text:
• NetworkError - Connection drops or socket disruptions
  • DownloadTimeoutError - CVM download timeout failures

docs.title: Keyword-Based Exception Matchers
docs.text:
For any other non-excluded exception, the strategy searches its lowercased message for these keywords:

  • "timeout"
  • "connection refused"
  • "connection reset"
  • "connection aborted"
  • "temporarily"
  • "unavailable"
  • "try again"

This fallback also accepts a generic exception, such as Exception("Operation timeout occurred"). Its message does not prove the failure is transient. For manual retry, use idempotent operations or apply your own classification before repeating a state change.

docs.title: Never Retryable (Fail-Fast) Exceptions
docs.text:
• PathPermissionError - File system authorization blocks
  • DiskFullError - Local volume capacity exhaustion
  • ValueError - Validation error

docs.title: HTTP Statuses in CVM Downloads
docs.text: The CVM adapter classifies HTTP statuses before translating failures into NetworkError. Only 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 allow retries. Other statuses, including 403, 404, and 410, end the attempt without additional backoff. Diagnostics retain the original status. Status selection takes precedence over keywords in the message or URL; timeouts and connection failures continue to use the shared strategy.

docs.title: HTTP Limits and Redirects
docs.text:
The download byte limit requires Accept-Encoding: identity. Responses with other HTTP content encodings are rejected before reading, including redirect responses; internal ZIP compression remains supported and is checked against extraction limits. The byte counter also limits intermediate redirect bodies without Content-Length. Calls to the shared adapter without a byte limit retain existing HTTP content decoding.

Downloads with HTTP identity encoding compare received bytes with the valid Content-Length from that same GET response. A mismatch rejects and removes only the attempt’s staging file; CVM applies its transport-failure retry policy. Missing or invalid metadata does not bypass byte limits or complete ZIP validation. CVM does not issue HEAD after downloading, avoiding comparisons between different representations when the source republishes a file.

HEAD also requests identity and closes bodies without reading or decoding, including redirect bodies. The Content-Length header is preserved as resource metadata; its value is not treated as a HEAD body size.

In the shared HTTP adapter, redirects changing scheme, host, or port retain only Accept, Accept-Encoding, Accept-Language, Connection, Host, and User-Agent. Credentials and custom headers are confined to the initial origin. CVM header configuration supplies User-Agent when provided.

docs.title: Instantiate Custom Strategy
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.core.utils.retry_strategy import RetryStrategy

strategy = RetryStrategy(
    initial_backoff=1.0,    # Base starting backoff delay (in seconds)
    max_backoff=60.0,       # Maximum delay ceiling (in seconds)
    multiplier=2.0          # Exponential multiplier step rate
)

docs.title: Validate Exception Eligibility
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.macro_exceptions import NetworkError

try:
    download_file()
except Exception as exc:
    if strategy.is_retryable(exc):
        print("✓ Transient network failure detected, scheduling retry")
    else:
        print("✗ Non-retryable exception encountered, aborting immediately")
        raise

docs.title: Compute Back-off Durations
docs.text:
# Derive staggered delay schedules across sequential attempts
for retry_count in range(3):
    backoff = strategy.calculate_backoff(retry_count)
    print(f"Attempt {retry_count + 1} scheduling delay: {backoff} seconds")

Sample Estimated Output (initial=1.0, multiplier=2.0 with bounded multiplicative jitter [0.5, 1.5]):

Attempt 1 scheduling delay: ~1.0 seconds (e.g. 0.92s)
Attempt 2 scheduling delay: ~2.0 seconds (e.g. 2.15s)
Attempt 3 scheduling delay: ~4.0 seconds (e.g. 3.80s)

Note: The calculate_backoff method applies bounded multiplicative jitter with a uniformly sampled factor between 0.5 and 1.5 on top of the base exponential calculation. This prevents thundering-herd retry collisions when multiple concurrent downloads fail in lockstep.

docs.title: Manual Defensive Retry Loop
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance.core.utils.retry_strategy import RetryStrategy
from globaldatafinance.macro_exceptions import NetworkError
import time

strategy = RetryStrategy(
    initial_backoff=1.0,
    max_backoff=30.0,
    multiplier=2.0
)

max_retries = 3

# max_retries counts additional attempts after the first execution.
for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
    try:
        result = download_file()
        break  # Successful execution completion
    except Exception as exc:
        if not strategy.is_retryable(exc):
            raise  # Abort loop on hard system faults

        if attempt < max_retries:
            backoff = strategy.calculate_backoff(attempt)
            print(f"Attempt {attempt + 1} failed. Next attempt scheduled in {backoff}s...")
            time.sleep(backoff)
        else:
            raise  # Exhausted maximum permitted attempts

docs.title: Automated Library Adapter Behavior
docs.text:
Concrete download adapters invoke RetryStrategy automatically during network operations:

from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM

# CvmDownloadAdapter natively integrates automated exponential backoff loops
cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM()
result = cvm.download(
    destination_path="/data/cvm",
    list_docs=["DFP"],
    initial_year=2023,
    last_year=2023,
)

The underlying adapter execution loop operates as follows:

  1. Executes asynchronous HTTP transfer requests
  2. If exceptions occur, evaluates if the resulting error matches retryable criteria
  3. Computes the required exponential back-off duration
  4. Yields worker threads for the duration of the computed back-off interval
  5. Repeats until the initial execution plus max_retries additional attempts are exhausted, or the operation succeeds

docs.title: Global Environment Retry Customization
docs.text:
Tune global network retry profiles via environment variable declarations:

# Define maximum connection retry attempts
export DATAFINANCE_NETWORK_MAX_RETRIES=5

# Modify the exponential delay scaling multiplier
export DATAFINANCE_NETWORK_RETRY_BACKOFF=2.0

docs.title: Project Exception Definitions
docs.text:
The RetryStrategy engine evaluates symbols generated from macro_exceptions:

from globaldatafinance.macro_exceptions import (
    NetworkError,          # Transient network communication interruptions
    DownloadTimeoutError,  # Download timeout events
    PathPermissionError,   # Filesystem write boundary lockouts
    DiskFullError          # Storage capacity exhaustion errors
)

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Use the environment prepared in the contributing guide. The default gate combines unit tests and deterministic integrations; each test creates its own local inputs.

docs.title: Run the default gate
docs.text:
uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m "not slow and not real_data and not perf" \
  --cov --cov-report=xml --cov-report=term-missing

For a localized change, start with the affected module, for example:

uv run --locked --no-sync pytest tests/application/b3_docs

pytest.ini defines discovery and markers; pyproject.toml defines coverage. For an HTML report, add --cov-report=html to the coverage command.

docs.title: Classify each test
docs.text:
Every test has exactly one primary tier:

Tier Contract unit Isolated behavior with pure collaborators, fakes, or stubs. integration Multiple real components and deterministic local filesystem. perf Benchmarks or resource measurements; always opt-in.

Use slow for heavy scenarios and asyncio for asynchronous execution. real_data requires integration, uses caller-supplied COTAHIST, and is opt-in. These qualifiers do not replace the primary tier.

uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m unit
uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m "integration and not slow and not real_data"
uv run --locked --no-sync pytest tests/perf -m perf -o addopts=''

A command with -m replaces the default selection; use explicit qualifiers to keep external and slow scenarios outside the intended run.

docs.title: Write useful tests
docs.text:
• Mirror the affected boundary: tests/application/, the source under tests/brazil/, or shared foundations. Subdirectories organize topics.
  • Prove behavior, limits, transitions, and regressions through observable outcomes; covered line counts do not replace useful assertions.
  • Use tmp_path and ZIP, CSV, or Parquet inputs created by the test. Replace network calls with httpx.MockTransport or local collaborators.
  • Parquet reading and writing also need real PyArrow proofs of schema, types, content, and temporary-file cleanup. Pandas and Polars are not runtime dependencies of the library.
  • Document deletions and consolidations in .test-integrity-policy.json.

The structural gate below checks tiers and observations in test bodies; it is heuristic and does not prove assertion semantics:

uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/check_test_quality.py

docs.title: Use local COTAHIST
docs.text:
Official data belongs in a caller-owned directory such as cotahist_b3_local/, which Git ignores. Tests do not download these files or read .env implicitly. Supply paths and a year explicitly:

COTAHIST_PATH=./cotahist_b3_local COTAHIST_TEST_YEAR=2023 \
  uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m "real_data and not slow"
COTAHIST_PATH=./cotahist_b3_local COTAHIST_TEST_YEAR=2023 \
  uv run --locked --no-sync pytest -m "real_data and slow"

The first selection does not write Parquet, but the current fixture performs full preflight of every catalog year, including hashes and every record. Even with not slow, this setup can read large files in full. Extraction proofs, including sampling, annual validation, and fast/slow parity, are slow. Full auditing uses an independent decoder.

The fixture inspects the complete catalog before selecting a year. Without COTAHIST_PATH, the selected suite is skipped. When it is set, invalid, empty, unreadable, or missing-year input fails. A sole year can be inferred; with multiple years, COTAHIST_TEST_YEAR is required and must contain four digits. ZIP takes precedence over TXT. Internal members accept modern COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT and historical COTAHIST.A{YYYY} and COTAHIST_A{YYYY} names, always matching the year.

cotahist_b3/ contains only the examples’ versioned synthetic samples, generated by scripts/generate_example_cotahist.py. They are tested under tests/examples without real_data. An official annual dataset may become mandatory in CI only after a versioned fixture or a published artifact with a compatible license exists.

docs.title: Coverage and CI
docs.text:
The product requires 85% aggregate coverage of src/, including branches. The real-validation executor has a separate 85% floor, also including branches. To run its gate without copying the module list and options:

uv run --locked --no-sync pre-commit run real-validation-coverage \
  --hook-stage pre-push --all-files

The quality matrix runs on Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14. Canonical settings are pyproject.toml, pytest.ini, .pre-commit-config.yaml, and .github/workflows/pipeline.yml. Release acceptance adds native Windows/macOS evidence, publication fault scenarios, and packages.

docs.title: Audit external data
docs.text: The complete CVM/COTAHIST campaign is opt-in and may take hours. Use the external-data validation guide to run it, interpret reports, and resume a campaign. It is outside the deterministic local gate.
