docs.title: extract()
docs.text:
def extract(
    self,
    path_of_docs: str,
    assets_list: list[str] | None = None,
    initial_year: int | None = None,
    last_year: int | None = None,
    destination_path: str | None = None,
    output_filename: str = "cotahist_extracted",
    processing_mode: str = "fast",
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> ExtractionResultB3:
    ...

Description: Parses COTAHIST archives (COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP or .TXT), filters target asset transactions, and compiles a unified Parquet file. The API accepts both local formats; official B3 downloads continue to be distributed as ZIP archives.

The parser is strict: 00/99 controls and blank lines are not persisted, and TPMERC outside the filter is counted as filtered. Every 01 record is validated before filtering. When a source contains invalid records, the facade returns success=False, output_file="", and contextual details in errors; callers must check the result. Direct parser calls may raise ExtractionError. Invalid financial values never receive a zero or null fallback.

Within the validated destination, an output-file symbolic link is rejected with a failure result without changing its target. Publication also prevents the output path from replacing a COTAHIST source.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Required Default Description path_of_docs str Yes - Directory containing COTAHIST ZIP or TXT inputs assets_list list[str] \| None No None (["todos"]) Asset classes; todos selects every valid numeric TPMERC initial_year int \| None No None (1986) First annual COTAHIST year, inclusive (>= 1986) last_year int \| None No None (current year) Last annual COTAHIST year, inclusive destination_path str \| None No None (path_of_docs) Output artifact destination directory output_filename str No "cotahist_extracted" Required basename; optional .parquet suffix is appended only when absent processing_mode str No "fast" "fast" permits concurrent sources; "slow" uses one source worker verbose bool No True When True, prints formatted execution summary to console

The Validating B3 files and Processing B3 files bars appear on stdout in both fast and slow, independently of verbose. They count annual sources found: the first advances after a source is validated; the second advances when a processing attempt finishes, including with an error. The summary is emitted only when verbose=True. Parquet consolidation, readback verification, and publication continue after the processing bar; the returned result confirms complete success. Failures and cancellation finish the bar’s output line at the observed count. Selections without files do not display empty bars.

Returns (ExtractionResultB3):

Typed dictionary (TypedDict) containing execution results:

  • success: bool — Whether extraction completed successfully.
  • message: str — Human-readable summary of the execution outcome.
  • total_files: int — Number of annual inputs resolved for the request.
  • success_count: int — Number of sources included in the committed output.
  • error_count: int — Number of entries in errors.
  • total_records: int — Committed output row count.
  • output_file: str — Newly committed output path; empty on failure.
  • errors: dict[str, str] — Dictionary mapping failed files to failure error messages (if any).
  • assets: list[str] — Asset category tags processed during extraction.
  • processing_mode: str — Processing mode used ("fast" or "slow").
  • elapsed_time: float — Total execution duration in seconds.
  • schema_version: int — Parquet schema version (2).
  • integrity: B3IntegrityReport — Coverage, selection, source, verification, warning, and published-output hash evidence.

When preflight fails, integrity retains previously validated sources, missing years, and normalized selection. success_count and total_records remain zero. Each validated source includes input and content hashes, uncompressed size, market counts, original controls encoded as Base64, generation date, trading-date range, trailer convention, blank lines, warnings, and expected and verified digests.

Input and empty-result semantics:

  • The API accepts COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP and COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT; when both formats exist for the same year, both are fully validated. ZIP is selected only when their uncompressed contents are identical; different contents cause failure.
  • Each ZIP read verifies the CRC of every member, including unselected ones, and reads the COTAHIST member from the same open, validated archive. Validation is renewed on every pass, preserving decompression limits and source identity checks.
  • output_filename must be a basename without path separators. The optional .parquet suffix is accepted and appended exactly once when omitted.
  • A missing requested year returns success=False, lists the year in integrity.missing_years, and does not publish a new output. An empty directory reports zero resolved files and every requested year as missing.
  • If every requested source is valid and the filter excludes all quotations, extraction publishes an empty result (success=True).

If valid inputs contain no records after asset filtering, extraction still succeeds and publishes an empty B3 Parquet with the explicit schema.

assets_list=None selects todos, including unknown numeric TPMERC codes; lote_bloco selects 021. All quote fields are validated before filtering, every requested year must be present, and the full output is read back before publication. Gaps or failures return success=False; integrity retains the observed coverage and reason. See the COTAHIST v2 schema reference and migration guide.

For asynchronous cancellation before commit, the service aborts publication, cleans temporary state, and re-raises asyncio.CancelledError; a pre-existing final artifact remains intact.

Preparation, transaction recovery and acquisition, Parquet verification, consolidation, source checksum rechecks, and rollback run outside the event-loop thread. Thread and process workers receive a cancellation signal owned by their extraction run. Cancellation is observed at bounded reads and batch boundaries. The service joins readers and writers before removing their temporary files, including after repeated cancellation requests. A cancellation checkpoint runs immediately before the commit decision. Once that decision starts atomic publication, new cancellation requests wait for completion and the API returns the publication outcome. Commit also runs outside the event-loop thread.

The final input checksum recheck and publication decision run in the same worker, without returning to the event loop between them. Hash reads remain cancellable; the worker checks cancellation once more before starting publication. Detected source changes fail and preserve the previous output. Callers must keep ZIP/TXT inputs unchanged during extraction: this recheck does not lock external writers or provide absolute isolation against concurrent modifications.

A cleanup failure after durable commit preserves success=True, the output path, verified counts, and published-output checksum. Its diagnostic appears in integrity.warnings: PUBLICATION_CLEANUP_RECOVERED means the cleanup retry succeeded; PUBLICATION_CLEANUP_PENDING means recovery state was preserved. For these warnings, source identifies the published Parquet basename. The original diagnostic is also logged. Failures before commit still return a failed outcome and preserve the previous output through rollback.

Raised Exceptions:

  • EmptyAssetListError: Empty array supplied for assets_list parameter.
  • InvalidAssetsName: Non-string filter item or unsupported alias.
  • InvalidFirstYear: Invalid initial year; supported range is 1986 through the current year.
  • InvalidLastYear: Invalid final year, above the current year, or before the initial year.
  • InvalidOutputFilename: Output filename contains path separators or traversal segments.
  • InvalidProcessingMode: Mode other than "fast" or "slow".
  • InvalidDestinationPathError: Empty or whitespace-only path.
  • PathIsNotDirectoryError: Missing input path or an input path that is not a directory.
  • SecurityError: Path rejected by the security policy.

Content and processing failures are collected in errors with success=False. See the exception reference for types used by lower-level calls.

Example:

from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3

def main() -> None:
    b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
    result = b3.extract(
        path_of_docs="/data/cotahist",
        assets_list=["ações", "opções"],
        initial_year=2022,
        last_year=2023,
        processing_mode="fast",
    )
    if not result["success"]:
        raise RuntimeError(result["errors"] or result["message"])
    print(f"Extracted {result['total_records']:,} records")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Integrity report
docs.text:
result["integrity"] is a B3IntegrityReport. Every key below is present, including on failure; nullable values use None. Dates are ISO YYYY-MM-DD strings. Counts and flags describe the supplied sources, without reconciliation against an external trading calendar or instrument registry.

Key Type Meaning status Literal["passed", "failed", "not_run"] Verification status schema_version int Schema version, 2 verification_method str Verification method or "not completed" requested_years list[int] Requested years selected_years list[int] Years of selected, validated sources missing_years list[int] Requested years without an input source complete_market_selection bool todos selection, including unknown numeric codes market_codes list[str] Selected codes; empty for complete market selection asset_classes list[str] Normalized, deduplicated aliases raw_quotes int Total 01 records in validated sources selected_quotes int Records selected by the filter intentional_exclusions int Records excluded by the filter excluded_records int Same value as intentional_exclusions written_rows int Rows written verified_rows int Rows checked during readback selection_complete bool Verification passed and selected = written = verified source_complete bool Complete row selection, no exclusions, and raw = written = verified source_first_trading_date str \| None First date in validated sources source_last_trading_date str \| None Last date in validated sources output_first_trading_date str \| None First date in verified output output_last_trading_date str \| None Last date in verified output unknown_market_counts dict[str, int] Counts by unknown TPMERC code warnings list[B3IntegrityWarning] Warnings associated with an input or published output sources list[B3SourceIntegrityReport] Per-source evidence, detailed below ignored_duplicate_sources list[str] Equivalent TXT inputs skipped in favor of ZIP output_sha256 str \| None SHA-256 of published output; None without confirmed output

output_sha256 identifies the bytes of the published Parquet file. The fast and slow modes can produce different hashes with the same values, types and row order: their different batch limits can change the physical Parquet layout, and an extraction with one source reuses its private artifact without rewriting it. The hash can also change with the PyArrow version or the physical Parquet layout. Use it to check the identity of a specific file. To compare content across modes, check each source’s expected_rows_sha256 and verified_rows_sha256 in the same order, together with the schema and selection; these digests preserve values and ordered occurrences.

Each item in sources contains these required keys:

Key Type Meaning source str Input filename year int Source year member str ZIP member; empty for TXT outer_sha256 str SHA-256 of the input file content_sha256 str SHA-256 of uncompressed COTAHIST bytes uncompressed_bytes int Uncompressed content size market_counts dict[str, int] Counts by TPMERC code unknown_market_counts dict[str, int] Counts by unknown TPMERC code header_records int Number of 00 controls trailer_records int Number of 99 controls generation_date str Declared generation date blank_lines int Observed blank lines warnings list[B3SourceWarningReport] Source warnings raw_quotes int Total 01 records selected_quotes int Selected records intentional_exclusions int Records excluded by the filter excluded_records int Same value as intentional_exclusions written_rows int Rows written for this source verified_rows int Rows verified for this source declared_records int Count declared in the trailer trailer_convention str Trailer count convention first_trading_date str First source trading date last_trading_date str Last source trading date header_base64 str Original 00 control in Base64 trailer_base64 str Original 99 control in Base64 expected_rows_sha256 str Ordered preflight digest of selected rows verified_rows_sha256 str \| None Verified output digest; None before verification

B3SourceWarningReport contains code: str, count: int, and explanation: str. B3IntegrityWarning adds source: str, the input or published Parquet basename. Post-commit cleanup warning codes are described under extract(). The B3 v2 schema defines the row-digest framing.

docs.title: Execution Configuration and Environment Variables
docs.text:
GDF_B3_EXECUTOR_BACKEND is resolved when HistoricalQuotesB3() is constructed and does not alter an existing instance. Resource policy reads GDF_B3_WORKER_LIMIT when calculating worker admission. These options add no public constructor parameters. The default process applies in fast with two sources, two workers, and a compatible spawn context. Conditions and measurements are in the COTAHIST performance guide.

  • GDF_B3_EXECUTOR_BACKEND: Accepts "thread" or "process"; the default is "process".
  • "thread": Uses ThreadPoolExecutor, with lower startup cost and buffers in the parent process.
  • "process": Uses ProcessPoolExecutor with spawn in eligible contexts. It isolates source buffers and can increase aggregate RSS. Measure complete operation time, CPU, and memory on the consumer’s corpus.
  • Fallback: slow, one source, or a one-worker limit use one thread worker. Daemons and sessions without an importable main module or readable script use threads. The logger records the incompatibility and last_phase_timings['effective_backend'] reports the actual backend. Failures after submission retain their diagnostics and normal cleanup.
  • Annual preflight: In fast with process, admits processes when policy allows at least two workers, the context is compatible, and stored annual candidates total at least 64 MiB. Coexisting ZIP and TXT files both count. Smaller workloads and size-read errors use serial validation. Order, first error, typed causes, and joining workers before cleanup are preserved.
  • Child workers instantiate default readers and parsers; internally injected custom collaborators are not serialized. Use threads for these collaborators.
  • Scripts must guard the call with if __name__ == '__main__':. Set GDF_B3_EXECUTOR_BACKEND=thread to explicitly select threads. Invalid values raise ValueError at construction.
  • GDF_B3_WORKER_LIMIT: Optional fast-mode worker cap. Use a positive integer; the effective limit remains the minimum of this value, source-file count, available CPUs, and memory budget. Slow mode remains single-worker. A non-numeric value preserves the default cap; values below one are clamped to one worker.

docs.title: Asset Classification Codes
docs.text:
Code Identifier Description Included B3 TPMERC Codes ações Equities / Stocks 010 (Spot Cash Market), 020 (Fractional Market) etf ETFs 010 (Spot Cash Market), 020 (Fractional Market) opções Options 070 (Call Options), 080 (Put Options) termo Term-market contracts 030 (Term Market) exercicio_opcoes Option Exercises 012 (Call Exercise), 013 (Put Exercise) forward Forward Contracts 050 (Forward with Gain), 060 (Forward with Movement) leilao Auction Market 017 (Auction Market) lote_bloco Block lot 021 (BBT and Midpoint) todos Complete selection Every valid numeric TPMERC

The Portuguese strings in this table are the accepted assets_list aliases. Validation lowercases the input; spelling and accents still matter. ações and etf select the same markets, 010 and 020, without distinguishing stocks from ETFs or classifying issuers. The aliases bdr and futuro are not in the catalog. Use get_available_assets() to query the installed version.

docs.title: Processing modes
docs.text:
Mode Execution Use fast Concurrent sources within CPU, memory, and file-count limits; default cap of 4 workers Allow source-level parallelism slow One source worker and smaller batches Limit concurrency and memory use

Both modes use bounded batches and the same schema and validation. slow does not reduce the requested data or the space needed for temporary files and output. COTAHIST measurements record the environment, corpus, and results. Previous-schema measurements remain in the historical benchmarks.

For consumers importing ProcessingModeEnumB3 through the source namespace, the FAST and SLOW values remain. The 2026-10-20 revision removes desired_concurrent_files, desired_workers, use_parallel_parsing and memory_threshold_mb, which did not control extraction. ResourcePolicyB3 continues to calculate actual limits, while telemetry exposes the effective backend and worker count.

docs.title: B3 Parquet Schema v2
docs.text: The default Parquet schema produced by HistoricalQuotesB3 is version 2. The 20 historical fields retain their order and logical values; v2 adds official COTAHIST fields, the record type, provenance, and original bytes. Every field is required except data_vencimento. The footer carries the integrity manifest and logical schema fingerprint.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column Type Description data_pregao date32[day] Trading session date codigo_bdi large_string BDI market classification code ticker large_string Trading symbol (e.g., PETR4) tipo_mercado large_string Market type nome_resumido large_string Issuer short name especificacao_papel large_string Security specification (e.g., ON, PN) preco_abertura decimal128(38, 2) Opening price preco_maximo decimal128(38, 2) Session high price preco_minimo decimal128(38, 2) Session low price preco_medio decimal128(38, 2) Average price preco_fechamento decimal128(38, 2) Closing price melhor_oferta_compra decimal128(38, 2) Best bid melhor_oferta_venda decimal128(38, 2) Best ask numero_negocios int64 Number of trades quantidade_total int64 Total traded quantity volume_total decimal128(38, 2) Total monetary turnover data_vencimento date32[day] Options/term expiration date; nullable fator_cotacao int64 Quotation scaling factor codigo_isin large_string ISIN code numero_distribuicao int64 Distribution number prazo_termo large_string PRAZOT kept as text, including leading zeros moeda_referencia large_string MODREF reference currency code preco_exercicio decimal128(38, 2) PREEXE exact decimal with scale 2 indicador_correcao large_string INDOPC code preserved, including "0" preco_exercicio_pontos decimal128(38, 6) PTOEXE exact decimal with scale 6 tipo_registro large_string Record identifier ("01") id_fonte large_string SHA-256 of uncompressed COTAHIST contents arquivo_origem large_string COTAHIST input filename membro_origem large_string Selected ZIP member; empty for TXT ano_origem int64 Year validated from the filename linha_origem int64 One-based physical source line registro_original fixed_size_binary[245] Original 01 record bytes without a terminator

preco_exercicio and preco_exercicio_pontos use exact decimals with scales 2 and 6; financial values never pass through floating point. Positions follow the official B3 layout.

docs.title: Ordered row digest
docs.text:
Each source has a SHA-256 computed in schema and physical-line order. The prefix is GLOBALDATAFINANCE-B3-ROW-DIGEST followed by a zero byte, version 2 as a 4-byte unsigned integer, and the column count as a 2-byte unsigned integer. All framing integers are big-endian. Each column name receives an N tag, its UTF-8 byte length as an 8-byte integer, and its content.

Each row starts with R. Null uses only Z; text, ISO dates, decimal integers, and financial values at their declared scale use S, an 8-byte UTF-8 byte length, and content. registro_original uses B, an 8-byte length, and the ASCII bytes of its standard padded Base64 representation. This distinguishes null from empty text and preserves order and repeated occurrences. The oracle implements this contract independently and compares the digests and other manifest facts with reconciled raw source data.

Preflight, replay, and verification readback use the same digest implementation. Preflight and replay group framing by row. Verification readback uses Arrow operations to group canonical columns into bounded segments, preserving the exact version 2 byte stream. Each segment ends at its source boundary; sources with no selected quotations also have their digest checked.

Common length headers use bounded constant tables. These tables contain only tags and lengths, without retaining financial values or source content.

Before merging, each temporary Parquet is checked for schema, complete footer, manifest, and row count. The merge repeats schema and metadata validation when opening each temporary and compares consumed batches with the footer row count independently of row-group flushes. CSV-to-Arrow conversion also requires one row per original record before building the provenance buffer. The final artifact undergoes one complete readback in bounded batches to verify values, provenance, order, and per-source digests before transactional publication. Replay and source identity checks remain mandatory.

Verification readback converts dates, integers, and decimals to canonical strings by column with Arrow, preserving decimal scale without floating point. Column framing also uses Arrow operations, with standard Base64 for original bytes. All 32 columns participate in the digest. Provenance, date, null, order, and count checks continue to cover every row, including batches that cross source boundaries.

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
Source numeric fields must contain only ASCII digits across their full width; leading and trailing spaces are rejected. indicador_correcao validates the single INDOPC digit and preserves it as text. Alphanumeric BDI, PRAZOT, MODREF, and ISIN retain their text contracts. data_vencimento accepts eight spaces or 00000000 as absence and preserves valid dates, including 99991231.

Use pyarrow.parquet.read_table() to load the complete table, or pyarrow.parquet.ParquetFile(...).iter_batches() with batch_size=200_000 for memory-bounded work. PyArrow is the production engine and the recommended reader. Pandas remains compatible as a downstream reader, but consumers must install it separately.

Schema v1 files cannot be promoted or filled with missing data. Regenerate them from the original COTAHIST files using the v2 migration guide.

docs.title: Audit of the Supplied COTAHIST Corpus
docs.text: This record preserves the independent audit of the local corpus used to plan the v2 contract. Input hashes are stored in the versioned cotahist-v2-supplied-corpus.sha256 manifest, with the actual names of all 27 ZIP files and each outer-file SHA-256. The baseline audit used revision c163c92f1a770fde0d3a6f6a83c2305e59a429bd.

docs.title: Controls and omitted fields
docs.text:
The 2025 and 2026 trailers declare quotations only, while earlier files include the 00 and 99 controls in their totals. Each file’s quotation count was confirmed by reading every type-01 line; the control difference is exactly two records.

Official field missing before v2 Rows with nondefault values PRAZOT 1,445,095 MODREF 22,305,860 PREEXE 15,196,391 INDOPC 10,395 PTOEXE 323,647

docs.title: Scope of this evidence
docs.text:
These figures describe the bytes of the frozen files in the manifest; they do not verify an external trading calendar or instrument registry. The local corpus does not include 1986–1999 or dates after 2026-09-02. A later v2 campaign recorded complete reconciliation of all 32 fields and row order, along with the 27 manifest checksums; see the 2000–2026 acceptance. These results are historical. A new campaign must recheck input hashes and reconcile the data before using these numbers as acceptance criteria.

Official format and offsets: B3 historical series layout.

    ...

Import Settings from globaldatafinance.core.config. The optional argument injects an immutable snapshot; with None, the client creates a snapshot from the current environment. The settings property returns the configuration used. See configuration.

docs.title: download()
docs.text:
def download(
    self,
    destination_path: str,
    list_docs: list[str] | None = None,
    initial_year: int | None = None,
    last_year: int | None = None,
    automatic_extractor: bool = False,
) -> DownloadResultCVM:
    ...

Description: Downloads CVM document archives into a local directory.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Required Default Description destination_path str Yes - Target local filesystem output folder list_docs list[str] \| None No None Targeted document codes (None = fetch all) initial_year int \| None No None Starting year (None = earliest available) last_year int \| None No None Last year, inclusive (None = current year) automatic_extractor bool No False Convert to Parquet through PyArrow

With automatic_extractor=True, every CVM column is Arrow string under the exact-text-v1 contract. Each field keeps its original text: decimals, leading zeroes, signs, case, and literals such as N/A, NULL, or None; empty fields are "". Header-only CSVs produce zero rows with string columns. QUOTE_NONE retains literal quotes. Short rows receive trailing empty fields; excess fields, empty or duplicate headers, more than 4,096 columns, and physical records exceeding 8 MiB UTF-8 fail explicitly.

Automatic extraction resolves its extractor per operation without changing the adapter’s configuration. Short-row normalization uses a separate spool for each member; it is removed when conversion finishes, including failures. Transaction staging retains its normal cleanup.

The SHA-256 of all decoded records is compared with reopened Parquet content before publication. Files include page checksums, ZIP and CSV member identity in metadata, and fsync synchronization. Confirmation requires all expected Parquets and their association with the ZIP. Row groups use an estimated 16 MiB budget, up to 50,000 rows. Reads stay on the same opened ZIP and the source is checked again before publication. Removed or renamed CSVs require regeneration into a clean destination when obsolete Parquets are associated with a ZIP of the same filename through cvm.source-archive metadata.

The result confirms the expected ZIP outputs. Output replacement and preservation of unidentified files follow the inventory contract.

The original ZIP is retained after success and failure, including non-CSV members. Concurrent calls to one destination fail before ZIP promotion. After abrupt termination, .cvm-write-lock requires explicit inspection before recovery. Multi-Parquet publication is recoverable as a batch; its visibility to concurrent readers is not instantaneously atomic. Undeclared encoding can be ambiguous, and accounting consistency is not inferred.

This schema change requires consumer migration.

The local filename is the URL path’s final component after one percent-encoding decode. The library rejects separators, invalid Win32 characters, controls, trailing periods or spaces, and reserved DOS devices such as CON, AUX, COM1, and LPT1 with SecurityError, before starting the download or creating staging.

Returns:

Returns a DownloadResultCVM object:

  • success_count_downloads: int — Total count of successfully completed download tasks.
  • error_count_downloads: int — Total count of failed download tasks.
  • successful_downloads: list[str] — List of completed document identifiers in {DOC}_{YEAR} format (e.g., "DFP_2023").
  • failed_downloads: dict[str, str] — Dictionary mapping failed items to specific error messages.
  • elapsed_time: float — Total execution duration in seconds.
  • has_errors() -> bool — Boolean indicator signaling whether failures occurred.

Synchronous Exceptions:

  • InvalidDocumentName: Unsupported document code.
  • InvalidDocumentType: An item in list_docs is not a string.
  • InvalidFirstYear: Invalid initial year.
  • InvalidLastYear: Invalid final year.
  • TypeError: Invalid type for list_docs, automatic_extractor, or a path.
  • InvalidDestinationPathError: Empty or whitespace-only path.
  • PathIsNotDirectoryError: A document or year directory already exists as a file.
  • PathPermissionError: No permission to create or write to the destination.
  • PathCreationError: Destination creation failed, including when a parent is a file.
  • SecurityError: URL-derived filename or local destination is unsafe.

Transient HTTP transmission failures during asynchronous downloads are handled by the internal retry mechanism. When retries are exhausted, each final failure is consolidated in DownloadResultCVM.failed_downloads without terminating the remaining downloads.

If the output directory disappears, becomes a file, or encounters an I/O error while creating the lock after the download, finalization records the failure in failed_downloads and continues other destinations. Replacement by another directory or a symbolic link raises SecurityError.

On systems supporting directory-descriptor-relative operations and child access through descriptor-backed paths, the lock, ZIP promotion, and cleanup remain bound to the opened directory. Automatic extraction reuses that ownership to read the ZIP, write staging, and publish Parquet. Readers and writers use descriptor-backed paths through /proc/self/fd or /dev/fd; if both are unavailable, extraction raises SecurityError before writing data through a mutable pathname. Manifests retain the original relative names. Cleanup preserves staging and logs a diagnostic when it cannot confirm the originally validated directory identity.

On systems without this complete support, the library verifies directory identity before path-based operations. Child traversal is checked before comparing the virtual path’s identity or creating the lock; systems such as macOS, whose /dev/fd does not support this access, use this fallback. Concurrent changes by processes that do not follow the ownership protocol do not have the same atomic guarantee on those systems.

URL selection respects each document’s first year: IPE in 2003; DFP, FCA, and FRE in 2010; ITR in 2011; CGVN and VLMO in 2018. A mixed interval does not generate URLs for years before the document starts.

Execution Example:

cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM()
result = cvm.download(
    destination_path="/data/cvm",
    list_docs=["DFP", "ITR"],
    initial_year=2022,
    last_year=2023,
    automatic_extractor=True
)
if result.has_errors():
    raise RuntimeError(result.failed_downloads)

docs.title: Exceptions and failure results
docs.text: This reference distinguishes input errors, failures collected in results, and lower-level exceptions. See also the CVM and B3 contracts.

docs.title: Handling a public call
docs.text:
Situation Behavior Invalid parameter or path Validation may raise an exception before the main operation A CVM download fails The result records its identifier and cause in failed_downloads; other downloads continue A B3 input is missing, corrupt, or invalid The facade returns success=False, details in errors, and no new output_file An empty B3 directory Returns zero total_files and requested years in integrity.missing_years Valid B3 sources with no quotations after filtering Returns success and publishes an empty Parquet with the B3 schema B3 async cancellation before the commit decision Waits for workers, cleans temporary files, and propagates asyncio.CancelledError

Check result.has_errors() for CVM and result["success"] for B3 before consuming artifacts. Transactional publication describes recovery, cancellation, and visibility limits.

docs.title: Shared exceptions
docs.text:
Import these types from globaldatafinance.macro_exceptions.

Exception Base Condition InvalidDestinationPathError ValueError Empty or whitespace-only path PathIsNotDirectoryError ValueError A required directory is missing or is a file PathPermissionError OSError No permission to create or write to the destination PathCreationError OSError Destination creation fails for another I/O reason FileWriteError OSError File write failure ParquetWriteError OSError Filesystem failure while writing or reopening Parquet DiskFullError OSError Insufficient destination storage ExtractionError Exception Extraction or content-validation failure CorruptedZipError ExtractionError Corrupt or unreadable ZIP SecurityError Exception Violation of path, file, or extraction policy NetworkError Exception Transport failure translated by the CVM adapter DownloadTimeoutError Exception CVM download timeout EmptyDirectoryError Exception Shared type representing the absence of input files

A sensitive destination raises SecurityError. Type errors may raise the built-in TypeError. The B3 facade reports an empty directory through its result as described above; catching EmptyDirectoryError does not replace that check.

During staged CVM Parquet writes, filesystem failures other than ENOSPC become ParquetWriteError with the original cause preserved; ENOSPC becomes DiskFullError. Download aggregation records ParquetWrite: ... when applicable and retains the ZIP for diagnosis. CSV, schema, count, and integrity failures continue to follow the extraction contract.

The CVM adapter translates transport failures, applies the retry policy, and collects persistent failures in failed_downloads. Catching NetworkError synchronously around the facade is not how callers identify these failed downloads.

docs.title: CVM exceptions
docs.text:
These types are defined in globaldatafinance.brazil.cvm.fundamental_stocks_data.errors. CvmError inherits from Exception; every other type in this table inherits from CvmError.

Exception Condition InvalidDocumentName Unsupported CVM document code InvalidDocumentType An item in list_docs is not a string InvalidFirstYear Initial year is not an integer, is below 2003, or exceeds the current year InvalidLastYear Final year is not an integer, exceeds the current year, or precedes the initial year EmptyDocumentListError Internal resolution type for an empty selection MissingDownloadUrlError Internal resolution type for a document without a configured URL

An outer list_docs value other than a list or None raises TypeError. None and [] select all document types. The catalog accepts DFP, ITR, FCA, FRE, CGVN, VLMO, and IPE.

The global year-validation floor is 2003. Per-document first years filter the URLs: a valid interval before DFP begins, for example, generates no DFP URLs for those years. See the first years in the CVM reference.

docs.title: B3 exceptions
docs.text:
These types are defined in globaldatafinance.brazil.b3_data.historical_quotes.errors. B3Error(Exception) is the base for the validation exceptions in this table:

Exception Condition EmptyAssetListError assets_list is empty or not a list; None selects todos InvalidAssetsName Non-string item or unknown alias InvalidFirstYear Initial year outside 1986 through the current year, or an invalid type InvalidLastYear Invalid final year, above the current year, or before the initial year InvalidProcessingMode Mode other than fast or slow InvalidOutputFilename Invalid output name or a name that is not a basename

Accepted aliases: ações, etf, opções, termo, exercicio_opcoes, forward, leilao, lote_bloco, and todos. Validation normalizes letter case. The output name accepts an optional .parquet suffix, appended when absent. Path separators and traversal are rejected.

The module also defines CotahistCatalogError(ValueError) and CotahistPreflightError(ExtractionError) for internal resolution and preflight. Neither inherits from B3Error. The facade converts these input-source failures into unsuccessful results. Catching B3Error handles input validation; processing failures require checking result["success"] and errors.

The CVM and B3 InvalidFirstYear and InvalidLastYear types are distinct classes. Source-specific exceptions are imported from their source modules; the globaldatafinance root exports the facades and ExtractionResultB3.

docs.title: CVM
docs.text:
This example requires access to CVM and a writable destination.

from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM
from globaldatafinance.brazil.cvm.fundamental_stocks_data.errors import CvmError
from globaldatafinance.macro_exceptions import SecurityError

try:
    result = FundamentalStocksDataCVM().download(
        destination_path="./data_cvm",
        list_docs=["DFP"],
        initial_year=2023,
        last_year=2023,
    )
except (CvmError, TypeError, ValueError, OSError, SecurityError) as error:
    raise SystemExit(f"CVM request failed: {error}") from error

if result.has_errors():
    raise RuntimeError(result.failed_downloads)
print(f"Downloaded: {result.success_count_downloads}")

docs.title: B3
docs.text:
Place COTAHIST_A2023.ZIP or .TXT in the input directory before running.

from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3
from globaldatafinance.brazil.b3_data.historical_quotes.errors import B3Error
from globaldatafinance.macro_exceptions import SecurityError


def main() -> None:
    try:
        result = HistoricalQuotesB3().extract(
            path_of_docs="./cotahist_b3",
            assets_list=["ações", "opções"],
            initial_year=2023,
            last_year=2023,
            output_filename="quotes_2023",
        )
    except (B3Error, TypeError, ValueError, OSError, SecurityError) as error:
        raise SystemExit(f"B3 request failed: {error}") from error

    if not result["success"]:
        raise RuntimeError(result["errors"] or result["message"])
    print(f"Rows: {result['total_records']}; output: {result['output_file']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Transactional publication
docs.text: The internal macro_infra/transactional_publication/ infrastructure publishes CVM and B3 artifacts as a recoverable batch. Source owners remain responsible for validating content, schemas, and counts before commit. Concurrent readers may observe individual replacements during commit; recovery delivers the old or new batch according to the durable journal.

docs.title: Lock acquisition and recovery
docs.text:
Acquisition and removal of .globaldatafinance-transaction.lock use an operating-system guard released when its descriptor closes or the process terminates:

  • POSIX locks the destination directory descriptor.
  • Windows uses the empty, private, persistent .globaldatafinance-publication.guard file. It is not transaction residue and must stay in place while writers may run: contenders must lock the same file.

The guard protects the window before owner.json is persisted and serializes recovery attempts. After initialization, the record still rejects live PIDs and locks from another host. A private lock without an owner is recovered automatically only when empty or containing private owner.json temporaries. Unrecognized contents, aliases, and unsafe permissions are preserved with an explicit error.

PID queries use psutil.Process.is_running(), without sending signals or Windows console events. Permission failures during the query prevent recovery and preserve their diagnostic cause.

docs.title: Staging and manifests
docs.text:
New transactions create staging inside the private lock, on the same filesystem as outputs. Manifest temporaries stay inside staging. Crashes before the first journal or external JSON promotion leave residues inside a tree with ownership established by the lock.

The private journal remains the authority for artifact recovery; the external JSON serves discovery. Directory and artifact identities, SHA-256, and ownership checks prevent the external record from authorizing caller-file deletion. Outputs changed outside the transaction are preserved. Cleanup removes children before owner.json, retaining the record if staging removal is interrupted.

docs.title: Compatibility and limits
docs.text:
Valid journals from the previous layout, with staging directly in the destination, remain recoverable, including when the external manifest is missing. Older directories and temporaries without verifiable authority remain preserved for explicit inspection; their prefixes cannot authorize deletion.

The guard requires filesystem support for native locking. The boundary still requires filesystem isolation and excludes hostile concurrent writers and arbitrary process access under the same UID. Publication recovery also does not replace the inspection required by the CVM flow’s outer .cvm-write-lock.

File data is synced before publication. On Windows, this uses write access as required by the CRT. Directory fsync on that platform is explicitly reported as unsupported with a warning; the flow does not attempt to open directories through the CRT file API. On platforms supporting this operation, permission and I/O failures still interrupt the transaction. Recovery after process termination does not imply power-loss durability on every filesystem.

docs.title: B3 historical quotes
docs.text: Use HistoricalQuotesB3 to convert local annual COTAHIST files into one consolidated Parquet. The library returns extraction status and metadata.

docs.title: Prepare the files
docs.text:
The extractor accepts local ZIP or TXT files named COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP or COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT. Obtain them from the official B3 page and place them in an existing directory. The library does not download them.

cotahist/
├── COTAHIST_A2022.ZIP
└── COTAHIST_A2023.TXT

Supply every requested year. If ZIP and TXT coexist for a year, both are fully validated; ZIP is chosen only when their decompressed contents are identical. Different contents cause failure. Keep the files unchanged during extraction.

Inside a ZIP, exactly one COTAHIST member must be at the root, named COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT, COTAHIST.A{YYYY}, or COTAHIST_A{YYYY} with the same year as the outer file. Missing, nested, ambiguous, or wrong-year members are rejected. Sources must contain at least one valid 01 record in addition to their controls.

docs.title: Diagnose UTF-8 text in records with an invalid width
docs.text:
The COTAHIST layout requires 245-byte records, excluding the line ending. A record with 245 characters can exceed this width when an accent is encoded in UTF-8. For example, Â occupies two bytes in UTF-8 and one byte in Latin-1. The field=record_length error reports the physical line and observed size. When strict conversion to Latin-1 produces 245 bytes, the diagnostic also identifies this possible encoding problem.

Every market is validated before filtering; an invalid auction record also prevents an ações extraction. fast and slow apply the same rule.

After confirming that the source is UTF-8, preserve the original and create a Latin-1 copy in another directory. On Linux, for a ZIP with the modern member:

set -o pipefail
mkdir ./cotahist_latin1
unzip -p ./cotahist/COTAHIST_A2026.ZIP COTAHIST_A2026.TXT \
  | iconv -f UTF-8 -t ISO-8859-1 \
  > ./cotahist_latin1/COTAHIST_A2026.TXT

Proceed only if conversion succeeds; on failure, remove the partial copy before trying again. Use path_of_docs="./cotahist_latin1" so the copy goes through full validation. Conversion must preserve text, lines, order, and values, with strict encoding errors. In Parquet, id_fonte and registro_original describe the normalized copy. Also retain hashes of the original and copy to track this preparation.

docs.title: Extract quotes
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3


def main() -> None:
    b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
    result = b3.extract(
        path_of_docs="./cotahist",
        destination_path="./data_b3",
        assets_list=["ações", "opções"],
        initial_year=2022,
        last_year=2023,
        output_filename="quotes_2022_2023",
        processing_mode="fast",
    )
    if not result["success"]:
        raise RuntimeError(result["errors"])
    print(result["output_file"], result["total_records"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

This example creates data_b3/quotes_2022_2023.parquet after validating the sources and verifying the final file. Years are inclusive. Set them explicitly; the defaults span 1986 through the current year.

docs.title: Choose markets
docs.text:
Values in assets_list are aliases for COTAHIST markets. They do not select companies by ticker. ações and etf use the same codes and include the spot market (010) and fractional market (020).

API value Selection ações, etf Spot and fractional: 010, 020 opções Call and put: 070, 080 termo Term: 030 exercicio_opcoes Exercise: 012, 013 forward Forward: 050, 060 leilao Auction: 017 lote_bloco Block lot: 021 todos Every valid numeric TPMERC, including unknown codes

The default assets_list=None means todos; an empty list is invalid. get_available_assets() lists the accepted aliases. API values stay in Portuguese, including when the rest of the program uses another language.

docs.title: Choose a mode and destination
docs.text:
Option When to use it processing_mode="fast" Default: processes files with concurrency bounded by CPU, memory, and source count. processing_mode="slow" Uses one worker and reduces memory use. destination_path Output directory; defaults to path_of_docs. output_filename Base name without directories; .parquet is optional and appended when absent. verbose=False Hides the final summary; progress bars remain visible.

Both modes apply the same data and integrity rules. For worker and resource settings, see advanced usage.

docs.title: Check and consume the result
docs.text:
The main ExtractionResultB3 fields are below. The complete list and exceptions are in the B3 reference. Inside an active event loop, use await b3.extract_async(...); arguments and results are identical. In scripts processing several sources with processes, protect the call with if __name__ == '__main__':, as shown in the parallel processing example.

Field How to use it success Check before consuming the output. errors Failure diagnostics by source or stage. output_file Path to the newly published Parquet; empty on failure. total_records Number of published rows. integrity Annual coverage, validation, provenance, and warnings.

A missing year or invalid source returns failure and publishes no new output. If all sources are valid but the filter selects no quotes, the result is successful with an empty Parquet. Zero rows alone do not indicate an error.

Parquet uses B3 schema v2: exact decimal prices, provenance fields, and the original record. Read it with PyArrow as shown in the quickstart. For files produced by earlier versions, see the migration guide.

docs.title: B3 operational practices
docs.text: Guidance for processing local COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP or COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT files and consuming Parquet output. The API accepts ZIP and TXT; see the B3 guide for input preparation.

docs.title: Plan the year range and resources
docs.text:
Set both ends of the range: every requested year must have a valid source. An omitted final year uses the current year; an omitted initial year requests from 1986 onward. Extraction does not download missing sources.

fast allows concurrent sources within CPU, memory, and file-count limits. slow uses one source worker and smaller batches. Both modes validate the same data and publish the same schema. COTAHIST measurements identify the corpus and environment for each comparison.

docs.title: Separate markets when needed
docs.text:
ações and etf are aliases for the same TPMERC codes, 010 and 020. Writing a file for each alias duplicates that selection; the filter does not distinguish stocks from ETFs within these markets. Consumers need an external registry to separate instruments. The example below separates the cash and fractional markets from options markets, using explicit year ranges:

from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3


def main() -> None:
    b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
    for asset, filename in [("ações", "cash_2023"), ("opções", "options_2023")]:
        result = b3.extract(
            path_of_docs="./cotahist_b3",
            assets_list=[asset],
            initial_year=2023,
            last_year=2023,
            output_filename=filename,
            processing_mode="fast",
        )
        if not result["success"]:
            raise RuntimeError(result["errors"] or result["message"])
        print(result["output_file"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Reserve space for temporary files and publication
docs.text:
Storage must cover the inputs, per-source temporary Parquets, and consolidated output; recoverable publication also preserves previous output when it exists. Required capacity depends on the data and compression. Check the destination filesystem and reduce the requested range when necessary. slow limits concurrency and memory; it does not reduce the requested data or the space used by the corresponding artifacts.

import shutil

free_bytes = shutil.disk_usage("./cotahist_b3").free
print(f"Available storage: {free_bytes / 1024**3:.2f} GiB")

docs.title: Read output in batches
docs.text:
Check the result before opening its output file. For analysis that does not need the whole table in memory, use PyArrow batches and choose a suitable batch_size:

import pyarrow.parquet as pq

for batch in pq.ParquetFile("./cotahist_b3/cash_2023.parquet").iter_batches(
    batch_size=200_000
):
    print(batch.num_rows)

Polars and pandas are optional readers installed separately by the consumer. See the B3 API, v2 schema, examples, and FAQ.

docs.title: CVM filings
docs.text: Use FundamentalStocksDataCVM to download CVM filings by document type and year. Downloads require internet access; Parquet conversion is optional.

docs.title: Choose documents and years
docs.text:
Code Content First year DFP Annual financial statements 2010 ITR Quarterly information 2011 FRE Reference form 2010 FCA Registration form 2010 CGVN Governance report 2018 VLMO Traded and held securities 2018 IPE Periodic and occasional documents 2003

Start and end years are inclusive. In mixed selections, each document respects its first year. get_available_docs() returns codes and descriptions; get_available_years() returns the limits by group and the current year.

docs.title: Download and convert
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM

result = FundamentalStocksDataCVM().download(
    destination_path="./data_cvm",
    list_docs=["DFP", "ITR"],
    initial_year=2023,
    last_year=2023,
    automatic_extractor=True,
)
if result.error_count_downloads > 0 or result.success_count_downloads == 0:
    raise RuntimeError(result.failed_downloads)
print(result.successful_downloads)

Choose a small range for the first run. The destination can be relative or absolute and must allow writing.

Option Behavior list_docs List of codes. None or [] selects all types. initial_year / last_year Inclusive limits. Without explicit limits, selection uses the available minimums and the current year. automatic_extractor=False Default: saves ZIPs. automatic_extractor=True Saves ZIPs and converts their CSV files to Parquet.

The CVM reference contains the full signature, year limits, and exceptions.

docs.title: Understand the generated files
docs.text:
Original ZIPs are retained, including attachments that are not CSV. Extraction creates one Parquet per CSV with the same base name. ZIPs and Parquets go under {destination_path}/{DOC}/{YEAR}/, for example:

data_cvm/DFP/2023/
├── dfp_cia_aberta_2023.zip
└── dfp_cia_aberta_BPA_con_2023.parquet

Each Parquet name depends on the CSV files present in the ZIP.

Under the exact-text-v1 contract, all CVM columns contain text. Leading zeros, decimal separators, and literal tokens are preserved; empty fields are "". Convert dates and numbers explicitly in your analysis. A header-only CSV produces an empty Parquet with the defined columns.

Content is verified before publication. The Parquet batch can be recovered after a failure; concurrent readers do not receive an instantaneous swap of the whole directory. Details are in the CVM reference and the publication protocol.

docs.title: Check success and handle failures
docs.text:
The return value is a DownloadResultCVM, not a data table:

  • successful_downloads lists completed identifiers, such as DFP_2023.
  • failed_downloads maps failures to their diagnostics.
  • success_count_downloads and error_count_downloads summarize the batch.

Individual file failures are recorded in the result and may coexist with completed downloads. Check these fields before continuing your analysis. Parameter or path errors can raise exceptions immediately; see the documented exceptions.

In notebooks or applications with an active event loop, use await cvm.async_download(...) with the same arguments and result, as described in the async API.

To adjust logs and attempts, see logging and retry. If you previously consumed Parquets with inferred types, follow the exact-text migration.

docs.title: Resume downloads with a checkpoint
docs.text:
Set base_path to a directory where the application has write access.

Record successful_downloads in an application-owned checkpoint. A year directory may remain after a failure. Request each pending year separately to respect gaps in history:

import json
from pathlib import Path

from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM

cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM()
base_path = Path("/data/cvm")
checkpoint = base_path / "completed-downloads.json"
completed_downloads = set()
if checkpoint.is_file():
    completed_downloads.update(json.loads(checkpoint.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
current_year = cvm.get_available_years().current_year
refresh_years = {current_year}
for year in range(2020, current_year + 1):
    identifier = f"DFP_{year}"
    if identifier in completed_downloads and year not in refresh_years:
        continue
    result = cvm.download(
        destination_path=str(base_path), list_docs=["DFP"],
        initial_year=year, last_year=year, automatic_extractor=True,
    )
    if identifier in result.successful_downloads:
        completed_downloads.add(identifier)
        pending = checkpoint.with_suffix(".tmp")
        pending.write_text(json.dumps(sorted(completed_downloads)), encoding="utf-8")
        pending.replace(checkpoint)
    if result.has_errors():
        print(result.failed_downloads)

The example uses a checkpoint owned by a single process and refreshes the current year on each run. CVM may also revise earlier years: include them in refresh_years according to your application’s policy. The checkpoint records previous successes; revalidate local artifacts before reusing them and remove identifiers whose files are missing or corrupted.

docs.title: Practical Examples
docs.text: This page provides end-to-end operational code examples illustrating how to implement Global-Data-Finance in real-world data engineering scripts and analytical workflows.

docs.title: Example 1: Full DFP Regulatory Ingestion
docs.text:
Download standardized annual financial statements directly from CVM servers and normalize them into columnar Apache Parquet artifacts.

from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM

# Instantiate public client
cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM()

# Trigger download with automated Parquet conversion
cvm_result = cvm.download(
    destination_path="/home/user/financial_data/dfp",
    list_docs=["DFP"],
    initial_year=2020,
    last_year=2023,
    automatic_extractor=True  # Automatically converts downloaded tables into Parquet
)
if cvm_result.error_count_downloads > 0 or cvm_result.success_count_downloads == 0:
    print(f"✗ Incomplete CVM download: {cvm_result.failed_downloads}")
    raise SystemExit(1)

print("✓ Ingestion and extraction completed successfully!")

docs.title: Example 2: High-Performance Equities and ETF Extraction

An integrated ingestion script compiling corporate fundamental disclosures from CVM alongside historical exchange quotes from B3.

base_dir = "/home/user/financial_data"

cotahist_dir = os.path.join(base_dir, "cotahist")

print("=" * 60)
print("PHASE 1: Downloading CVM Financial Filings")
print("=" * 60)

docs.title: Example 5: Bounded PyArrow Batch Processing
docs.text:
Use PyArrow to process Parquet data in bounded batches.

import pyarrow.compute as pc
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3

# Extract transaction records
b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
result = b3.extract(
    path_of_docs="/data/cotahist",
    assets_list=["ações"],
    initial_year=2020,
    last_year=2023
)

# Project and filter without loading the entire artifact
parquet = pq.ParquetFile(result['output_file'])
for batch in parquet.iter_batches(
    batch_size=200_000,
    columns=['ticker', 'preco_minimo', 'preco_maximo'],
):
    petr4 = batch.filter(pc.equal(batch.column('ticker'), 'PETR4'))
    if petr4.num_rows:
        print(petr4)

docs.title: Example 6: Command-Line Automation Script
docs.text:
A self-contained CLI script designed for scheduled cron executions and unattended batch data harvesting.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Automated CLI batch harvester for downloading and normalizing financial data.
"""

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM, HistoricalQuotesB3

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Automated financial data harvester")
    parser.add_argument("--source", choices=["cvm", "b3", "both"], required=True, help="Target repository data source")
    parser.add_argument("--destination", type=str, required=True, help="Root target output folder")
    parser.add_argument("--start-year", type=int, default=2022, help="Initial historical fiscal year")
    parser.add_argument("--end-year", type=int, default=2023, help="Ending fiscal year")
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true", help="Enable verbose console debugging output")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    # Verify and initialize destination repository tree
    dest_path = Path(args.destination)
    dest_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    try:
        if args.source in ["cvm", "both"]:
            print("Downloading CVM corporate regulatory archives...")
            cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM()
            cvm_result = cvm.download(
                destination_path=str(dest_path / "cvm"),
                list_docs=["DFP", "ITR"],
                initial_year=args.start_year,
                last_year=args.end_year,
                automatic_extractor=True
            )
            if cvm_result.has_errors() or cvm_result.success_count_downloads == 0:
                print("✗ CVM document download failed", file=sys.stderr)
                for doc, err in cvm_result.failed_downloads.items():
                    print(f"  • {doc}: {err}", file=sys.stderr)
                return 1
            print(f"✓ Downloaded {cvm_result.success_count_downloads} CVM archives")

        if args.source in ["b3", "both"]:
            print("Extracting B3 historical exchange quotes...")
            b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
            b3_result = b3.extract(
                path_of_docs=str(dest_path / "cotahist"),
                assets_list=["ações", "etf"],
                initial_year=args.start_year,
                last_year=args.end_year,
                destination_path=str(dest_path / "quotes")
            )
            if not b3_result['success'] or b3_result['total_records'] == 0:
                print("✗ B3 quotes extraction failed", file=sys.stderr)
                for file_name, err in b3_result['errors'].items():
                    print(f"  • {file_name}: {err}", file=sys.stderr)
                return 1
            print(f"✓ Normalized and consolidated {b3_result['total_records']:,} transaction rows")

        print("✓ Automated batch processing script finished cleanly!")
        return 0

    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"✗ Fatal execution exception encountered: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Execution Examples:

# Execute only CVM regulatory harvesting
python harvester.py --source cvm --destination /data --start-year 2022

# Execute only B3 market quote processing
python harvester.py --source b3 --destination /data --start-year 2020 --end-year 2023

# Execute comprehensive harvesting across both sources
python harvester.py --source both --destination /data --verbose

docs.title: Example 7: Jupyter Notebook Interactive Visualizations
docs.text:
Harnessing Global-Data-Finance inside interactive Jupyter notebook sessions to generate financial charting analytics.

Optional Dependencies

Pandas and the visualization libraries used in this example (matplotlib, seaborn) are optional external packages:

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

if not result["success"]:

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
docs.text: Answers and solutions addressing common inquiries regarding installation, configuration, and architectural usage of Global-Data-Finance.

docs.title: How do I install Global-Data-Finance?
docs.text:
Execute the simple pip command below inside your terminal:

pip install globaldatafinance

Consult our comprehensive Installation Guide for deeper instructions involving virtual environments and alternate package managers like uv.

docs.title: Which Python version is required?
docs.text: Global-Data-Finance requires Python >=3.12,<4.0. The current CI workflow exercises Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14; other versions inside the supported range are not implied to be CI-tested.

docs.title: Is installing within a virtual environment recommended?
docs.text:
Yes, absolutely! Isolating dependencies via venv or conda is deeply recommended to avoid cross-package collisions:

python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Linux/macOS
pip install globaldatafinance

docs.title: Where does the library store downloaded files?
docs.text:
Downloaded bundles and extracted Parquet datasets are saved into the directory specified in destination_path, organized into subdirectories by document type and fiscal year (format {destination_path}/{DOC}/{YEAR}/). For example:

from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM

cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM()
cvm.download(
    destination_path="/home/user/financial_data",
    list_docs=["DFP"],
    initial_year=2023,
    last_year=2023,
)
# Files persisted under: /home/user/financial_data/DFP/2023/dfp_cia_aberta_2023.zip

docs.title: How can I dynamically inspect which documents and asset classes are supported?
docs.text:
Invoke the introspectable public get_available_* discovery methods attached to each public facade:

from globaldatafinance import (
    FundamentalStocksDataCVM,
    HistoricalQuotesB3,
)

# For CVM Corporate Filings
cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM()
docs = cvm.get_available_docs()
years = cvm.get_available_years()

# For B3 Market Quotes
b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
assets = b3.get_available_assets()
years = b3.get_available_years()

docs.title: What financial disclosure categories can be downloaded from CVM?
docs.text:
• DFP: Standardized Annual Financial Statements (Demonstrações Financeiras Padronizadas)
  • ITR: Quarterly Interim Financial Statements (Informações Trimestrais)
  • FRE: Reference Form Disclosures (Formulário de Referência)
  • FCA: Corporate Cadastral Registration Forms (Formulário Cadastral)
  • CGVN: Corporate Governance Reports (Código de Governança)
  • VLMO: Securities Trading & Holding Declarations (Valores Mobiliários)
  • IPE: Periodic and Eventual Filings (Informações Periódicas e Eventuais)

See CVM Documents for full parameter references.

docs.title: How do I restrict downloads to a single document type?
docs.text:
Pass a one-element list containing your target document code into list_docs:

cvm.download(
    destination_path="/data",
    list_docs=["DFP"],  # Restricts download strictly to DFP archives
    initial_year=2022
)

docs.title: What does the automatic_extractor parameter do?
docs.text:
When specifying automatic_extractor=True, downloaded ZIP bundles are automatically decompressed, evaluated, and converted into columnar Apache Parquet files natively optimized for high-speed dataframe analytics:

from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM

cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM()
result = cvm.download(
    destination_path="/data",
    list_docs=["DFP"],
    automatic_extractor=True,  # Converts raw accounting CSV ledgers straight into .parquet files
)

docs.title: How does the library handle connection dropouts or interrupted HTTP transfers?
docs.text: The underlying network layer features automated asynchronous retries coupled with custom exponential back-off strategies. For mission-critical production pipelines, consider pairing library retries with application-level orchestration traps (review our Retry Strategy Architecture).

docs.title: Where can I obtain official COTAHIST historical quote archives?
docs.text:
Download raw historical bundles directly from B3’s official data portal: 🔗 https://www.b3.com.br/pt_br/market-data-e-indices/servicos-de-dados/market-data/historico/mercado-a-vista/cotacoes-historicas/

The API accepts COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP or the uncompressed COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT. When both formats exist for a year, both are validated; ZIP is selected only when their decompressed contents are identical. Conflicting contents fail. path_of_docs is an existing local input directory; the library does not download or populate the B3 files. BDRs and Futures are Planned, not currently accepted asset categories.

docs.title: What is the distinction between fast and slow processing modes?
docs.text:
Processing Profile Default workers Measured throughput* Measured peak RSS* Recommended Use fast Up to 4, bounded by CPU count, available memory, and source file count 34,313.8 rows/s 429.88 MiB Prioritize throughput slow 1 worker 29,759.9 rows/s 331.11 MiB Reduce memory use

Historical implementation v3 measurement on 27 files (2000–2026), excluding 2,283 TPMERC 021 rows; it does not describe or directly compare with schema v2. See the benchmark details.

from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3

b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()

# Execute using Fast mode (Recommended Default)
result_fast = b3.extract(
    path_of_docs="/data/cotahist",
    assets_list=["ações"],
    processing_mode="fast",
)

# Execute using Slow mode
result_slow = b3.extract(
    path_of_docs="/data/cotahist",
    assets_list=["ações"],
    processing_mode="slow",
)

docs.title: How do I filter extractions for stock-class records?
docs.text:
Supply "ações" inside the required assets_list argument. This alias selects both spot (010) and fractional (020) market records:

from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3

b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
result = b3.extract(
    path_of_docs="/data/cotahist",
    assets_list=["ações"],  # Selects TPMERC 010 and 020 equity records
    initial_year=2023,
    last_year=2023,
)

docs.title: Can I extract multiple asset classifications simultaneously?
docs.text:
Yes! Include multiple asset keywords within the passed list array:

from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3

b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
result = b3.extract(
    path_of_docs="/data/cotahist",
    assets_list=["ações", "etf", "opções"],
    initial_year=2023,
    last_year=2023,
)

docs.title: How can I customize the filename of the produced Parquet artifact?
docs.text:
Provide your preferred base filename string (excluding the .parquet extension) via output_filename:

from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3

b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
result = b3.extract(
    path_of_docs="/data/cotahist",
    initial_year=2023,
    last_year=2023,
    assets_list=["ações"],
    output_filename="equities_2023",  # Generates an artifact titled: equities_2023.parquet
)

docs.title: How are CVM file downloads accelerated?
docs.text: Global-Data-Finance uses asynchronous concurrent downloads by default (CvmDownloadAdapter, up to 10 simultaneous downloads). Elapsed time depends on the network, CVM servers, and requested volume; see the full CVM pipeline baseline.

docs.title: How can I maximize B3 market quote extraction throughput?
docs.text:
Maintain the default "fast" processing profile:

from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3

b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
result = b3.extract(
    path_of_docs="/data/cotahist",
    assets_list=["ações"],
    processing_mode="fast",
)

docs.title: Can I spawn parallel worker processes across separate historical years?
docs.text:
Yes! You can orchestrate multi-threaded or multi-process concurrent extractions utilizing Python’s native concurrent.futures or multiprocessing toolsets:

from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3


def process_fiscal_year(year: int) -> dict:
    b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
    return b3.extract(
        path_of_docs="/data/cotahist",
        assets_list=["ações"],
        initial_year=year,
        last_year=year,
        output_filename=f"stocks_year_{year}",
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as executor:
        results = list(executor.map(process_fiscal_year, range(2020, 2024)))

docs.title: What libraries should I use to analyze generated Parquet datasets?
docs.text:
Use PyArrow by default. If DataFrame workflows are preferred, install Pandas separately with python -m pip install pandas:

import pyarrow.parquet as pq
for batch in pq.ParquetFile("cotahist_extracted.parquet").iter_batches():
    print(batch)

# Optional: after installing Pandas in the consumer environment
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_parquet("cotahist_extracted.parquet")

docs.title: Which engine does extraction use?
docs.text:
• PyArrow: the production read/write engine and a bounded-batch option for large inputs.
  • Pandas: optional downstream reader compatible with generated Parquets; it is not installed by the library.

Polars is not installed by the package, but consumers can add it as an optional downstream reader.

docs.title: How do I isolate trading activity for a specific ticker symbol?
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_parquet("cotahist_extracted.parquet")
petr4 = df[df['ticker'] == 'PETR4']

docs.title: “No module named ‘globaldatafinance’”
docs.text:
Cause: The library has not been installed into your active Python interpreter or your virtual environment remains inactive. Solution: Activate your environment and reinstall:

pip install globaldatafinance

docs.title: “Python version not supported”
docs.text: Cause: The script is executing under a Python runtime outside >=3.12,<4.0. Solution: Install a supported Python release and recreate the environment.

docs.title: “InvalidDocumentName”
docs.text:
Cause: An unconfirmed document acronym string was supplied to list_docs. Solution: Confirm valid document strings via programmatic catalog inspection:

docs = cvm.get_available_docs()
print(list(docs.keys()))

docs.title: Empty B3 directory or missing year
docs.text: An empty input directory returns success=False, total_files=0, and output_file=""; requested years appear in integrity.missing_years. The call also fails when any requested year is missing. Add the annual files or restrict the range to available years. No new output is published. See the B3 contract.

docs.title: Download Failures or Network Timeouts
docs.text:
Cause: Intermittent network connection drops or transient unavailability of CVM regulatory servers. Solution:

  1. The library automatically performs retries with exponential backoff during asynchronous downloads.
  2. Inspect result.failed_downloads after execution to determine which individual documents encountered persistent failures.
  3. If necessary, configure network timeout and retry limits via DATAFINANCE_NETWORK_TIMEOUT and DATAFINANCE_NETWORK_MAX_RETRIES environment variables.

docs.title: Is Global-Data-Finance ready for production usage?
docs.text:
The package distribution is classified as Beta. The currently implemented CVM and B3 workflows are considered Production for their documented contracts and are exercised by the repository’s quality gates. BDRs, Futures, and other planned capabilities are not supported. Production deployment guidelines:

  • Maintain diagnostic logging setups
  • Wrap invocations within robust application-level exception handlers
  • Monitor local storage capacity and system RAM parameters

docs.title: How do I automate unattended periodic data syncing?
docs.text:
Schedule automated script executions using operating system schedulers such as cron on POSIX servers:

# Crontab configuration executing harvesting script daily at 02:00 AM
0 2 * * * /path/to/venv/bin/python /path/to/harvester.py

docs.title: How can I integrate extraction steps into Apache Airflow or modern data pipelines?
docs.text:
Global-Data-Finance integrates cleanly into orchestration engines such as:

  • Apache Airflow: Build Python Operators inside DAG definitions
  • Prefect: Implement processing routines inside tasks and flows
  • Dagster: Package extractions as software-defined ops or assets
  • Luigi: Wire methods directly inside operational pipeline steps

Minimal Airflow Task snippet:

from datetime import datetime
from airflow import DAG
from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator
from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM


def sync_cvm_filings():
    cvm = FundamentalStocksDataCVM()
    cvm.download(
        destination_path="/data/cvm",
        list_docs=["DFP"],
        initial_year=2023,
        automatic_extractor=True,
    )


with DAG(
    dag_id="cvm_sync_dag",
    start_date=datetime(2024, 1, 1),
    schedule="@daily",
    catchup=False,
) as dag:
    task = PythonOperator(
        task_id="download_regulatory_filings",
        python_callable=sync_cvm_filings,
    )

docs.title: Verify the installation
