print(FundamentalStocksDataCVM().get_available_docs())
print(HistoricalQuotesB3().get_available_assets())

These queries do not download data. The library already installs PyArrow. Pandas and Polars are optional readers for Parquet analysis; install them separately when needed.

docs.title: Resolve common problems
docs.text:
Symptom What to check No module named globaldatafinance Use the same Python for installation and execution; check python -m pip show globaldatafinance. Unsupported Python Create the virtual environment with a version in the supported range. Dependency conflict Install in a new virtual environment; project versions are in pyproject.toml. Installation permission failure Use a virtual environment in a directory where you have write access.

Continue with the quickstart.

docs.title: CVM exact text preservation migration
docs.text:
The exact-text-v1 contract writes every CVM column as Arrow string. This changes persisted schemas: consumers depending on inferred int64, uint64, float64, booleans, or nulls must migrate explicitly. The original ZIP remains available after successful extraction.

CSV input Previous Parquet exact-text-v1 Parquet 000012345 Integer without leading zeroes "000012345" 1.234567890123456789 Rounded float64 decimal "1.234567890123456789" 1e-400 0.0 "1e-400" N/A, NULL, None Inferred null Original text Empty field Inferred null "" TrUe Boolean "TrUe" Header-only CSV Arrow null columns Arrow string columns, zero rows

docs.title: Regeneration and consumer cutover
docs.text:
1. Keep original ZIPs and previous output during migration.
  2. Regenerate Parquets in a new directory using automatic_extractor=True. The download-only default, automatic_extractor=False, remains available.
  3. Check has_errors() and completed {DOC}_{YEAR} identities.
  4. Check regenerated files for cvm.contract=exact-text-v1 metadata.
  5. Convert only required columns according to your data dictionary and test those consumers before switching the directory read by the application.

A previous Parquet that already rounded values or removed zeroes cannot recover original text. Regeneration requires the corresponding ZIP or a new official download. Combining previous and new schemas in one dataset can cause incompatibility or coercion; migrate into a new destination.

from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

import pyarrow.parquet as pq

path = Path("cvm-exact/DFP/2024/dfp_cia_aberta_DRE_con_2024.parquet")
table = pq.read_table(path)
assert table.schema.metadata[b"cvm.contract"] == b"exact-text-v1"

raw_value = table.column("VL_CONTA")[0].as_py()
amount = Decimal(raw_value) if raw_value else None

Financial conversion also requires interpreting currency, scale, reporting period, version, and statement type according to the CVM dataset. The pipeline preserves supplied fields; accounting consistency of the declared filing remains a consumer business validation.

docs.title: Integrity and operation
docs.text:
Before publication, the pipeline compares a SHA-256 of all decoded records with the reopened Parquet content. Metadata includes cvm.contract, cvm.content-sha256, cvm.source-archive, cvm.source-archive-sha256, cvm.source-member, and cvm.source-encoding. Extraction confirmation requires every expected Parquet and its association with the consumed ZIP. Page checksums, complete reads, and fsync protect persisted publication.

Every pass reads the same opened ZIP; source changes abort extraction before publication.

docs.title: Output inventory
docs.text:
Parquets expected by the ZIP are published under their corresponding names, replacing within the transaction the regular file that occupies one of those names. A symbolic link at an expected name is rejected as ExtractionError: extraction of that ZIP fails, the facade records the failure in failed_downloads, and neither the link nor its target changes. Regular files outside this inventory block reprocessing when cvm.source-archive associates them with a ZIP of the same filename. Without this identity, they remain caller data without filename recognition and can coexist with new outputs even after success. Symbolic links outside the inventory are not inspected and are also preserved.

The result confirms expected outputs without certifying every Parquet in the directory. To replace a dataset, retain previous files, regenerate into a new destination, and verify the data before switching consumers.

docs.title: Text contract limits
docs.text:
Quotes remain literal under the QUOTE_NONE dialect. Short rows receive trailing empty fields; the retained ZIP preserves the distinction between absent and empty fields. Excess fields, empty or duplicate headers, more than 4,096 columns, and physical records exceeding 8 MiB in UTF-8 fail explicitly. Row groups contain up to 50,000 rows, reduced to respect an estimated 16 MiB data and offset budget; this budget is not an absolute process RSS limit.

UTF-8 and UTF-8 BOM are validated completely. For non-UTF-8 sources, the documented policy distinguishes CP1252 and Latin-1 from observed bytes. An input without an encoding declaration can be ambiguous; original ZIP bytes remain available for independent inspection.

Concurrent calls to one destination fail before ZIP replacement. .cvm-write-lock/owner.json identifies the owning process. After abrupt termination, the library retains that lock and requires explicit inspection before recovery: confirm no active writer exists, preserve evidence, and recover derived transaction state. The library never automatically takes an unverifiable lock. Failures remain in the result; a Parquet’s existence alone does not establish success.

IPE includes 2003 onward. get_available_years().ipe_min_year exposes that minimum as a property; the four tuple fields continue to describe general documents, ITR, CGVN/VLMO, and the current year.

See the CVM reference and testing guide for the official campaign with independent comparison of every file and record.

docs.title: Migration: infrastructure clean cut
docs.text: This breaking change belongs to the 0.x line and is planned for v0.2.0, not for the patch release v0.1.5. Obsolete generic APIs and the automatic Pandas dependency have been removed. The root facades, public CVM/B3 signatures, output names, Parquet schemas, and transactional publication semantics remain unchanged. The cut is deliberately incompatible: no alias, warning, shim, or fallback is retained for removed names.

docs.title: Version removed from the package root
docs.text:
globaldatafinance.__version__ is no longer exported. Read the installed distribution metadata at runtime instead:

from importlib.metadata import version

package_version = version('globaldatafinance')

docs.title: Download timeout
docs.text:
Before:

from globaldatafinance.macro_exceptions import TimeoutError

After:

from globaldatafinance.macro_exceptions import DownloadTimeoutError

try:
    download()
except DownloadTimeoutError:
    recover_or_report()

DownloadTimeoutError keeps the former (doc_name, timeout=None) constructor and human-readable message format. The old name is no longer importable. Python’s built-in TimeoutError remains an internal transport failure handled by the CVM adapter; it is not the domain exception.

docs.title: Removed generic adapters
docs.text:
ExtractorAdapter and ReadFilesAdapter are no longer part of globaldatafinance.macro_infra. The modules globaldatafinance.macro_infra.extractor_file and globaldatafinance.macro_infra.read_files were removed.

Before:

from globaldatafinance.macro_infra import ExtractorAdapter, ReadFilesAdapter

After, use the source boundary that owns the data contract:

from globaldatafinance.brazil.cvm.ingestion.extract import (
    CvmParquetExtractor,
)

cvm_extractor = CvmParquetExtractor()
convert_zip = cvm_extractor.extract
convert_zip('download.zip', 'cvm-output')

For B3 files, use the HistoricalQuotesB3 facade and the source-owned components documented in B3 Historical Quotes. Do not recreate a generic adapter for the removed modules: CVM and B3 have different format rules, year floors, and diagnostics.

docs.title: Pandas is no longer installed automatically
docs.text:
The library runtime uses PyArrow for CSV and Parquet. A consumer that still needs DataFrames must declare the dependency independently:

python -m pip install pandas

For the recommended memory-bounded reader, no additional package is needed:

import pyarrow.parquet as pq

for batch in pq.ParquetFile('cotahist.parquet').iter_batches(
    batch_size=200_000
):
    consume(batch)

Pandas and Polars may still be used as optional downstream readers, but they are not installed or imported by the package.

docs.title: B3 catch boundary
docs.text:
B3 input-validation exceptions preserve their own types and inherit from B3Error. The example uses execution and handling functions defined by the consumer:

from globaldatafinance.brazil.b3_data.historical_quotes.errors import B3Error

try:
    result = run_b3_operation()
except B3Error as error:
    handle_b3_input_error(error)
else:
    if not result["success"]:
        raise RuntimeError(result["errors"] or result["message"])

B3Error is source-local and is not exported from globaldatafinance or used as a global base. Year policies remain separate: B3 still has its 1986 minimum, and each source retains its own InvalidFirstYear and InvalidLastYear classes.

CotahistCatalogError inherits from ValueError and CotahistPreflightError from ExtractionError; they are internal types outside this hierarchy. The facade returns source failures in errors, with success=False. The exception reference distinguishes these paths.

docs.title: CVM Parquet write failures
docs.text:
Filesystem failures during staged Parquet creation, writing, closing, or reopening are now ParquetWriteError, with the original cause preserved. ENOSPC remains DiskFullError; CSV, Arrow, schema, row-count, corrupt-ZIP, and combined rollback failures remain ExtractionError where that is the appropriate contract.

Download aggregation records a recognized failure as:

ParquetWrite: Failed to write Parquet file '...'

The source ZIP is retained for diagnosis. Consumers that previously treated all ExtractionError values alike can catch ParquetWriteError explicitly when they need to distinguish an infrastructure failure from bad source content.

docs.title: Destinations and internal temporary files
docs.text: CVM and B3 share only invariant destination normalization and preparation. The source owner remains responsible for creating directories, and the transactional publisher does not create the destination. Downloads and Parquet writers reserve hidden temporary files beside the destination so publication remains eligible on the same filesystem.

docs.title: Migration 0.2.0: PyArrow and ingestion integrity
docs.text:
Version 0.2.0 moves production ingestion paths to PyArrow, removes Polars from library dependencies, and strengthens CVM and B3 integrity guarantees. The three root public facades and their signatures remain stable:

from globaldatafinance import (
    ExtractionResultB3,
    FundamentalStocksDataCVM,
    HistoricalQuotesB3,
)

docs.title: Consumer-facing changes
docs.text: Change Required action Strict B3 parser Correct the source file or handle ExtractionError; invalid values no longer fall back to zero, an empty string, or null. Polars removed Install Polars explicitly if the application uses it to read Parquet. ExtractorAdapter.extract_csv_from_zip_to_parquet removed Migrate internal use to the CVM facade or another appropriate public interface. Pandas metadata removed Do not depend on physical b'pandas' metadata; use logical schemas and values. Fully filtered B3 input Treat an empty Parquet as a valid result when TPMERC filtering finds no assets. Canonical archive namespace Use Settings.archive; Settings.archive_safety no longer exists and has no compatibility alias. Strict logging configuration Use only documented LoggingSettings fields and environment variables; LoggingSettings(structured=True) and unknown DATAFIN_LOG_* variables now raise ValidationError. Logging destination and context Use a log_file under an application-approved directory; roots/protected directories are rejected, and common secret fields receive best-effort redaction. Do not send secrets to logging. Exact CVM preservation Regenerate Parquets as exact-text-v1; all columns are strings and numeric conversions are explicit. B3 internal clean cut Remove data_writer from integrations constructing ExtractionServiceB3 and do not pass resource_monitor to ParquetWriterB3; use the current facades and signatures. Reserved B3 sentinel The literal __GLOBALDATAFINANCE_NULL__ is not accepted as a value; use None for nulls.

docs.title: CVM
docs.text:
The current CVM contract is exact-text-v1: string columns, empty fields as "", original values preserved, and ZIP retention after extraction. QUOTE_NONE keeps literal quotes and short rows receive trailing empty fields. Multi-Parquet publication remains recoverable as a batch, with all records verified before promotion. See the CVM exact text migration for regeneration, explicit conversions, and lock inspection after interruption.

Library logging does not alter the application root logger. Before an explicit setup_logging() call, the globaldatafinance namespace uses a NullHandler and remains quiet; a handler reconfiguration failure preserves the previous configuration.

docs.title: Notes for release 0.2.0
docs.text:
The text below is the prepared body for the 0.2.0 GitHub release. The existing .github/workflows/publish.yml runs gates and publication from the published-release event. Version, tag, and publication must await approval of the acceptance evidence; this draft does not claim a release was published.

Dependency requirements for the next release:

  • PyArrow: >=26.0.0,<27.0.0.
  • psutil: >=7.2.2,<8.0.0.
  • pydantic-settings: >=2.16.2,<3.0.0.

The development lock also updates virtualenv to 21.14.13, fixing GHSA-cx6f-vjhg-g3cc in Bash environment activation. This dependency is used by pre-commit.

Breaking COTAHIST contract changes:

  • The default selection now preserves every type-01 quotation, including TPMERC 021 and unknown numeric markets. Omit assets_list or use todos; specify classes when a consumer requires a filter.
  • Parquet moves to versioned schema 2 with 32 columns. The original 20 fields retain their order and values; the 12 additions include the omitted official fields, provenance, and the original 245 quotation bytes.
  • Regenerate v1 Parquets from the original ZIP/TXT sources. Append and merge across incompatible schemas fail; converting v1 files cannot recover missing data. Follow the cutover and rollback procedures on this page.
  • Specify an available annual range: any missing requested year or invalid record fails extraction, including a record in a filtered-out market.
  • Publication requires complete staged-output readback and exact data and manifest verification. Failures preserve the previous output; consumers must check success, schema_version, and integrity before switching files.

The local acceptance corpus covers 2000–2026, with a snapshot ending on 2026-09-02. The release must attach final frozen-corpus evidence and checksum manifests. These bounds are not independent confirmation of exchange coverage or availability of every historical year.

Every 01 record is validated and converted before market selection. Blank lines and 00/99 controls are counted, while every other nonempty identifier fails. Both modes use canonical conversion and bounded CSV row batches through Arrow. fast uses batches of up to 25,000 records and can process sources in parallel; slow uses batches of up to 10,000 records and one worker. Both preserve the same logical schema, order, and values.

docs.title: B3 schema v2 and regeneration
docs.text:
The persisted COTAHIST contract changed incompatibly to versioned schema 2. The default is now assets_list=None, equivalent to assets_list=["todos"]: all type-01 quotations with numeric TPMERC codes are preserved, including 021 and codes that are not yet known. The output has 32 columns, adding the five previously omitted official fields, source coordinates, and the original 245 bytes of each quote. Financial values use exact decimals; preco_exercicio_pontos has scale 6.

Version 1 Parquets do not contain TPMERC 021 rows, all official fields, or original source bytes. Do not convert or append these files into v2. Regenerate from the raw ZIP/TXT sources and validate the output before switching consumers.

Cutover procedure:

  1. Preserve the COTAHIST sources and record their hashes.
  2. Choose the annual range actually available. Pass initial_year and last_year; defaults still cover 1986 through the current year, and any gap inside the requested range fails extraction.
  3. Write to a separate destination using assets_list=["todos"] (or omit assets_list).
  4. Require result["success"] is True and result["schema_version"] == 2. Review selection_complete, source_complete, counts, selected years, and output_sha256 in result["integrity"] for the consumer’s requirements.
  5. Read the Arrow schema and adapt consumers to the 12 added columns and exact types in the B3 v2 schema reference.
  6. Switch consumers to the verified output and retain v1 files until the cutover is accepted.

Rollback procedure:

  1. Keep the previous package version, consumer configuration, and v1 Parquet paths together until accepting the migration. Record the SHA-256 of each previous output and generate v2 in a separate directory.
  2. If acceptance fails, restore the previous package version and consumer configuration to read the retained v1 paths. Leave the original COTAHIST and separate v2 artifacts available for diagnosis.
  3. Verify the retained v1 checksums and reopen them with the previous consumer. Do not overwrite v2 with v1 or append rows between schema versions.

The library publishes one caller-selected output; changing the consumer’s chosen path belongs to the application. A failed extraction preserves the previous file at that output path and returns output_file="". These guarantees are exercised by tests/application/b3_docs/test_publication_integrity.py and tests/application/b3_docs/test_schema_migration.py.

A filtered v2 Parquet may contain zero rows and still be complete for the requested selection; review selection_complete, source_complete, and intentional-exclusion counts. source_complete=True requires zero exclusions. Reports include outer and uncompressed-content hashes, Base64 controls, trailer convention, observed dates, row digest, and final Parquet hash. These facts attest the supplied files; they do not confirm a trading calendar or instruments outside the corpus. Years before 2000 require separate source files and are not included in the locally audited corpus.

Integrations that depended on removed internal objects must migrate to the facade flow. The B3 session now has an explicit lifecycle (NEW → OPEN → CLOSED) and cannot be reopened after closing, including when final validation fails.

Internal workers use only the canonical CotahistParserB3 conversion, including source replay and digest verification for subclasses. Custom factories that provided only parse_line() must implement the complete parser contract; the alternative dictionary path was removed. The internal normalize_decimal_v99 helper and unused ZipProcessingResult/ProcessSingleFileResult types were removed. Use normalize_decimal with an explicit scale in internal extensions.

Text-reading interfaces and ParquetWriterB3 with existing callers remain available over the current implementation. Module documentation lives in README.md and README.en.md; the stale README.pt.md copy was removed.

In this migration to 0.2.0, the following five historical names are retained to preserve existing integrations in their current internal namespaces:

Name Status in this migration CotahistParserB3.EXPECTED_LINE_LENGTH Historical record-width attribute derived from the canonical 245-byte layout. extraction_service.types.ParsedRecord Typing alias retained for existing imports. extraction_service.types.ExtractionSummary Historical type retained for existing imports; it does not define the complete public result. ExtractHistoricalQuotesUseCaseB3.execute_sync Synchronous entrypoint retained over the current asynchronous implementation. CreateSetToDownloadUseCaseB3 File discovery retained over current path and source validation.

New integrations should use HistoricalQuotesB3 and the public ExtractionResultB3 contract. Retaining these names in this migration does not expand root exports.

docs.title: Dependencies and measurement
docs.text: ReadFilesAdapter was removed together with the automatic Pandas dependency; consumers who still want DataFrames must install Pandas themselves. PyArrow is the only production CSV/Parquet engine. Use scripts/benchmark_ingestion.py for local fresh-process measurements; its numbers depend on hardware, environment, and corpus, so they are not universal time or RSS guarantees. The complete timeout, generic adapter, B3 catch-boundary, and write-failure migration is documented in Infrastructure clean cut.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: After installing the library, choose a source. CVM requires internet access; B3 uses local files. The examples below process only 2023.

docs.title: Download CVM filings
docs.text:
from globaldatafinance import FundamentalStocksDataCVM

result = FundamentalStocksDataCVM().download(
    destination_path="./data_cvm",
    list_docs=["DFP"],
    initial_year=2023,
    last_year=2023,
    automatic_extractor=True,
)
if result.error_count_downloads > 0 or result.success_count_downloads == 0:
    raise RuntimeError(result.failed_downloads)
print(result.successful_downloads)

The download saves the original ZIP and converts its CSV files to Parquet in the selected directory. CVM columns contain text; convert dates and numbers in your analysis when needed. To download ZIPs without conversion, use automatic_extractor=False.

See the CVM guide to choose documents and handle partial failures.

docs.title: Extract B3 quotes
docs.text:
Obtain files from the official B3 page and place the desired year in the input directory. The extractor accepts local ZIP or TXT files named COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.ZIP or COTAHIST_A{YYYY}.TXT. The library does not download these files. For this example, supply 2023:

cotahist/
└── COTAHIST_A2023.ZIP

from globaldatafinance import HistoricalQuotesB3

b3 = HistoricalQuotesB3()
result = b3.extract(
    path_of_docs="./cotahist",
    destination_path="./data_b3",
    assets_list=["ações"],
    initial_year=2023,
    last_year=2023,
)
if not result["success"]:
    raise RuntimeError(result["errors"])
print(result["output_file"], result["total_records"])

ações selects spot and fractional markets. The result is a dictionary of status and metadata; data is stored in the Parquet at output_file. See the B3 guide for other markets, years, and processing modes.

docs.title: Read the Parquet
docs.text:
Use the path returned by the preceding B3 extraction. To inspect a small sample without loading the entire file:

import pyarrow.parquet as pq

parquet = pq.ParquetFile(result["output_file"])
print(parquet.schema_arrow)
for batch in parquet.iter_batches(batch_size=5):
    print(batch.to_pydict())
    break

To run repository examples with the included synthetic B3 samples, see practical examples.
